ACCOUNT_ALIASES.title: Account, aliases and Your account — 0.25.0
ACCOUNT_ALIASES.content:
# Account, aliases and Your account — 0.25.0

My profile → Account and Aliases are now functional. Your account opens a menu that stays within the viewport, including mobile and a collapsed sidebar. It provides Online/Away/Offline, System/Light/Dark, Account settings, User aliases, Change workspace and Sign out.

## Upgrade

Keep your existing backend `.env` and back up PostgreSQL. Replace application source, activate your project's virtual environment, and run **from backend**:

```powershell
python -m alembic upgrade head
python -m alembic current
```

Account/aliases were introduced in **0017**; the current release head is **0018**, which also adds Agent Knowledge. Restart backend/frontend. This update has database changes; extracting the ZIP alone does not apply them. Requirements, dependency pins, existing migrations 0001–0016, existing workspace data and unlimited AI-agent creation/import are retained. No new environment variable or dependency is required. Existing SMTP and verified email domain configuration is used for ticket replies.

0017 adds personal settings, immutable avatar assets, user aliases and per-user conversation persona selections. It adds internal author IDs to livechat messages, distinguishes initial versus manual ticket email, and retains idempotent initial notifications while permitting multiple manual replies. Existing account names are split for the form without changing their saved full name. Existing assigned chats with human reply history retain account identity until explicitly changed. Downgrading removes the new personal/alias data and manual ticket replies, preserving older account/workflow/ticket records; use backups if intentionally reverting.

## Account

Save first/last name, an avatar, and live agent language. Email is read-only and stays tied to the verified sign-in account. PNG, JPEG and GIF uploads support up to 10 MB, are decoded with image-size limits, stripped of metadata and saved as 256 × 256 PNG; GIF uses its first frame. The profile image appears on the account menu and account-persona replies. Removing or changing it does not rewrite prior reply images.

The language becomes the user's support profile language in existing workspaces and the default for newly created support profiles. AI agent language configuration remains separate. Personal settings belong to the authenticated account across its workspaces and do not require workspace-management permissions.

## Notification preferences

Browser notifications, platform notices and event sounds are saved independently of account details. Events are Conversation assigned to you, Conversation assigned to team, Conversation transferred to you, New message in open conversation, and New message in other conversation. Each has None, Byte, Chime or Bell.

Platform notices appear while the signed-in application is running. Authorized Inbox changes are checked every five seconds, with historical items silent on the initial poll. Opening a notice navigates to the conversation and respects unsaved draft/field handling. Message alerts concern customer messages, not your own replies. Browser notifications require a supported secure browser and site permission; the application asks only when the user enables that option. Browser notices appear when the app is not visible. This is active-browser polling, not an offline service-worker push service.

Enable & test sound unlocks the browser audio context through your click. Browsers may require this after a restart. Settings are persisted even if a device blocks browser notifications or audio; the UI reports permission/unavailability rather than pretending to enable them. With platform and browser notices both disabled, incoming alert sounds are muted.

Open conversations in multi-chat view enables up to eight Inbox tabs. Each open conversation keeps its own unsent draft while switching. Closing a tab with a draft or leaving the page/workspace asks before discarding unsent work. These drafts are held in browser memory, not sent or stored as support messages; a reload discards them after the browser's unsaved-work handling.

## Aliases

Create an alias with a display name, optional avatar, Set as default, email signature name and email signature content. Names are unique within your own active aliases; other accounts can use the same name. One default is allowed. Setting a new default clears the previous one. Without a default, new conversations use your account name, falling back to “Support agent” when it is blank. Your email address is never substituted as a public reply name.

The Reply as selector appears above livechat and ticket reply editors. Each user has their own selection for each conversation; the last selected/used identity wins over later default changes. An explicit account selection remains the account persona. You can switch at any time. A different identity can appear to the customer as a different support representative.

Select X beside an alias and confirm deletion. The alias is archived and disappears from all future pickers. Existing messages and ticket emails keep their saved display name, avatar reference and signature. Updating an alias also affects only future replies. Deleting a selected alias falls back to the current default or account identity. Avatar endpoints require ownership or access to a conversation/ticket that actually uses that image. Each live reply retains the authenticated author's internal ID for audit and usage; that ID is not exposed as part of the customer-facing message.

Aliases are global to your account, not shared team accounts. There is a technical cap of 50 active aliases per account. Signatures are plain text with line breaks; email HTML escapes their contents. Arbitrary signature HTML or scripts are not executed.

## Ticket replies and signatures

Tickets now has Customer replies as well as Initial email notifications. Choose the configured default support sender or a DNS-verified sender, select Reply as, write the reply and Send. The selected alias supplies the sender display name and signature. The selected shared sender address is used; changing an alias does not change the authenticated account or verified sender domain. Customer email and ticket subject remain the existing ticket values.

Each reply and its signature are committed before SMTP. Failed and uncertain delivery uses the existing review/retry workflow, retaining the exact saved content/persona. Repeated client request IDs cannot send duplicate replies; changed contents with the same ID are rejected. Multiple distinct manual replies are allowed while the initial customer/assignee notifications remain unique. Resolved/closed tickets must be reopened; active bans and current ticket-management permissions are enforced. Sent manual replies are counted as Manual emails in the existing weighted usage report. Incoming mailbox replies use the optional authenticated provider adapter described in [Tickets](TICKETS.md).

## Presence, themes and workspace switching

Away and Offline immediately exclude the user from automatic livechat assignment. Heartbeats do not override those choices. Existing owned chats remain available for follow-up. Online resumes available presence in the current team/workspace; normal role, language, capacity and team eligibility still apply. Enabling Inbox availability explicitly sets Online. Expired/revoked support sessions remain unavailable regardless of the selected status.

Theme is saved on the account, cached in the browser for startup, and applied to the actual UI. System follows the device's colour-scheme changes. Light/Dark set explicit modes. Workspace primary branding and logos remain available; Light uses a readable neutral surface/text palette instead of forcing a dark workspace background.

Change workspace lists only actual memberships, marks the current workspace and switches the active authenticated workspace. Unsaved settings, alias edits, ticket notes/replies and livechat drafts are checked first. Personal preferences and aliases remain with the user across workspaces. No membership, role, plan or workspace is fabricated by the menu.

## APIs

All mutations require the existing CSRF header and revision checks.

- `GET /api/me/profile`; multipart `POST /api/me/profile/account`.
- `POST /api/me/profile/preferences`: expected_revision plus presence, theme or multichat.
- `POST /api/me/profile/notifications`: expected_revision and the notification configuration.
- `GET|POST /api/me/aliases`; multipart `POST /api/me/aliases/{id}`; `POST .../{id}/delete` with expected_revision.
- `GET /api/profile-assets/{id}`: owned or referenced-by-authorized-record image access.
- `GET|POST /api/workspaces/{ws}/support/{chats|tickets}/{id}/persona`: user's current/default identity, own aliases and a selection revision.
- Existing livechat reply accepts optional alias_id. Omit to use remembered/default; send null to use account.
- `POST /api/workspaces/{ws}/tickets/{id}/reply`: ticket expected_revision, UUID client_request_id, content, optional domain_id/alias_id/cc/takeover. Omit domain_id for the saved sender, or send null for the server default.
- `GET /api/workspaces/{ws}/profile-updates?since=<timestamp>`: authorized active-browser notification changes.
- Existing `/api/workspaces` and workspace select endpoints power the menu; authentication and workspace policy checks still apply.

ADVISOR.title: Advisor — 0.33.0
ADVISOR.content:
# Advisor — 0.33.0

Advisor is the private in-dashboard guide to Petrix AI. Open the lightning bolt **Advisor** entry in the main navigation.

## Using Advisor

The homepage greets the current user and shows five starting questions: testing an AI agent, teamspaces, custom fields, banning and adding team members. Selecting a suggestion fills the composer; Send submits it. Enter sends and Shift+Enter adds a line. **Start Chat** opens a fresh discussion. Selecting an earlier conversation continues that private history.

History is grouped into Today, Yesterday and Earlier using the workspace timezone, with pagination for both conversations and long message histories. Advisor questions, replies, source links and supported attachments persist across refresh. A submitted turn survives leaving the page because it is queued durably. An interrupted turn can be retried without duplicating the user's question. Conversation deletion requires confirmation and removes its messages/files; late background results cannot restore it.

Advisor provides guidance and links. It does not execute platform actions, alter settings, send customer messages, inspect other users' conversations or automatically read private CRM/Inbox/agent records. Documentation navigation shortcuts respect the current user's grants; actual destination APIs enforce their own permissions. Uploaded attachments are data, not executable instructions.

## Documentation and model modes

Without a configured model, common questions receive explicit guidance from the bundled platform guide, or relevant documentation/attachment excerpts. The interface labels these documentation replies and does not claim that an unavailable model answered. A short question with a new topic is handled independently from the preceding question. Ambiguous follow-ups can use prior conversation context.

An optional OpenAI-compatible connection enables conversational answers grounded in retrieved platform documentation and user attachments:

```dotenv
ADVISOR_BASE_URL=
ADVISOR_API_KEY=
ADVISOR_MODEL=
ADVISOR_VISION_ENABLED=false
ADVISOR_WORKER_ENABLED=true
```

The base URL is the service's API base; `/chat/completions` is appended. Keep keys server-side. If a dedicated base URL/model pair is absent, Advisor reuses a configured support AI pair, then a configured tester LLM pair. A dedicated key is used with its dedicated endpoint; credentials from different connections are not mixed. A configured connection is not a claim that a health check succeeded. HTTPS is required for a dedicated production Advisor connection.

The model receives the last bounded discussion context, selected documentation passages, relevant attachment text and optional images. It receives no account token, API key, other user's history or automatically fetched private support records. Reply source and navigation IDs are validated against the supplied evidence. Invented/invalid source IDs, malformed output, unavailable providers and provider failures fall back to clearly labelled documentation guidance. This verifies the source references, not every semantic claim a model might make.

The system prompt requests JSON with `answer`, `citation_ids` and `navigation_ids`. It prioritizes the current Platform guide over older release notes, explicitly identifies unavailable features and refuses to claim that an action was executed. Advisor uses no model action/tool execution capability. Questions outside available platform evidence should be clarified rather than answered from invented platform behavior.

## Attachments

Use the paperclip to upload up to **five files**, **10 MiB per file**, and **20 MiB total per message**. Supported files are readable PDF, DOCX, TXT, Markdown, CSV and JSON, plus validated PNG, JPEG, GIF and WebP images. Corrupt, empty, oversized and unsupported files are rejected. PDF/DOCX extraction uses the existing bounded text-ingestion implementation. Scanned/encrypted PDFs with no readable text require a readable replacement or a written description; no OCR is claimed.

File bytes and extracted text are stored in owner-scoped Advisor records, separate from agent Knowledge, Copilot Knowledge and customer conversation attachments. Image input is normalized to a bounded JPEG preview without metadata. Enable `ADVISOR_VISION_ENABLED` only for a model that accepts `image_url` input. Up to the two most recent images are sent per reply; the interface explains when image understanding is unavailable. Original file download remains authenticated and private.

Removing an unsent attachment removes the staged copy. Unsent staged files expire after 24 hours during worker/upload cleanup. Sent files remain with their conversation. Attachment reads, previews, downloads, submission and deletion check ownership, workspace membership and current conversation teamspace access. Even an administrator cannot read another user's private Advisor history through this API. Advisor accepts at most 20 questions per user/workspace per minute. Pending turns prevent concurrent sends in the same conversation; message IDs make safe retry reconciliation possible.

## Documentation and footer links

The footer links open:

- **APIs:** an authenticated in-dashboard reference generated from the running application's OpenAPI schema, searchable by method/path/tag, with a JSON download.
- **Documentation:** the bundled documentation viewer, with searchable guides and links from individual Advisor replies.
- **Privacy Policy / Terms of Use:** the existing legal pages, which remain explicitly marked as development previews until final legal documents are supplied.

The current guide is [Platform guide](PLATFORM_GUIDE.md). Older individual manuals retain historical upgrade/release notes. The current application is **0.33.0**, schema **0025**. Markdown renders text, lists, code, tables and safe links; raw HTML and active image/URL schemes are not executed. Documentation is bundled inside `backend/app/advisor/manual.json`, so it works in the existing backend Docker image without an external documentation host. After editing source manuals, rebuild the bundle from the project root:

```bash
python scripts/build_advisor_manual.py
```

## Worker and upgrade

Keep the current database and `backend/.env`. From backend:

```bash
python -m alembic upgrade head
```

Restart the API and frontend. Additive migration **0025** creates three Advisor tables. Migrations 0001–0024 are unchanged. Dependencies, Windows Python 3.9.12 compatibility targets, previous modules and unlimited agent creation/import are retained.

The API starts the Advisor worker by default. To use a separate worker, disable the API worker and run from backend:

```bash
python -m app.advisor.worker --watch
```

Without `--watch`, one queued turn is processed. Pending/running/completed/failed state, expiring leases and fenced writes support restart recovery. Model calls run outside database transactions. Workspace/teamspace access is checked before processing and again before saving the result. This worker is independent of Inbox, Knowledge and Perception workers.

## Analytics scrolling correction

The dashboard's fixed-height parent clipped Analytics because its flex content retained its content minimum height. The Analytics dashboard content now has `min-height: 0` and a bounded overflow container. Its report grid row and report pane also permit shrinking, allowing actual vertical scrolling to the lower charts, metric sections, Users/feedback tables and report notes. Changing reports resets the report pane to the top; quiet live refreshes retain scroll position. Perception uses the same corrected dashboard height boundary. Browser checks cover mouse-wheel scrolling and reaching the bottom of all six reports, plus narrow-screen scrolling.

## API

Paths are relative to `/api/workspaces/{workspace_id}/advisor`; mutations use the existing session and CSRF mechanism.

| Method | Path | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/options` | Accessible teamspaces, greeting name/timezone, suggestions and connection flags |
| GET / POST | `/conversations` | Private paginated history / idempotent new discussion |
| GET | `/conversations/{id}` | Latest messages or earlier-page cursor |
| POST | `/conversations/{id}/messages` | Queue a revision-checked, idempotent question and uploaded file IDs |
| POST | `/conversations/{id}/retry/{message}` | Retry a failed latest assistant turn |
| POST | `/conversations/{id}/delete` | Confirm private conversation deletion |
| POST | `/attachments` | Validate and stage one multipart file |
| GET | `/attachments/{id}` | Private original file download |
| GET | `/attachments/{id}/preview` | Private normalized image preview |
| POST | `/attachments/{id}/delete` | Remove an unused staged file |
| GET | `/docs` / `/docs/{slug}` | Bundled guide list / allowed document |
| GET | `/openapi` | Running schema; `download=true` downloads JSON |

AI_AGENTS.title: Petrix AI — Manage AI Agents
AI_AGENTS.content:
# Petrix AI — Manage AI Agents

Milestone 2 adds persisted AI-agent configuration to the existing passwordless account and workspace flow. The dashboard uses the supplied screenshots as layout references while retaining Petrix branding.

## Upgrade your existing Windows installation

1. Stop the backend and Angular terminals with Ctrl+C. Mailpit can keep running.
2. Extract the updated source and copy its contents into `C:\Users\Admin\petrix-ai`. Keep your current `backend/.env`, root virtual environment, database, and Mailpit executable. The source archive excludes those items.
3. Run the migration from the backend directory with your virtual environment active:

```powershell
cd C:\Users\Admin\petrix-ai\backend
python -m alembic upgrade head
python -m uvicorn app.main:create_app --factory --reload --port 8000 --no-access-log
```

Migration `0002` adds the agent tables, permissions, and workspace plan capacity. It inserts one Default AI Agent into every existing workspace, with a first version and change-log entry. New registrations create their default agent in the same transaction as account/workspace creation. Listing agents and returning sign-ins do not recreate a deleted default agent. Existing authentication and workspace data are retained.

4. Start Angular in a second terminal:

```powershell
cd C:\Users\Admin\petrix-ai\frontend
npm ci
npm start
```

Use `http://localhost:4200` consistently. The start script binds to `localhost` to match the configured request origin. Complete email sign-in using your Mailpit inbox at `http://localhost:8025`, or reuse your existing session.

Python 3.9.12 remains the backend runtime. Version `0.4.0` adds pinned Groq and embedding dependencies; follow [INTENT_MATCHING.md](INTENT_MATCHING.md) when upgrading to the current source.

## Agent management

The top selector lists real agents from your workspace. Its Create AI agent action opens New AI agent and Import AI agent choices. Your selection is reflected in the URL and remembered for that workspace during the browser session.

Creation accepts a name, default language, and optional avatar. Avatar uploads accept actual PNG, JPEG, or GIF data up to 10 MiB and 16 million source pixels. Images are re-encoded as 256×256 PNGs without source metadata; animated GIFs use the first frame.

The Agent tab separates Personalization, Languages, Settings, and Danger zone. Each section has its own Save button and draft state. Saving one section keeps drafts in other sections. Switching agents, reloading, or leaving with unsaved changes requires a discard confirmation. A stale revision returns 409, allowing the user to reload rather than overwrite another editor's saved changes.

The LLM toggle controls Groq intent recognition and optional generative replies for unmatched text. Exact/fuzzy matching, configured semantic embeddings, and saved actions work when it is off. Supported workflow languages are selected from the language catalog; the default must be a selected language. See [WORKFLOWS.md](WORKFLOWS.md) and [INTENT_MATCHING.md](INTENT_MATCHING.md).

## Import and export

Import accepts a Petrix JSON export up to 15 MiB. It creates a new agent after server-side validation and language-capacity checks; there is no agent-count limit. Exports include saved identity, persona, languages, voice preferences, and the sanitized avatar, using this contract:

```json
{
  "format": "petrix-agent",
  "schema_version": 1,
  "agent": {
    "name": "Banking assistant",
    "llm_enabled": true,
    "persona": "Provide clear, professional banking support.",
    "languages": ["en", "sw"],
    "default_language": "en",
    "voice_enabled": false,
    "voice_name": "",
    "voice_speed": 1.0,
    "avatar_base64": null
  }
}
```

Exports omit workspace/user IDs, credentials, versions, chat logs, and external relationship IDs. Imports cannot set ownership or capacity. Proto exports require a format-specific conversion; no Proto compatibility is claimed without a real export schema. A sample Petrix JSON file is included in `examples/banking-assistant.petrix.json`.

## Complete portable imports (0.26.1)

Schema version 1 also accepts optional `workflows: {"nodes": [...]}` and `knowledge_files` arrays. Each PDF entry has `name`, `filename`, `data_base64`, and optional `enabled` (default true). Omit both for legacy settings-only imports. Standard exports remain settings-only; they do not export an existing agent’s workflows or source files.

A complete import creates a new agent, validates and rebinds every workflow node, path and Jump target, and extracts/indexes embedded PDFs before one database commit. Any invalid workflow or PDF rejects the whole import without leaving an empty agent. The four permanent system triggers are required and receive the new agent’s IDs. Workflow numbers are assigned locally. Branch outcome paths and nested steps remain connected. Imports cannot reference another workspace’s integrations, media, teams, users, agents or custom fields; configure those actions after importing. Portable actions are Send message, Ask survey, Set variable, Branch, Jump, Switch Language, LLM Processing, Close chat and Collect feedback.

Limits: 15 MiB total JSON, 1 MiB workflow definition, existing 500-node/12-level workflow bounds, and up to five non-encrypted text PDFs of 10 MiB/200 pages/256 KiB extracted text each. PDF bytes are checked and parsed with the existing isolated, time-limited document reader; Ready source records retain authorized original downloads. Existing source quotas, CSRF, management permissions, language capacity and unlimited agent creation/import remain unchanged. There is no additional migration or runtime dependency.

See [the complete test bot](TEST_BOT.md) for a working example of specific workflow commands followed by PDF fallback. Uploading a PDF alone does not override a matched workflow.

## Permissions and unlimited agents

Owners always retain Manage AI Agents. Administrators have it by default; members initially have view access. Owners and administrators can grant or revoke the permission for the Administrator and Member roles under Settings → Workspace → Roles & permissions. Agent write operations, export, and tester messages check this permission on the backend. All writes require session authentication, CSRF validation, and a permitted origin. Foreign workspace and agent identifiers return 404.

AI agent creation and import are unlimited for every existing and new workspace as of version 0.15.1. The selector and plan summary display the actual count alongside “Unlimited”. The default language capacity remains three languages per agent; `DEFAULT_LANGUAGE_LIMIT` configures this for new workspaces. `DEFAULT_AGENT_LIMIT` is no longer used, and existing environment files may retain it without changing behavior. Subscription automation and payments are a later milestone.

The API retains the `agent_limit` key for compatibility and returns `null` to mean unlimited. The old PostgreSQL `workspaces.agent_limit` column is retained for schema compatibility; its stored value is ignored. There is no additional migration or dependency. Existing agents, workflow data, step numbers, and settings are preserved.

A platform administrator with local database access can update an existing workspace using this helper from the project root:

```powershell
python .\scripts\set_workspace_plan.py WORKSPACE_UUID --plan "Professional" --languages 5
```

The helper changes the plan name and language capacity, and rejects a language downgrade below current usage. Its legacy `--agents` argument is optional and ignored; it cannot restore an agent-count cap. Workspace permissions and CSRF checks still apply to creation/import. Existing row locks and revision checks are retained. Native PostgreSQL concurrency stress tests remain an environment check.

## Versions and change log

Creation/import starts at version 1. A saved configuration change creates an immutable snapshot and change-log entry; an unchanged save does not create a duplicate version. Version snapshots include the sanitized avatar. Restoring earlier settings applies the current language quota and creates a new version if the configuration changes. Later history remains available. Version and change-log lists support pagination.

Network changes and role-permission changes are recorded in the audit table. Network stores directed relationships between agents in the same workspace. The Network tab shows incoming and outgoing links, with add/remove actions. Workflow handoff execution and channel routing are subsequent milestones.

Deletion requires the current revision and the exact agent name. It permanently removes configuration, avatar, versions, and network links. Historical tester conversations/messages and audit records retain the agent's recorded name with a null agent reference. Live channel publishing and audience migration are future features; their deletion integration must preserve this retention policy.

## Voice

The Voice tab saves an enable flag, preferred voice identifier, and speaking speed (0.5×–2×), and includes them in version snapshots and exports. Live synthesis, speech recognition, voice-provider discovery, and voice channels require later integrations. The UI indicates that no voice channels are connected.

## Optional conversation tester

The tester's initial greeting is executed from the saved Chat started → Send message action. For the Groq intent-recognition stage, configure `GROQ_API_KEY` as described in [INTENT_MATCHING.md](INTENT_MATCHING.md). For optional generative answers to unmatched text, configure a separate OpenAI-compatible chat-completion connection in `backend/.env`, then restart FastAPI:

```dotenv
LLM_BASE_URL=https://api.groq.com/openai/v1
LLM_API_KEY=YOUR_PROVIDER_API_KEY
LLM_MODEL=YOUR_AVAILABLE_CHAT_MODEL_ID
LLM_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=30
LLM_MAX_TOKENS=1024
LLM_TESTER_REQUESTS_PER_MINUTE=20
```

The Groq base URL and chat endpoint are documented in [Groq's compatibility guide](https://console.groq.com/docs/openai) and [API reference](https://console.groq.com/docs/api-reference). Select a chat model currently available in your provider account. Other compatible providers or a local model server can use their own base URL and model ID; local HTTP connections are permitted in development. Production connections require HTTPS.

The generative adapter supplies the saved persona and supported/default languages, and retains up to 20 recent messages as model context. The intent classifier uses a separate routing prompt and at most six recent messages. API keys remain on the backend. Generative-provider failures return a generic 503; failed turns are not added to conversation history. Intent-provider failures can reach a configured workflow fallback and produce controlled tester diagnostics. User/agent ownership and CSRF checks protect conversations, and a shared per-user model request limit returns 429 when exceeded. Resetting the tester starts a new conversation and replays Chat started; previous chat records are retained. Disabling the LLM stops both model stages while exact, fuzzy, semantic, and saved-action execution remain available.

Knowledge retrieval, action handlers beyond Send message and Set variable, channel publishing, and Co-pilot are subsequent milestones. The existing agent import/export format and Agent Versions tab cover agent settings. Workflow definitions and their revision counter are separate; settings restoration does not change workflow trees. See [SET_VARIABLE.md](SET_VARIABLE.md) for session data and expressions.

AI_AGENT_HANDOFF.title: AI Agent Handoff
AI_AGENT_HANDOFF.content:
# AI Agent Handoff

Version **0.21.0** makes **Add action → Handoffs → AI agent handoff** Ready. Connect a receiving agent with its Network credentials, select it, and Save. The receiving agent continues in the same Agent tester window, including subsequent customer replies, surveys, media, and feedback. The originating workflow stops at the action.

Both platforms must implement the Petrix AI network protocol v1 supplied in this release. Use Petrix AI **0.21.0 or later** on each side. An agent ID, secret, and domain from an unrelated chatbot product are not compatible credentials. Agents on the same Petrix instance use the same authenticated receiver service without an unnecessary HTTP round trip; different instances communicate over HTTPS.

## Upgrade

Keep the database, existing `backend/.env`, and `SESSION_SIGNING_SECRET`. From the backend directory, with your virtual environment active:

```powershell
cd C:\Users\Admin\petrix-ai\backend
python -m alembic upgrade head
python -m alembic current
```

The current head is **0015** (Workspace settings); 0014 adds tickets/email settings. Restart backend/frontend and reload. Migration 0013 adds incoming credentials, verified outgoing connections, incoming sessions, a request ledger, and outgoing transfer state. It retains accounts, workflows, permanent numbers, conversations, existing handoffs, files, settings, and unlimited AI agent creation/import. No dependency or new environment variable is required.

For a remotely accessible receiver, set its existing `API_BASE_URL` to the platform's actual HTTPS API origin, such as `https://support.example.com`, then restart. Verification checks that this origin matches the supplied domain. A domain is an origin without a path, query, or embedded credentials. HTTP is allowed only for the exact configured local origin on `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, or `::1`; a second instance on a different origin requires HTTPS. Private remote hosts require the existing explicit `SEND_API_ALLOWED_PRIVATE_HOSTS` configuration. Metadata and link-local targets remain blocked.

## Connect two agents

Use an account with **Manage AI Agents** permission for each agent you configure.

1. Open receiving **Agent B → Network**.
2. Enable **Allow incoming AI agent handoffs** and click **Generate & enable**. Incoming access is initially disabled for every agent.
3. Copy **AI agent ID** and **Platform domain**. Click **Show**, then **Copy** for **AI agent secret**. Hide it when finished.
4. Open originating **Agent A → Workflows** and add **AI agent handoff**.
5. Open its **AI Agent** selector and choose **Connect external AI agent**. This option also connects another agent on the same instance.
6. Enter B's ID, secret, and platform domain. Click **Verify & Save**. Verification authenticates against B and checks its identity and protocol version. Failed verification retains the form for correction.
7. The verified connection is selected automatically. Click the action's separate **Save** button to add it to the workflow.

Connections belong to their originating agent. Agent A's Network tab lists its verified transfer connections. The older **Agent network** map below these settings continues to describe workspace relationships; a map edge does not establish authenticated handoff credentials. Remove a connection from all workflow steps, including disabled steps, before deleting it. A transfer still awaiting confirmation also protects its connection from deletion.

## Test a complaint flow

Prepare B's **Chat started** workflow with these actions:

| Action | Configuration |
| --- | --- |
| Set variable | Name `customer_name`; Python value `variables.get("_transferred_context", {}).get("customer_name", "customer")` |
| Send message | `Hello {customer_name}. I am your complaints specialist.` |
| Ask survey | Question `Please describe the complaint.`; variable `complaint_description`; Text reply |
| Send message | `Thank you, {customer_name}. We recorded: {complaint_description}` |

The fallback in Set variable also lets B's standalone tester start without a transfer. Use the existing survey `.text` or `.norm.value` views when a subsequent expression needs a particular answer representation.

Prepare A with a **Message received** trigger matching `complaint`:

| Order | Action | Configuration |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Ask survey | `What is your name?`; variable `customer_name`; Text reply |
| 2 | Send message | `Connecting you to our complaints agent.` |
| 3 | AI agent handoff | Select the verified connection to B |

Restart A's tester, send `complaint`, and answer `Chris`. A's connecting message appears once; B then greets Chris and asks for the complaint in the same chat. Answer the question to exercise B's survey continuation. Add a Message received trigger on B matching `status` with a Send message action, then send `status` through A's still-open tester. B handles it. Reloading the page restores the same conversation and current receiver.

## Session continuity and context

The browser keeps A's original conversation ID and original authenticated file routes. B creates its own durable receiving conversation and runs its **Chat started** workflow once. Later events go to B's conversation. Receiving workflow stacks, secrets, private schema, and browser sessions stay on their own server. Source language and channel-preview controls are locked after transfer; B uses A's current language when configured on B, otherwise B's default language. B's Switch Language action continues to work.

Public source chat variables are placed in B's single read-only variable **`_transferred_context`**. It contains JSON data, rather than an interpolated JSON string. Examples:

```python
variables.get("_transferred_context", {}).get("customer_name", "customer")
_transferred_context.get("customer_name", "customer")
```

An authored message may use `{_transferred_context.customer_name}` when that property is present. Copy a value into B's own ordinary variable if B needs to update it; Set variable cannot replace `_transferred_context`. Other private underscore names and private Python attributes remain unavailable. Chained A → B → C handoffs merge the earlier public context with B's current public variables; B's newer values take precedence. Repeated agents and chains beyond eight agents are rejected.

The transfer includes up to 40 recent user/assistant text messages within a 16 KiB text budget, with individual messages limited to 4,000 characters. This provides recent context to B's conversation and context-aware actions. Authored B workflows must explicitly use the transferred variables where needed; switching agents does not automatically change their message templates.

### Filtering and limits

Before each transfer, the server removes underscore/internal keys, known password/secret/token/credential/session/header keys, protected API URLs, and known sensitive field names. It recursively filters objects, limits lists to 100 entries and nesting depth to eight, and redacts known secret formats such as labelled passwords, Bearer tokens, JWTs, and database connection strings. Known sensitive source-variable values are also redacted from recent history. Ordinary customer names, complaint text, and public structured API result data can carry over. The filtered top-level context must fit within 100 variables and 32 KiB, otherwise the handoff is rejected before starting B.

This is conservative key/pattern filtering, not universal secret or personal-data detection in arbitrary prose. Keep only the public business context needed by the receiving agent. Earlier attachment bytes and protected download URLs are not transferred. File values are reduced to safe name/content-type descriptors; a receiver needing the original document must ask for it again or use an independently authorized business integration.

## Receiving actions, files, and closure

B's normal workflows handle subsequent messages, surveys, carousels, graphs, attachments, and live-agent handoffs. B's live agents use B's Inbox/workspace. A forwards customer replies and polls public receiving state into the original tester. Uploaded survey files are validated and retained on A before forwarding; the receiver enforces the existing 10 MiB-per-file and 20 MiB-per-batch survey limits. New outgoing files use the original conversation's authenticated proxy and support downloads, inline previews, and byte ranges. Successfully fetched receiving files are cached with A's conversation, so that cached history remains downloadable even if receiving credentials are later revoked. Unfetched protected files still require an active receiving session.

A's interpreter is terminal after a successful transfer: later siblings, enclosing continuations, and A's Chat Closed actions do not run. A Close chat action, human closure, or Collect Feedback at B follows B's existing lifecycle. Feedback remains available in the original window, then B's continuation runs if configured. Closing B does not return to A. Use a separate explicit AI handoff in a new, loop-free route when another specialist must take over.

An agent with an open incoming/outgoing conversation or pending feedback cannot be deleted. Previously closed history is retained. This release connects the existing authenticated Agent tester and Inbox surfaces. Publishing customer widgets or channel adapters remains a separate feature.

## Credentials and recovery

Each receiving agent has a unique high-entropy secret. Saved secrets and session tokens are encrypted using a domain-separated key derived from `SESSION_SIGNING_SECRET`; keep that environment secret stable. Ordinary settings/list responses are masked. Revealing a secret requires authenticated management access and CSRF. Secrets are excluded from agent import/export, change logs, traces, and safe validation errors. Remote verification/start uses `X-Petrix-Agent-Secret`; later operations use a separate session Bearer token without browser cookies. TLS verification, pinned DNS, bounded responses, and disabled redirects/proxies/retries use the existing safe HTTPS transport.

An incoming session expires after seven days. Disabling incoming access or rotating B's secret revokes existing incoming session tokens immediately. Reconnect A with the new secret and start a fresh conversation after rotation. The user who enabled B must retain current workspace membership and Manage AI Agents permission; revoking that access also prevents network execution. Incoming secrets authorize access to that agent and its configured workflows, so share them only with authorized systems.

The source commits a unique transfer ID and preceding transcript before starting B. A repeated start with the same ID/context returns the same receiving session. Subsequent events have durable request IDs and a receiver request ledger; changed input cannot reuse an ID. The tester keeps a stable ID for retrying the same start, message, or upload. After a lost acknowledgement, **Retry saved request** resends that saved operation rather than creating another conversation or replaying completed actions. Reload also restores a pending initial start when its original response was lost.

An unavailable, revoked, or uncertain receiver keeps A paused and displays an error. There is no automatic fallback to A or a different agent. A request recorded as running before a process crash is not automatically replayed, because it may already have produced external effects. Review the receiving workflow/integration state before starting a new test conversation. Explicit Restart creates a new conversation; it does not undo a previous transfer. A missing connection or invalid/oversized context blocks the handoff before starting the receiver.

## API

Management/tester routes use prefix `/api/workspaces/{workspace_id}/agents/{agent_id}`. They require current membership, Manage AI Agents, and agent/conversation ownership; mutations require CSRF.

| Method / route | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| GET `/network/credentials` | Masked ID/domain/enabled/revision/secret-presence state. |
| POST `/network/credentials` | `{expected_revision, enabled, rotate:false}`; generate, enable/disable, or rotate. |
| POST `/network/credentials/reveal` | Explicit authorized secret reveal. |
| GET `/network/transfer-connections` | Safe verified destination list. |
| POST `/network/transfer-connections` | Verify and save `{agent_id, secret, domain}`; returns connection metadata without the secret. |
| POST `/network/transfer-connections/{id}/delete` | Delete an unreferenced connection. |
| POST `/tester/conversations/{id}/ai-retry` | Retry a saved start/request on an owned conversation. |
| GET `/tester/conversations/{id}/ai-files/{file_id}` | Authorized receiving-file proxy/cache; optional `inline=true`. |

The saved action config is `{connection_id:"verified-connection-uuid"}`. Public tester text events accept optional UUID `client_event_id`; survey uploads accept it as a form field. Pass the same ID only when retrying the exact same operation. Conversation snapshots/results include `ai_handoff` with receiving agent ID/name/domain, status, pending/error, and configured languages. Internal tokens, source transfer payloads, and receiver workflow stacks are not returned.

Peer routes have prefix `/api/ai-network` and authenticate independently of browser cookies:

| Method / route | Authentication / contract |
| --- | --- |
| POST `/agents/{agent_id}/verify` | Agent secret header; returns protocol `version:1`, public agent identity/languages, and platform domain. |
| POST `/agents/{agent_id}/handoffs` | Agent secret header; v1 transfer UUID, filtered context/history, language/channel, and visited-agent trail; returns session ID/token and public result. |
| POST `/sessions/{session_id}/events` | Session Bearer token; `{request_id,event,files}` with validated optional base64 uploads. |
| GET `/sessions/{session_id}/snapshot` | Session Bearer token; current public state and transcript. |
| GET `/sessions/{session_id}/files/{file_id}` | Session Bearer token; only files exposed in that receiving conversation. |

Network JSON is bounded to 2 MiB, or 30 MiB for upload events/file responses; raw file limits still apply. Verification/start requests are limited to 120 per IP per minute; session operations to 600 per session per minute. Existing workflow, action, and LLM budgets remain in effect. Public tester fields cannot supply a trusted network actor or private continuation mode.

ANALYTICS.title: Analytics — version 0.31.0
ANALYTICS.content:
# Analytics — version 0.31.0

Analytics provides **Live report, Messaging, Chats, CSAT, Tickets and Live agents**. Reports use operational records in your database. The previous custom analytics iFrame remains under **Custom** with its existing permission/plan rules.

## Upgrade and timezone

Keep your database, virtual environment and `backend/.env`. Replace the source and run from `backend`:

```powershell
python -m alembic upgrade head
```

Migration **0023** adds measured presence intervals, transactional assignment/status/feedback history and workspace timezone/tracking metadata. Migrations 0001–0022 are unchanged. Restart the API and Angular. No dependency update is required over 0.30.0. Inbox, People, Tickets, Livechats, aliases, workflow/PDF agent imports and unlimited AI agent creation/import remain available.

Set **Settings → Workspace → General → Workspace timezone**, using an IANA name such as `Africa/Nairobi` or `UTC`. Existing workspaces default to Africa/Nairobi. Analytics dates are inclusive local calendar dates; the server converts their boundaries to UTC and handles daylight-saving days. Historical reports support up to 366 days and reject future dates. Changing the timezone changes report grouping, not stored event timestamps. Billing keeps its existing billing-period rules.

## Common controls

Choose a report from the Analytics sidebar and select a teamspace or all permitted teamspaces. Reports show the timezone explicitly. Date inputs and **Apply dates** change the reporting period. Agent activity and the agent table use one selected day; the heatmap supports a date range.

**Theme** changes chart colours, starting with Mild. Mild, Vivid, Distinct, Blue and Neutral are available and the browser remembers the selection. Group by and Segment by support time, chat type, AI agent, live agent, team, recorded channel and status where applicable. CSAT also groups by rating; Tickets also groups by creator type; Messaging can segment by message type.

Open **Advanced · Add filter**, make selections, then Apply filters. Supported dimensions include chat/creator type, AI agents, channels, live agents, teams, status, CSAT ratings/unrated, tags/groups and typed conversation custom fields. Multiple values within one category use any selected value; categories combine all their conditions. Group-assigned tags and configured field defaults are respected. Clear filters resets the applied conditions.

Each chart has a table view, CSV download and PNG capture. CSV contains the chart's filtered/grouped values and protects text cells against spreadsheet formulas. PNG captures the current chart and legend. Count/time axes include zero and time-series plots fit the report width. Chart tables retain exact values. Report values of **—** indicate no recorded sample; an actual measured zero remains zero.

## Permissions and data scope

The existing independent report grants are used: View Messaging, View Chats, View CSAT, View Tickets and View Users and Teams. The Live report shows only sections allowed by those grants. Report access authorises aggregate reporting in the user's permitted teamspaces; it does not grant permission to open an Inbox conversation or read People contact fields.

CSAT names are shown only when the current role can view the linked People record and name field. Conversation links require their own chat-view permission. Internal notes, private Copilot output, customer message bodies and email bodies are not returned in report responses. Message calculations load event metadata, not body text. Report dimensions expose current workspace agent/team names under the corresponding reporting scope.

## Live report

The Live report refreshes every ten seconds while the page is visible and also has a manual refresh control. Operational counters reflect current records; new-volume charts and daily measurements use the current workspace day.

| Counter | Calculation |
| --- | --- |
| Unassigned livechats | Pending human chats with an assigned user or routing team; pending chats without either are excluded |
| Open livechats | Human conversations in Open or Overdue state |
| Open AI chats | Open conversations still controlled by AI; external handoffs are excluded |
| Unassigned tickets | Pending/in-progress tickets, regardless of assignee |
| Open tickets | Tickets currently Open |

Hourly charts show new AI chats, new livechats and new tickets. A conversation is classified as a livechat after a human handoff; it is not counted a second time as an AI chat in the same new-chat total. Explicitly marked test conversations are excluded unless included by the report filter; older unmarked records retain their saved channel classification.

Responsiveness includes assignment-to-first-reply wait, AI and human first/ongoing reply times. Reassignment starts a separate first-reply interval and uses that assignee's reply. Capacity shows available online agents' configured simultaneous-chat slots and current assigned usage. Capacity snapshots retain the configured teamspace limits seen at the time; observing capacity does not create or change assignment configuration.

The daily satisfaction/abandonment section includes average AI/live CSAT, closed without feedback and closed without person replies. People totals require People visibility: New people counts profiles created today; Active people counts distinct visible people with customer-facing chat/email activity today. User filters and pagination apply to the Users table. The table shows current status, teams, last observed online activity, active workload and measured active hours.

## Messaging

Messaging counts individual customer-facing message events during the selected period. It is separate from weighted billing interactions. The report includes person messages, AI messages, human replies, received customer email and successfully sent customer email. CC recipients do not multiply a message count.

Private notes, Copilot suggestions, unsent/failed email, assignee alerts and copied transfer-history messages are excluded. Repeated network request IDs are deduplicated across the selected chat records. Grouping/segmentation changes the chart without changing the filtered underlying message total.

## Chats

Chats uses conversations created in the selected period. Summary cards show total new chats, AI/live counts and percentages. Status, breakdown, responsiveness, engagement and abandonment use the same filtered cohort. An AI-controlled open chat appears under Open in the status chart. External transfers retain an explicit External label. Pending/in-progress ticket labels are handled consistently in ticket reports.

| Timing | Statistic |
| --- | --- |
| AI first response | Median creation-to-first recorded AI reply |
| AI response | Median person-message-burst-to-next-AI-reply wait |
| Live agent first response | Mean assignment-to-that-agent's-first reply, separately for each recorded reassignment |
| Live agent response | Mean person-message-burst-to-next-human-reply wait |

A burst starts with the first outstanding person message and ends with the next assistant reply. Greetings can be valid first AI responses. First-response intervals without a corresponding reply are excluded from timing averages.

Engagement reports messages per chat/AI chat/livechat and average completed duration for those groups. Duration uses recorded completion timestamps and excludes conversations whose completion time is unknown. Cohort engagement/timings use the recorded lifetime of those selected conversations; Messaging instead uses the dates of the individual message events. Abandonment counts completed conversations without submitted feedback or without person replies.

## CSAT

CSAT uses the feedback submission date where known. Legacy ratings without a submission timestamp use their chat creation date and carry an explanatory report note; their table date is shown as Not recorded.

| Metric | Calculation |
| --- | --- |
| Rated chats | Conversations with an integer rating from 1 through 5 |
| Average CSAT | Arithmetic mean of rated chats |
| CSAT % | Ratings 4 or 5 divided by rated chats × 100 |
| Positive CSAT % | Ratings 5 divided by rated chats × 100 |

Overall, AI-agent and live-agent metrics use the same filtered rows. Distribution separates rated/unrated AI chats and livechats. Rating breakdown labels 1 Bad, 2 Poor, 3 Okay, 4 Good, 5 Great. The Feedback surveys table shows chat ID, permitted person name, recorded submission date and rating. Its filters are shared with the chart and summary; pagination affects only the table, not the aggregate totals. Survey-only submissions can appear as Unrated.

## Tickets

Tickets uses tickets created within the selected period. It shows new ticket totals, current status distribution, breakdown, average customer emails per ticket, first delivered human response and first recorded resolution time. Creator type distinguishes manual/live-agent tickets from workflow/AI-created tickets. Recorded channel is Email; AI agent filters use the linked conversation when available.

Email counts include successfully sent customer notifications/replies and received email, with one count per email event. Initial automated notifications do not count as a human first reply. Resolution timing uses the first recorded Resolved transition after creation; a later note cannot overwrite it. Unknown legacy resolution times are excluded rather than inferred from the record's last update. Current `in_progress` is presented as Pending in these reports.

## Live agents

**Live agents activity** shows each selected agent's day on a timeline with Online, Away, Offline and Logged out colours. Hover/focus a segment for exact workspace-local times. The table summarises the four durations. Unrecorded history and future time are distinguished visually and excluded from active hours.

**Live agents** shows current members, teams, current observed availability, last online observation, assigned active chats/tickets and recorded active hours for the selected day. Active hours combine Online and Away. Workload uses recorded assignment/status history at the selected day's cutoff; current-day records can use their current assignment where older history is unavailable.

**Conversations heatmap** uses recorded assignment events over the selected date range. Choose days/weeks/months for columns, agents/teams for rows, and all conversations/livechats/tickets for type. Reset filters restores the heatmap defaults. Each cell counts distinct conversations assigned to that row and period. Transfers can therefore appear under more than one assignee; these cells are not an exclusive count of unique workspace conversations.

Presence is recorded with server timestamps by authenticated app activity every 25 seconds and by support availability/heartbeat updates. A 90-second lease bounds disconnected time. Expired or revoked sessions cannot extend an interval. Overlapping sessions are merged so active hours are not counted twice. Presence changes are observed by subsequent activity updates. These are recorded application-presence hours, not keyboard activity or payroll timesheets.

## History and retained data

Existing messages, creation dates, statuses and saved feedback feed the reports after upgrade. New transactional assignment/status/feedback events provide precise transfer, historical workload and resolution evidence going forward. Existing valid handoff/close/feedback timestamps are used where available. No historical shifts, transfers, ticket-resolution times or working hours are fabricated.

A tracking-start note explains missing older intervals. Changes to reports and capacity calculations do not mutate routing/assignment settings or consume billing interactions. Removing operational records removes their related Analytics events through foreign keys; current membership and teamspace permissions continue to scope reports. The Analytics module does not send conversation content to an external AI or analytics provider.

API.title: Petrix AI API
API.content:
# Petrix AI API

API paths begin with `/api`. Use the same public origin for the frontend and `/api` reverse proxy. FastAPI exposes OpenAPI documentation at `/docs` when running locally.

## Authentication

| Method | Path | Request | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/api/auth/options` | None | Availability of email, Google, and Microsoft; configured magic-link lifetime |
| POST | `/api/auth/magic-link` | JSON `{ "email": "you@gmail.com" }` | 202 after SMTP accepts the message; generic eligibility message |
| POST | `/api/auth/verify` | JSON `{ "token": "opaque-token-from-email" }` | Authenticated account/workspace context; session and CSRF cookies |
| GET | `/api/auth/me` | Session cookie | Current account/workspace context and next onboarding/dashboard path |
| POST | `/api/auth/logout` | Session cookie and CSRF header | 204; revoke current session and remove cookies |
| GET | `/api/auth/oauth/{provider}/start` | `provider` is `google` or `microsoft` | Redirect to configured provider |
| GET | `/api/auth/oauth/{provider}/callback` | Provider authorization response | Validate authentication and redirect to setup, dashboard, or email association |
| POST | `/api/auth/provider-email/info` | JSON `{ "token": "opaque-provider-ticket" }` | Provider name and optional email hint |
| POST | `/api/auth/provider-email` | JSON `{ "ticket": "opaque-provider-ticket", "email": "you@example.com" }` | Request mailbox verification for first provider association |

The magic-link email contains `/auth/verify#token=...`. The fragment keeps the token out of ordinary server URL logs. The frontend reads and removes the fragment, and submits the token only after the user selects Continue. A GET request never consumes a magic link.

Account context example:

```json
{
  "user": { "id": "user-uuid", "email": "you@gmail.com", "full_name": null },
  "workspace": {
    "id": "workspace-uuid",
    "name": "My AI Workspace",
    "role": "owner",
    "industry": null,
    "country_code": null,
    "website": null,
    "setup_completed": false,
    "avatar_url": null,
    "permissions": { "manage_ai_agents": true, "manage_workspace_roles": true },
    "subscription": { "plan_name": "Starter", "agent_limit": null, "language_limit": 3 }
  },
  "next_path": "/onboarding/workspace"
}
```

## Workspaces

| Method | Path | Request | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/api/onboarding/options` | Session cookie | Industries, supported countries, optional default country |
| GET | `/api/workspaces/{id}` | Session cookie | Metadata only for a workspace the user belongs to |
| POST | `/api/workspaces/{id}/setup` | Multipart form, session cookie, CSRF header | Save fields; mark setup complete; return dashboard path |
| GET | `/api/workspaces/{id}/avatar` | Session cookie | Sanitized PNG avatar for a workspace member |
| GET | `/api/health` | None | 200 when the database is reachable; 503 otherwise |

Workspace setup form fields:

| Field | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| `name` | Required; trimmed; 1–100 characters |
| `country_code` | Required; valid supported ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code |
| `industry` | One of the offered industries; defaults to Other |
| `website` | Optional; full HTTP(S) URL |
| `avatar` | Optional file; actual PNG, JPEG, or WebP; at most 2 MiB and 16 million source pixels |

The avatar is re-encoded to a 256×256 PNG, with metadata removed, and stored in PostgreSQL. Repeat setup requests update the same workspace. Membership and Owner permission are checked by the backend.

## Session and error contract

The `petrix_session` cookie is HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, and Secure in production. Its token is hashed in the database. The readable `petrix_csrf` cookie must be echoed in `X-Petrix-CSRF` for authenticated mutations. Angular's HTTP client handles that automatically for relative same-origin API requests.

Errors use FastAPI's `detail` response field. The UI shows failure messages after failed requests and advances only after successful API responses.

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 400 | Expired/used authentication request, invalid provider association, or blocked email |
| 401 | Missing, expired, or revoked session |
| 403 | Failed CSRF check, disallowed request origin, or insufficient role |
| 404 | Workspace unavailable to this user, or no avatar |
| 409 | Identity already belongs to another account, or inconsistent membership |
| 422 | Invalid email, workspace fields, country, industry, or avatar |
| 429 | Authentication request limit reached; `Retry-After` included |
| 503 | Email delivery or database temporarily unavailable |

## AI agents

The prefix below is `/api/workspaces/{workspace_id}/agents`. All requests require a valid session and membership in that workspace. Mutations require the CSRF header and Manage AI Agents permission. The workspace must have completed onboarding. All resource lookups are scoped to the workspace.

| Method | Path after prefix | Request | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GET | Empty | None | Agents, current permission, plan capacity and usage |
| POST | Empty | Multipart `name`, `default_language`, optional `avatar` | 201; saved agent, version 1 |
| POST | `/import` | Multipart `file` containing a Petrix JSON export | 201; new agent, version 1 |
| GET | `/{agent_id}` | None | Saved configuration and revision |
| GET | `/{agent_id}/avatar` | None | Sanitized PNG |
| GET | `/{agent_id}/export` | Manage permission | Portable JSON download |
| POST | `/{agent_id}/personalization` | JSON `expected_revision`, `llm_enabled`, `persona` | Saved agent with updated revision |
| POST | `/{agent_id}/languages` | JSON `expected_revision`, `languages`, `default_language` | Saved agent; selected-language/quota checks |
| POST | `/{agent_id}/identity` | Multipart `expected_revision`, `name`, optional `avatar`, `remove_avatar` | Saved agent |
| POST | `/{agent_id}/voice` | JSON `expected_revision`, `voice_enabled`, `voice_name`, `voice_speed` | Saved voice preferences |
| POST | `/{agent_id}/delete` | JSON `expected_revision`, exact `confirmation_name` | 204; configuration deleted, historical chats retained |
| GET | `/{agent_id}/versions?offset=0` | None | Version metadata, `has_more` |
| GET | `/{agent_id}/versions/{number}` | None | Snapshot metadata and configuration |
| POST | `/{agent_id}/versions/{number}/restore` | JSON `expected_revision` | Saved agent; earlier history retained |
| GET | `/{agent_id}/changes?offset=0` | None | Change history, `has_more` |
| GET | `/{agent_id}/network` | None | Workspace nodes and directed connections |
| POST | `/{agent_id}/network` | JSON `target_id` | 201; same-workspace connection |
| POST | `/{agent_id}/network/{connection_id}/delete` | Empty JSON | 204; remove an outgoing connection |
| POST | `/{agent_id}/tester/messages` | JSON `content`, optional `conversation_id` | Model reply and conversation ID |

`GET /api/agents/options` returns the language catalog, upload size, import contract, and configured tester/voice-runtime availability.

`GET /api/workspaces/{workspace_id}/roles` and `POST` on the same path require Owner or Administrator role. The POST JSON contains Boolean `admin` and `member` fields for Manage AI Agents. The Owner grant is immutable.

Version and change-log pages contain up to 50 records. Stale revisions and capacity conflicts return 409; invalid fields/images/languages/imports return 422; an import larger than 15 MiB returns 413. Unconfigured or failing model connections return 503. Tester request limits return 429.

See [AI_AGENTS.md](AI_AGENTS.md) for configuration, import examples, retention policy, and provider setup.

## Workflows and event tester

Milestone 3 adds these paths beneath `/api/workspaces/{workspace_id}/agents/{agent_id}`:

| Method | Path | Request | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/workflows` | Session and membership | Saved tree, workflow revision, trigger/action catalogue |
| POST | `/workflows` | Manage permission, CSRF; JSON `expected_revision`, `nodes` | Validated tree and new workflow revision |
| POST | `/tester/events` | Manage permission, CSRF; JSON `event`, event fields, optional language, conversation ID after start | Saved conversation ID, assistant messages, quick replies, execution trace, lifecycle state |

Each saved workflow node includes a positive integer `number`, unique within the agent across triggers and actions. The backend assigns it on creation and preserves it by node UUID on subsequent saves, including reordering. Deleted numbers are not reused. Clients may omit `number`; supplied values cannot override server assignments. Use the returned tree after saving to obtain new numbers. The tester's trace includes `node_number` alongside `node_id`; both are null for a generative reply. The allocation counter is internal and is not a client-editable document field.

Version `0.4.0` adds `matching` to tester responses: method, scope, selected node ID/number/name, score, entities, optional context summary, clarification fields, stage attempts, and controlled provider warnings. `match_mode: "approximate"` now uses fuzzy → semantic → Groq recognition when configured; `"exact"` opts out of the added stages. A clarification response has message source `clarification`, executes no workflow actions, and preserves the relevant waiting context. Entities are available to actions through `system["intent"]`; they are not automatically copied into custom variables. See [INTENT_MATCHING.md](INTENT_MATCHING.md).

Start with `{"event":"chat_started"}`. Subsequent events require that response's `conversation_id`. Message events use `{"event":"message_received","conversation_id":"...","content":"Balance"}`. Attachment events use `attachment: {name, media_type}` with `media_type` one of `image`, `audio`, `video`, or `file`; these are simulated metadata. As of 0.12.0, `collect_feedback` requires a closed chat, a pending rating request, its `feedback_token`, and an integer `rating` from 1 to 5. Other supported events are `chat_closed`, `chat_timeout`, and `ai_timeout`.

The Angular tester uses `/tester/events`, including its saved greeting. `/tester/messages` remains available as the earlier direct generative endpoint for compatibility; it does not execute workflows. See [WORKFLOWS.md](WORKFLOWS.md) for node schemas, ordering rules, matching, supported placeholders, and current limits.

Set variable is now available as `type: "set_variable"`, with config fields `variable_name` and `chat_script`. It stores a typed value in the current conversation and creates no assistant message. `/tester/events` includes `variables` in its response. Variable assignment errors and missing message placeholders return 422, rolling back that turn's data and messages. Existing session/CSRF/role/ownership checks and revision-based workflow saves apply. See [SET_VARIABLE.md](SET_VARIABLE.md) for expressions, system variables, limits, and the complete example.


Branch is available as `type: "branch"`. Its config contains 1–10 ordered `{id, name, chat_script}` conditions and `else_path_id`. Store its distinct action lists in `paths: [{id, children}]`, with exactly one matching path per condition and Else; ordinary `children` must be empty. Path IDs are unique UUIDs and have no step number. Node validation, numbering, and Jump reference checks traverse every path. Tester traces include `outcome: "branched"`, `path_id`, and `condition_name`. The first truthy condition wins; errors return 422 with transactional rollback. See [BRANCH.md](BRANCH.md) for examples, survey-value syntax, and continuation behavior.


Send API is available as `type: "send_api"`. Config fields are `method`, `url`, `headers: [{key,value}]`, `payload_mode` (`json` or `expression`), `payload`, `variable_name`, `timeout_seconds` (default 30), and three UUIDs: `success_path_id`, `error_path_id`, `timeout_path_id`. Store one matching `paths: [{id,children}]` container per outcome and keep `children` empty. The result variable contains `{ok,status_code,body,error}`. Traces include the selected path, outcome, HTTP status, and controlled error code. Authentication and workflow revision checks are unchanged. See [SEND_API.md](SEND_API.md) for request/response formats, limits, private-network configuration, and handling external side effects.


## Database connections and SQL Query (0.8.0)

Database routes use `/api/workspaces/{workspace_id}/database-connections`. Normal cookie sessions, workspace membership, CSRF on writes, and origin checks apply. Owners/admins manage connections; Manage AI Agents allows access to safe verified connector options.

| Method | Suffix | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | empty | Connection table and supported types; never returns passwords or ciphertext |
| GET | `/options` | Verified `{id,name,type}` choices in this workspace for workflow configuration |
| POST | empty | Create, encrypt password, and verify connection; 201 with verified/error status |
| POST | `/{id}` | Update fields with `expected_revision`, optional password, and reverify |
| POST | `/{id}/verify` | Recheck access; requires `expected_revision` |
| POST | `/{id}/delete` | Delete an unused connection; requires `expected_revision` |

Fields: `name`, `type: "postgresql"`, `host`, `port` (default 5432), `database`, `username`, `password`, `ssl_mode` (`verify-full`, `require`, `disable`; default verify-full). An omitted/null/empty password on edit retains the saved secret. Names are case-insensitively unique. Responses include status, verification time, a controlled error code, revision, and timestamps. Failed verification is persisted as `status: "error"` and excluded from options. Stale changes and deletion of referenced connections return 409. Foreign IDs return 404. Up to 20 connectors per workspace.

SQL Query has `type: "sql_query"` and config `connection_id`, `query`, `query_mode` (`template` or `expression`), `timeout_seconds` (1–120, default 30), `variable_name`, and three distinct UUIDs: `success_path_id`, `error_path_id`, `timeout_path_id`. Keep normal `children` empty; each ID must have one matching `paths: [{id,children}]` container. Workflow save validates connector ownership/verification. Runtime rechecks the connector, binds scalar chat parameters, applies read-only transactions and timeouts, and returns exactly one outcome. The result is `{ok,rows,columns,row_count,truncated,error}`. Traces include `outcome`, `path_id`, `row_count`, and a controlled `error`. An empty result follows Success. See [SQL_QUERY.md](SQL_QUERY.md) for limits and data formats.


## Switch Language (0.9.0)

`type: "switch_language"` is now available, with `config: {"target_language":"fr"}`. Choose a supported language code already present in this agent's configured languages. A workflow save rejects unavailable targets at every nesting level; runtime checks them again. The action uses ordinary children, emits no assistant message, and updates the conversation's existing `language` state. Tester responses use the existing top-level `language`; its trace entry also contains `previous_language` and `target_language`. Branch/scripts see the new `language` immediately. The workflow tester passes the active language to generative fallback prompts, while the legacy `/tester/messages` endpoint retains its existing default behavior.

Language settings changes and agent-version restoration reject removal of a language referenced by any saved Switch Language action (including disabled ones). Update or remove those actions first. Existing workspace/agent ownership, Manage AI Agents, CSRF, workflow revisions, and conversation checks are unchanged. Switch Language itself introduced no migration; the current Send Attachment release requires head 0007. See [SWITCH_LANGUAGE.md](SWITCH_LANGUAGE.md).


## Send Attachment (0.10.0)

All paths below use `/api/workspaces/{workspace_id}/agents/{agent_id}` and the current session. Mutations also require Manage AI Agents permission and the `X-Petrix-CSRF` header.

| Method and path | Request / result |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /workflow-assets` | Multipart `file_format` (`image`, `audio`, `video`, `document`) and one `file`, at most 20 MiB. Returns 201 with `{id,name,format,content_type,size_bytes,url}`. |
| `GET /workflow-assets/{id}` | Agent/workspace-scoped upload metadata. |
| `GET /workflow-assets/{id}/file` | Authenticated download; `?inline=true` permits supported image/audio/video MIME previews. Byte ranges return 206; invalid ranges return 416. Documents remain downloads. |
| `POST /workflow-assets/{id}/delete` | Deletes an unused upload. Returns 409 while any saved action translation references it, including disabled/nested/outcome steps. |
| `GET /tester/attachments/{id}` | Conversation-owner download. Also supports safe inline media and byte ranges. |

An action uses this workflow config:

```json
{"translations":{"en":{"file_format":"document","source":"upload","asset_id":"<uploaded-asset-uuid>","url":"","chat_script":""}}}
```

For `source:"link"`, set `url` to an HTTP(S) file URL and `asset_id` to null. For `source:"script"`, set `chat_script` to a safe Python expression returning a URL string. Inactive source fields are cleared when saved. Asset references must belong to this agent/workspace and match the selected format. Per-language settings follow Send message's active/default/first fallback. Runtime script URLs may also be an attachment-survey URL belonging to the current conversation.

The existing revision-checked `POST /workflows` saves the action. Tester output contains `source:"send_attachment"`, the action's `node_id`, empty `content`/`quick_replies`, and a one-item `attachments` array. Each file has `{id,name,url,content_type,size_bytes,format,external}`. Hosted files have `size_bytes:null` and `external:true`; no backend request is made. Uploaded assets are copied into conversation-owned storage and return a conversation download URL. Ten attachment actions may run per turn; a failed action rolls back that turn, including newly delivered file copies. Each agent has a 100-file/1-GiB asset quota. See [SEND_ATTACHMENT.md](SEND_ATTACHMENT.md). Schema head is **0007**.


Each translation requires 1–10 cards and at most three buttons per card. Cards and buttons have UUID identities unique within that language. Text limits are title/label 80, subtitle 200, reply message 1,000; URLs use at most 2,048 characters. Image is null, `{source:"upload",asset_id:"<image-asset-uuid>",url:""}`, or `{source:"link",asset_id:null,url:"https://example.com/image.png"}`.
