## Chat Closed and Collect Feedback (0.12.0)

`GET /workflows` includes two flags on each action definition: `allowed_after_close` identifies the 13 post-conversation types; `post_close_only:true` identifies Collect Feedback. Planned action definitions remain `available:false`. Chat Closed's entire subtree must contain allowed actions, including disabled children and outcome paths. Jump destinations and their automatic continuations are validated across roots; incoming waits and conversational actions are rejected with 422. Incoming triggers cannot be nested under Chat Closed. Ordinary workflows cannot Jump into its steps.

Save the new action with `kind:"action", type:"collect_feedback"` and config:

```json
{
  "rating_enabled": true,
  "translations": {
    "en": {"webchat_rating_title": "Please rate the conversation"},
    "fr": {"webchat_rating_title": "Veuillez évaluer la conversation"}
  }
}
```

The flag must be a JSON boolean. While enabled, at least one translation is required and each configured title must be nonempty and at most 500 characters. Titles support existing text substitutions. The action must be physically beneath the permanent Chat Closed trigger. Existing feedback receiving triggers retain `kind:"trigger", type:"collect_feedback"` with their existing config.

Post `{"event":"chat_closed","conversation_id":"..."}` to `/tester/events` to simulate a live-agent close event. The conversation is marked closed before automation, pending surveys/waits are cancelled, and later normal events are rejected with 409. Tester closures record actor/time and `close_source:"tester"`. Chat timeout does not invoke this trigger. Livechats/Inbox and published-channel close events are not integrated by this release.

Tester responses now include `closed_at`, `csat_rating`, `automation_error`, and `feedback`. With an outstanding request, `feedback` has this shape (IDs below are illustrative):

```json
{
  "token": "eab1be7d-513b-4f2a-8f56-a05fcd1b2b39",
  "title": "Please rate the conversation",
  "node_id": "e6e37774-841c-412c-bb88-a7f91973ff96",
  "node_number": 7,
  "language": "en",
  "min_rating": 1,
  "max_rating": 5
}
```

It is structured state, not an assistant message. The first enabled request issued during closure is retained. The action traces `outcome:"rating_requested"` and then continues. The title is resolved when issued and remains valid even after saved workflow changes.

Submit `{"event":"collect_feedback","conversation_id":"...","rating":4,"feedback_token":"..."}`. A strict integer 1–5 is required; booleans, numeric strings, fractional values, and missing/out-of-range ratings return 422. A missing/wrong/foreign request token, no outstanding request, an open chat, or a second submission returns 409. Ownership/permission/CSRF checks still apply. On success `feedback:null`, `feedback_submitted:true`, and `csat_rating:4` are returned. An optional matching feedback trigger may emit its own messages; without one, rating storage completes without generic fallback or an artificial assistant reply.

Closing and rating acceptance are committed before their workflow automation runs. Expected workflow failures return **200 with the actual closed/accepted state**, a nonempty `automation_error`, diagnostic `notice`, and `outcome:"automation_failed"` trace. Failed automation state changes are rolled back; closure or the accepted rating remains stored. Retrying the close event or accepted rating returns 409 and does not replay external effects. Successful ordinary turns retain their existing atomic behavior. There is no automatic lifecycle retry or distributed rollback of external API calls.

The frontend disables normal chat controls after closure and renders the issued rating panel separately. Both `/tester/events` and the older `/tester/messages` endpoint reject normal replies to a closed conversation; the latter makes no model call for that conversation. Client integrations must use the returned feedback token rather than posting arbitrary CSAT. See [CHAT_CLOSED.md](CHAT_CLOSED.md). No new dependency or migration; schema head remains **0007**.

## Complete Collect Feedback (0.13.0)

This extends the 0.12.0 lifecycle contract above. Chat Closed remains permanent and restricted to its 13 allowed types. Collect Feedback supports ratings, survey answers, or both; it now pauses the remaining post-close actions until submission. Existing 0.12.0 configs and outstanding rating tokens remain readable without a migration.

Save `kind:"action", type:"collect_feedback"` beneath Chat Closed with this configuration (field UUID is illustrative):

```json
{
  "rating_enabled": true,
  "rating_variable_name": "feedback_rating",
  "survey_enabled": true,
  "fields": [
    {"id":"960979b8-3832-4495-b482-2282a20d0b39","reply_type":"open_response","required":false,"variable_name":"feedback_comment"}
  ],
  "translations": {
    "en": {
      "webchat_rating_title": "How did we do?",
      "rating_request_message": "How would you rate your conversation?",
      "submission_text": "Thank you for your feedback!",
      "fields": {
        "960979b8-3832-4495-b482-2282a20d0b39": {"question":"Any other comments?","placeholder":"Please share your comments","choices":[]}
      }
    }
  }
}
```

`rating_enabled`, `survey_enabled`, and each `required` are strict booleans. Up to 50 unique fields are supported. `reply_type` is `open_response`, `number`, `email`, `phone`, or `choice`. Choice translations require 1–13 distinct nonempty strings of at most 100 characters. Questions are 1–1,000 characters, placeholders at most 200, rating titles at most 500, and rating requests/submission text at most 4,000. Unknown language/field IDs, duplicate variable names, reserved names, and incomplete enabled settings return 422. Variable names follow existing 1–64-character naming and capacity rules; `feedback_rating` is now an ordinary persisted variable, and `language` cannot be used for feedback storage.

Each translation contains its localised text and optional field translations keyed by the shared field UUID. Every enabled survey field needs a question in at least one language. Missing field translations use active/default/first fallback independently; all top-level configured translations require submission text and, when rating is enabled, both rating prompts. Legacy rating-only configs gain default request/confirmation text when validated or saved.

Start the tester with optional `channel:"webchat"|"messaging"|"bitrix24"|"africas_talking"` (default `webchat`). The channel is stored on the conversation; a conflicting later channel returns 409 and requires a new conversation. This is a tester preview contract, not a transport connection.

After `chat_closed`, response `feedback` retains `token`, `title`, `node_id`, `node_number`, `language`, `min_rating`, and `max_rating`, and adds:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `rating_enabled` | Whether a rating is requested |
| `rating_variable_name` | Stored rating variable |
| `request_message` | Resolved non-Webchat rating prompt |
| `channel` | Stored tester preview channel |
| `typed_rating` | True for Bitrix24/Africa’s Talking |
| `rating_buttons` | `[1,2,3,4,5]` for Messaging buttons; otherwise `[]` |
| `fields` | Ordered issued fields with shared `id`, `reply_type`, `required`, `variable_name`, resolved `question`, `placeholder`, and translated `choices` |

Private workflow revision/continuation and submission template are not returned in the public form. `waiting` continues to describe ordinary chat waits and stays false for the closed feedback form. `close_automation.status` is stored as `waiting_feedback` while the form is outstanding.

Submit all enabled parts through the existing `/tester/events` route:

```json
{
  "event": "collect_feedback",
  "conversation_id": "<conversation UUID>",
  "feedback_token": "<issued token UUID>",
  "rating": 4,
  "feedback_answers": {
    "960979b8-3832-4495-b482-2282a20d0b39": "Very helpful agent."
  }
}
```

`feedback_answers` is a UUID-keyed map of strings, up to 50 entries and 4,000 characters each. Number/Email/Phone strings are validated and normalized into typed stored values. Only issued fields are accepted. Required blanks, invalid formats, malformed/foreign field IDs, extra answers, oversized text, booleans/nested answer values, missing enabled ratings, or a rating supplied for a survey-only form return 422 **without consuming the token or partially saving variables**. Optional blanks save `null`. Rating remains a strict integer 1–5 when enabled. For survey-only forms, omit `rating`. Token, one-submission, permission, ownership, CSRF, and rate-limit checks remain enforced.

Acceptance commits the answer variables, optional `csat_rating`, submission flag/time, and removes the pending form before resuming actions. Normal success returns `feedback:null`, `feedback_submitted:true`, `feedback_confirmation` (the resolved localised Settings text), optional rating, and the variables. Confirmation placeholders resolve with submitted variables. The action’s children and remaining post-close actions resume once, then the optional existing feedback receiving trigger runs. Without that trigger no generic fallback runs. Both features off means no form is issued and actions continue immediately.

An action after Collect Feedback can now use `feedback_rating` and `feedback_comment` directly. Use actions before it for closure work that must run without a submission. A workflow revision change preserves the original form’s answer/variable snapshot but blocks its stale continuation after saving the answers. Legacy 0.12.0 outstanding requests have no saved continuation and are accepted without replaying previously completed close actions.

Expected continuation/confirmation/callback errors return 200 with accepted feedback, stored variables, and `automation_error`; accepted answers remain saved and duplicates return 409. Partial automation changes are rolled back. External effects are not automatically retried or undone. The chat remains closed throughout; normal messages and generic chat waits stay unavailable. See [CHAT_CLOSED.md](CHAT_CLOSED.md) and [COLLECT_FEEDBACK.md](COLLECT_FEEDBACK.md). Schema head remains **0007**; no new dependency.

## Close Chat (0.14.0)

The existing action catalogue reports `type:"close_chat", available:true, allowed_after_close:true, post_close_only:false`. Save the action with `kind:"action"`, `type:"close_chat"`, `config:{}`, and normal name/description/enabled/children fields. Unknown configuration fields are rejected with 422. Authentication, Manage AI Agents, CSRF, ownership, and optimistic workflow revision checks are unchanged.

When the action executes in an open conversation, the interpreter returns a server-owned close command and stops its current flow. The route persists the incoming turn, earlier output messages/files, collected variables, close time/actor, `close_source:"workflow"`, and the closing action ID/number before running the permanent `chat_closed` trigger once. No second client event is needed. Actions following the open-flow Close chat, its children, and enclosing continuations do not execute.

The existing `/tester/events` response includes `closed:true`, `closed_at`, `close_source`, earlier messages and a combined trace. Close action traces use `type:"close_chat", outcome:"closed"`; a Close chat encountered in an already-closed conversation traces `outcome:"already_closed"`, continues normally, and does not dispatch another closure. Existing feedback request/token/submission behavior is unchanged. The explicit tester close event continues to record `close_source:"tester"`.

A failure before reaching Close chat rolls back the ordinary turn and leaves the conversation open. A failure in the following Chat Closed automation returns 200 with `closed:true`, the earlier committed messages/files/variables, a visible `automation_error`, and a close-automation failure trace. Partial post-close state changes roll back. Repeated ordinary messages or close events return 409 and do not replay the workflow. External side effects are not automatically retried or undone.

This action is usable in the current tester, including Branch paths, API/SQL outcomes, survey completion, and Jump destinations. Livechats controls and published-channel delivery remain separate milestones. No new migration/dependency is added; schema head remains **0007**. See [CLOSE_CHAT.md](CLOSE_CHAT.md).

`GET /api/workspaces/{workspace_id}/agents/{agent_id}/workflows` adds `llm_processing` metadata containing `model`, `provider:"Groq"`, `available`, and `knowledge_supported`. Availability reflects the server key; the catalogue action remains Ready so it can be configured before the key is installed.
```json
{
  "input": "{description.text}",

  "model": "intent",

  "timeout_path_id": "bf0f9b90-0ba0-4262-838e-5cdbe78c9602"
}
```

The node needs `children:[]` and exactly three `paths` entries with the matching IDs and their own `children`. Both prompt modes accept `template` or `expression`. Expressions use the existing safe Python interpreter. Temperature must be numeric, finite, and 0–2. Timeout must be an integer 1–120. Model is the server-controlled `intent` alias, not an arbitrary provider or API key.

Success stores a string directly in the named variable. Error/Timeout stores null instead of retaining stale output, provided a variable slot is available. | Method | Path | Request/result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/api/workspaces/{workspace_id}/agents/{agent_id}/knowledge` | Returns `agent_id`, `revision`, `sources`, and `updated_at`; no row is created by GET. |

## Live Agent Handoff and Inbox (0.19.0)

See [INBOX.md](INBOX.md) for endpoint and payload contracts. Dynamic team variables accept an active workspace team ID or Auto Team Match `{id,name}` result.

The runtime pauses and saves the original workflow/continuation on a successful handoff. Public `live_chat` status contains the current status, revision, assignee ID, return status, and resume flag, rather than the saved snapshot. Customer messages while pending/active go to the live thread without invoking AI. Inbox claim/reply/close routes require current workspace membership and eligibility/assignment; they do not require AI management rights. Mutations require CSRF. Replies use a client UUID for idempotency; queue/status mutations use revisions and row locks.

Human closure invokes the existing durable Chat Closed/feedback engine, then an internal saved handoff continuation. This return mode cannot be posted as a public tester event. Post-close automation/return errors preserve closure and accepted answers; retries do not replay a consumed return. A pending/active live chat prevents AI agent deletion and team membership/deletion changes affecting that chat. **Migration 0011 is required.** No runtime dependency is added. Existing agent creation/import remains unlimited.


## External integrations and one-way handoff

Version 0.20.0 adds workspace-scoped `/external-integrations`, `/external-integrations/options`, and `/{platform}/verify` routes, plus owned tester `/external-link` and `/external-review` routes. ## AI Agent Handoff and Network credentials

Version 0.21.0 adds masked incoming Network credentials, explicit enable/rotate/reveal, and verified outgoing connections under each agent. The Ready `ai_agent_handoff` action stores a connection UUID. The source conversation stops executing locally and forwards events to the authenticated receiving agent, retaining the browser conversation ID. Public source variables arrive in read-only `_transferred_context`; recent sanitized history, surveys, receiving media, and feedback continue through the existing tester. A receiving close does not resume the source.

See [AI_AGENT_HANDOFF.md](AI_AGENT_HANDOFF.md#api) for the full management and protocol-v1 route tables, authorization, body limits, request IDs, retry semantics, revocation, and file proxy. Cross-instance peer routes authenticate with agent secrets and scoped session tokens, independently of browser cookies. Remote receiving instances require HTTPS and Petrix 0.21+; same-instance calls use the authenticated local receiver service.

Tester event JSON and uploads accept optional UUID `client_event_id` for retries of the exact same input. Responses add safe `ai_handoff` destination/status/language/pending/error metadata. GET conversation restores receiving state; POST `tester/conversations/{id}/ai-retry` retries a saved operation. Public inputs cannot provide trusted network actors or internal resume state. Apply migration **0013** before starting the API. Existing dependency pins and unlimited agent creation/import are unchanged.


## Create Ticket, settings and support cases

Version 0.22.0 activates `create_ticket` with tags/groups, assignee, verified sender, variable-aware subject/description/customer fields, separate optional templates, and typed custom-field overrides. Conversation assignments are copied before overrides; their source values remain unchanged. A successful action sets read-only system value `last_ticket` and adds ticket ID/reference to its trace. It does not emit a message, close the chat, or transfer ownership. It is allowed under Chat Closed.

Workspace routes `/ticket-settings/{kind}` manage tags, groups, email-domains and email-templates with current management permission, CSRF and revisions. Sender verification uses live CNAME/TXT DNS checks with a 30-day validity window; existing SMTP provides outbound transport. `/tickets/options` provides current action choices. `/tickets` lists access-scoped summary pages; `/tickets/{id}` exposes detail/activity/email metadata. Status/assignment updates, internal notes, queued sends and explicit failed/unconfirmed email retries use separate POST routes. See [CREATE_TICKET.md](CREATE_TICKET.md#api) for the complete route table and [TICKETS.md](TICKETS.md) for permissions and SMTP recovery.

Ticket/email intent is committed before any SMTP attempt. Stable action/event receipts prevent duplicate tickets for the same operation. Failed SMTP does not remove the ticket, and unconfirmed sends are never automatically replayed. A new event or a different ticket node can create a distinct case. Incoming mailbox/reply synchronization is not part of these initial notifications. Apply migration **0014** before starting the API; all earlier migrations and dependency pins remain unchanged.

## Perception (0.32.0)

The authenticated `/api/workspaces/{workspace_id}/perception` API implements permission-scoped Overview, keyword/source configuration, durable collection logs/retries, read-only entry previews and translation settings. View and Manage grants are independent and every mutation requires CSRF; source/settings edits use optimistic revisions. Collection requires the configured server-owned public collection endpoint. Alerts and Categorization remain unavailable. See [Perception](PERCEPTION.md) for the route table, JSON collection contract, limits and schedule semantics. Apply additive migration **0024**.


## Advisor (0.33.0)

The `/api/workspaces/{workspace_id}/advisor` API provides owner-private conversation history and durable replies, validated staged attachments, bundled documentation and the current OpenAPI reference. Every conversation/file access checks the requesting user, workspace and current teamspace access. CSRF protects all mutations; client IDs and revisions reconcile safe retries. See [Advisor](ADVISOR.md) for routes, file/model limits, supported modes and migration **0025**. Advisor never executes workspace actions or exposes another user's private history.


## Publish Webchat — 0.34.0

Staff channel management lives under `/api/workspaces/{workspace_id}/agents/{agent_id}/webchat`. Public widget/session/conversation routes live under `/api/webchat`; they use visitor capabilities and never staff cookies. Staff mutations still require existing grants, CSRF and revisions. The generated OpenAPI reference includes both sets of routes. See [Webchat](WEBCHAT.md) for the full endpoint map, framing policy, frozen workflow revisions, file/privacy boundaries and deployment steps.

### Webchat message order — 0.34.1

Public Webchat messages include `sequence`, a decimal string identifying their stable order within that conversation. Sort and page by this server order; do not sort by display timestamp or random message UUID. The `before` cursor remains the message UUID. A user message also carries its own `client_message_id` when available, so a retried send can replace its optimistic bubble without duplication. Sequence values may have gaps and are unrelated to other visitors. Migration 0027 retains message IDs, content and original times.

## Publish → WhatsApp (0.35.0)

Staff prefix: `/api/workspaces/{workspace_id}/agents/{agent_id}/whatsapp`. Reads require View AI agents with workspace/teamspace access; mutations require Manage and CSRF. Channel creation is idempotent by `client_id`. Configuration and Basics changes use `expected_revision`; stale writes return 409. Secrets never appear in normal responses. Publishing enable/processing/delivery requires Lite or above.

| Method | Suffix | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET / POST | empty | List / create disabled channel (`client_id`, `name`). |
| GET / POST | `/{channel_id}` | Read / save Basics (`expected_revision`, `name`, `enabled`, `config`). |
| POST | `/{channel_id}/configuration` | Save numeric `app_id`, `phone_number_id`, private `app_secret`, `access_token`; blank secrets keep saved values. |
| POST | `/{channel_id}/verify` | Check saved token/phone with Meta; returns `verified` and safe `last_error`. No customer message is sent. |
| POST | `/{channel_id}/setup-secret` | Protected reveal of `verify_token`, with `expected_revision`. |
| POST | `/{channel_id}/reissue` | Confirmed Petrix verify-token rotation; disables and invalidates callback verification. |
| POST | `/{channel_id}/delete` | Confirmed deletion; native People/conversation history retained. |
| GET | `/{channel_id}/activity?offset=0` | Twenty incoming/outgoing activity items with `has_more`. |
| POST | `/{channel_id}/activity/{inbound|outbound}/{job_id}` | `{action,confirmed}`: dismiss interrupted inbound; retry known failed/blocked outbound; cancel remaining unsent/unconfirmed parts. Uncertain sends cannot be retried. |

Public callback: **GET `/api/whatsapp/webhooks/{meta_app_id}`** validates `hub.mode`, `hub.verify_token`, `hub.challenge` and returns the exact plain-text challenge. **POST** authenticates the raw body using `X-Hub-Signature-256` and the encrypted Meta App secret; caps bodies at 2 MiB and events at 1,000; deduplicates durable message/status receipts and routes by Phone number ID. Public cross-site intake does not relax staff origin/CSRF checks. Processing and delivery run in the durable worker, not the webhook request. Signed status callbacks bind recipient/channel/send identity and reconcile acceptance, delivery and read state.

Native Inbox `/reply` persists and queues WhatsApp staff replies atomically, checks active channel/ban and the 24-hour service window, and returns 409 with a useful explanation outside it. See [WhatsApp](WHATSAPP.md) for media caps, BSUID handling and recovery semantics.

### Inbox queue reads (0.35.1)

`GET /api/workspaces/{id}/inbox/conversations` retains its parameters, permission boundaries, filters, sorting, totals and page shape. Membership/roles are read afresh per request. Lightweight candidates and latest message/channel evidence are read in batches; visible People names and action grants are resolved for the returned page. Private runtime variables and full history are excluded from list queries. Detail and mutation endpoints authorize independently. No schema change is required.

ASK_SURVEY.title: Ask survey
ASK_SURVEY.content:
# Ask survey

Ask survey sends preset questions as regular chat messages, waits for each answer, validates it, and saves it in a chat variable. When the last field is answered or skipped, the workflow continues through the survey's nested steps and following actions.

## Configure the action

Open a workflow, choose **Add action → Messaging → Ask survey**, then use **Add field** for each question. Fields run from top to bottom. Expand a field to edit it, or use its delete icon to remove it before saving.

| Setting | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Question | Required question text, up to 4,000 characters. Existing variable placeholders work, including answers to earlier fields. |
| Answer must be | Text, Number, Attachment, Attachment(s), Email, or Phone. |
| Invalid answer reply | Required reply shown when validation fails. The same question remains active. |
| Chat variable name | A unique custom variable per field; 1–64 characters, starting with a letter, followed by letters, numbers, or underscores. System names and Python reserved names cannot be used. |
| Quick answers | Up to 13 optional, distinct buttons of 1–100 characters each. These offer choices without restricting other valid answers. |
| Enable skip | Allows the person to type `skip` or choose **Skip question** in the tester. The variable is set to null and the next question is asked. |

Click **Save** after filling the required settings. A survey supports 1–50 fields. Question text, invalid replies, and quick answers support the same variable placeholders as Send message. The editor does not automatically translate these texts.

## Answer formats

| Format | Saved value |
| --- | --- |
| Text | Non-empty text with surrounding whitespace removed. |
| Number | A finite JSON number; integers remain integers. Signed decimals and scientific notation are accepted. Grouping commas, NaN, infinity, and numbers outside the supported range are rejected. |
| Email | A syntactically valid email address, with normalized domain casing. No DNS/delivery verification is performed. |
| Phone | A string of 7–15 digits, optionally starting with `+`. Spaces, parentheses, dots, and hyphens are removed. No country inference or ownership verification is performed. |
| Attachment | One uploaded file represented by an object with `id`, `name`, `content_type`, `size_bytes`, and an authenticated download `url`. |
| Attachment(s) | One to ten uploaded files submitted together, stored as a list of those objects. |

File limits are 10 MiB per file and 20 MiB per answer. Files must not be empty. File bytes are stored in PostgreSQL with the conversation; only metadata enters the chat variable. The download endpoint checks workspace, agent, and conversation ownership, and delivers files as downloads. Original filenames are normalized to remove path components.

During a file question, use **Upload a file** or **Upload files together**, then **Send files**. Sending one answer never reuses those files for the next question; the picker resets. Text answers to file questions produce the configured invalid reply. The existing **Test an event → Attachment received** control simulates metadata only and cannot satisfy a survey's real upload requirement.

## Example

Create a survey with:

| Field | Question | Format | Variable |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | What is your name? | Text | `customer_name` |
| 2 | What is your email address? | Email | `email` |
| 3 | Upload your document. | Attachment | `document` |

Follow it with a Send message action:

```text
Thank you, {customer_name}. We have recorded your email as {email}.
```

Later actions can read `{document.name}` or `{document.url}`. For multiple files, paths such as `{documents.0.name}` are supported. A Jump after the confirmation can return to an existing menu.

## Conversation behavior

- A pending survey receives message/file answers before intent matching, fallback, or generative replies. There are no model calls to classify its answers.
- Each valid answer is saved before the next question is sent. Invalid answers do not advance or overwrite a variable.
- Skipping stores null, including when that variable held a value from a previous visit. Without skip enabled, `skip` is treated as a normal answer and validated against the format.
- The final answer resumes the exact saved branch continuation. Consecutive surveys and nested triggers remain sequential; a final answer is never consumed as the next survey's first answer.
- Closing or timing out the chat cancels the pending survey and runs the relevant lifecycle workflow. Completed answers remain in that conversation's variables.
- A saved workflow change invalidates the pending answer token. Restart the tester after editing a running survey.
- A failed downstream action rolls back the entire answer turn, including file bytes, messages, and variable changes. The original question remains active for retry.

Questions, answers, skips, and validation replies are persisted as regular messages. Channel-specific auto-fill buttons, external channel publishing, and subscription interaction billing are separate integrations; this update provides the workflow builder and authenticated tester.

## Apply this update on Windows

Keep your existing `backend/.env`, virtual environment, Mailpit, and database. Stop the API, copy the updated source into your project, then run from **backend**:

```powershell
python -m alembic upgrade head
python -m alembic current
python -m uvicorn app.main:create_app --factory --reload --port 8000 --no-access-log
```

The migration check should show `0006 (head)`. Migration `0005` adds `agent_attachments`; it does not reset existing workflows, numbers, accounts, or conversations. No new dependency is required for Ask survey. Restart Angular with your existing `npm start` command.

## API

The prefix remains `/api/workspaces/{workspace_id}/agents/{agent_id}`.

| Endpoint | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /workflows` | The existing revision-checked whole-tree save. An `ask_survey` node has `config.fields[]` with the field settings described above and a stable field UUID. |
| `POST /tester/events` | Survey text answers use `event: message_received`, `content`, `conversation_id`, and the current `survey_answer_token`. |
| `POST /tester/attachments` | Multipart `conversation_id`, `survey_answer_token`, optional `language`, and one or more `files` parts. Upload and answer processing are atomic. |
| `GET /tester/attachments/{id}` | Authenticated download for the same conversation owner and agent/workspace. |

Tester responses include `survey` (or null), progress, the expected format, skip permission, and the answer token. Send that token with each answer. A stale/replayed token returns 409 and does not advance the survey. File responses also include `attachments[]`; the tester displays their download links as regular user messages.

Implementation lives in `backend/app/workflows/actions/ask_survey`, `backend/app/workflows/attachments.py`, the existing workflow runtime/routes, and `frontend/src/app/features/workflows/actions/ask-survey`.

AUTHENTICATION.title: Authentication and account association
AUTHENTICATION.content:
# Authentication and account association

## Independent registration

An invitation is not needed. All syntactically valid, eligible personal and professional email addresses are accepted, including Gmail and Yahoo. `BLOCKED_EMAIL_DOMAINS` optionally contains a comma-separated domain block list. No corporate-domain-only policy is applied.

Email is normalized using a case-insensitive account policy. Gmail dots and plus aliases are not rewritten. Email format validation does not require an MX lookup at registration; ownership is proved through the inbox link.

The user, initial workspace, and Owner membership are created in one database transaction after authentication succeeds. The workspace starts with a Default AI Agent, its first configuration version, and default role permissions in that same transaction. Unique email constraints and PostgreSQL conflict handling prevent concurrent registration attempts for one normalized email from creating duplicate users and workspaces.

On later sign-ins, the same user and existing membership are loaded. An unfinished setup returns to onboarding. A completed setup returns to `/app/agents`.

## Magic links

Links contain 32 random bytes encoded as a URL-safe token. Only its SHA-256 digest is stored in the magic-link table. The configured lifetime is `MAGIC_LINK_MINUTES`, initially 15. Consumption is a conditional database UPDATE requiring an unused, unexpired token. GET requests never consume tokens. Account creation and session issuance commit only after successful validation.

The email-request endpoint is limited per normalized email and client IP in a database-backed fixed time window. Initial limits are five requests per email and thirty per IP in fifteen minutes. The response does not disclose whether the account already exists. Invalid or explicitly blocked addresses can be rejected according to the registration policy.

SMTP acceptance is required before returning 202. On SMTP failure, the token and pending changes are rolled back and the client receives 503. Application logs omit recipients, authentication links, and raw provider token responses. A delivered message could become unusable if a subsequent database commit fails; the user can request another link.

## Google

Create a Web application OAuth client for Petrix AI in your Google project. Configure the local callback exactly as:

`http://localhost:8000/api/auth/oauth/google/callback`

Set `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` and `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` on the backend. Google sign-in requests `openid email profile` and uses PKCE. Authlib validates OAuth state and the ID token's signature, issuer, audience, expiry, and nonce.

For a verified `@gmail.com` address, or a verified Google Workspace address with an `hd` claim, Google is treated as authoritative for the mailbox. A matching existing normalized email is associated with that verified identity, avoiding a second user or workspace. Otherwise Petrix AI requests fresh mailbox verification before first association. The provider's email address alone does not grant access.

## Microsoft

Register a Web application in Microsoft Entra. To accept personal and work accounts, select the audience that supports accounts in any organization directory and personal Microsoft accounts. Use the local callback:

`http://localhost:8000/api/auth/oauth/microsoft/callback`

Set `MICROSOFT_CLIENT_ID` and `MICROSOFT_CLIENT_SECRET`. The default authority is `common`; the implementation also accepts `consumers`, `organizations`, or a configured tenant UUID. Use an authorization code flow; the application does not use the implicit grant flow.

Authlib validates signature, audience, expiry, nonce, state, and PKCE. For the `common` issuer template, the code additionally validates that the signed tenant ID is a UUID and that the issuer exactly equals `https://login.microsoftonline.com/{tid}/v2.0`. Configured tenant restrictions are enforced.

A Microsoft email claim is treated as a hint, not proof of ownership. On first association, the user confirms an email through a fresh magic link. An existing Petrix user should enter the email already associated with their account. Completing the link associates the stable Microsoft issuer and subject with that user. Later Microsoft sign-ins use the linked issuer and subject directly.

An external identity cannot be reassigned to a different account through this flow. Database uniqueness enforces that rule.

## Sessions and workspace access

Sessions are random opaque tokens whose hashes are stored in PostgreSQL, initially lasting seven days. Session tokens are not stored in browser local storage. Sign-out revokes the current session. Authenticated mutations require a session-bound CSRF token and an allowed browser origin. Workspace metadata, setup, and avatars require membership; initial setup additionally requires Owner permission.

Country choices come from ISO country data. `SUPPORTED_COUNTRIES` optionally restricts that list. `DEFAULT_COUNTRY=KE` is a configurable initial selection, not geolocation detection; users can change it. Names and countries are required. Industry defaults to Other. Website and avatar can be omitted.

## Environment boundary

Development defaults use Mailpit. Enabling an OAuth button requires both its backend client ID and secret. Live Google/Microsoft provider authentication needs valid app registrations and matching callback URLs; tests use local identity data and do not log in to real provider accounts.

Production requires HTTPS origins, Secure cookies, an adequately long signing secret, and encrypted SMTP. Serve the frontend and API behind one public origin so session/CSRF cookies work consistently. Configure trusted ingress addresses before relying on forwarded client IPs for throttling.

AUTO_FILL_FIELD.title: Auto Fill Field
AUTO_FILL_FIELD.content:
# Auto Fill Field

Version 0.16.0 makes **Add action → AI & data → Auto Fill Field** Ready and implements **Settings → Teamspace → Custom fields**.

The action classifies conversation information against selected **Single Select (Grouped)** conversation fields. It saves recognised option values on the chat and records the assignment result in a chat variable. It does not send a question or message by itself. A valid response with no matching options follows Success and leaves unmatched fields unchanged; a previously unset field stays unset.

## Upgrade

Keep your existing database and `backend/.env`. With your virtual environment active, run:

```powershell
cd C:\Users\Admin\petrix-ai\backend
python -m alembic upgrade head
python -m alembic current
```

The current revision is **0010 (head)**, including Teams settings. Migration **0009** adds workspace custom-field definitions and an independent JSON assignment column on existing conversations. Earlier workflows, agent settings, Knowledge sources, messages, media, and step numbers are retained. No new runtime dependency is added.

Use the same server model connection as LLM Processing:

```dotenv
GROQ_API_KEY=your_groq_key
GROQ_INTENT_MODEL=openai/gpt-oss-20b
```

Restart backend/frontend after replacing source. Enable LLM in the agent's Personalization settings. Auto Fill uses the configured Groq model at temperature 0 with a 30-second provider timeout. Provider timeouts follow **Error**, since this action has two outcome branches.

## Create a grouped conversation field

1. Open **Settings → Teamspace → Custom fields → Conversation fields**.
2. Click **Create new field** and select **Single Select (Grouped)**.
3. Set Name to `Enquiry type` and describe what it categorises.
4. Replace Field Options with the following JSON:

```json
[
  {
    "name": "Banking",
    "options": [
      {
        "value": "mobile_banking",
        "label": "Mobile banking",
        "description": "Mobile application access, mobile transfers, or mobile payments."
      },
      {
        "value": "accounts",
        "label": "Accounts",
        "description": "Account opening, account details, or account maintenance."
      }
    ]
  },
  {
    "name": "Cards",
    "options": [
      {
        "value": "card_issue",
        "label": "Card issue",
        "description": "Lost cards, card declines, card activation, or card PIN issues."
      }
    ]
  }
]
```

5. Leave Default value empty if you want unmatched enquiries to remain unset, or select an appropriate default.
6. Click **Create**.

`value` is the stable option identifier; `label` is its displayed name. Descriptions help the model distinguish choices. Values must be unique throughout one field, including across different groups. The field receives a UUID and a stable key such as `enquiry_type`. Renaming its display name preserves that key and all saved action references. Reopen the field to see its chat reference and full ID.

See [CUSTOM_FIELDS.md](CUSTOM_FIELDS.md) for the other supported settings field types, defaults, permissions, editing, and deletion behavior. People fields are explicitly marked Later. Only grouped conversation fields appear in the Auto Fill picker.

## Configure the action

| Setting | Example |
| --- | --- |
| Select fields | Enquiry type; select additional grouped fields if needed |
| Variable name | `matched_enquiry` |

Save, then configure actions under **Success** and **Error**. Up to 20 fields can be selected. Each action has its own result variable; names must start with a letter and use only letters, numbers, or underscores, up to 64 characters. Python keywords, built-in function names, read-only system names, and `language` are reserved.

## Complete test flow

1. Under **Chat started**, add Ask survey with question `Please describe your enquiry.`, Text answer, and variable `description`.
2. Add Auto Fill Field after the survey, select Enquiry type, and use result variable `matched_enquiry`.
3. Under Success, add Branch with condition:

```python
"enquiry_type" in matched_enquiry.fields
```

4. In that Branch's If path, send:

```text
I categorised your enquiry as {matched_enquiry.fields.enquiry_type.label}.
```

5. In Else, send `I could not identify a category from the information provided.` You can add a manual choice or handoff when those downstream actions are appropriate.
6. Under the Auto Fill action's Error path, send `Could you tell me more about your enquiry?` or another suitable fallback.
7. Restart the tester and answer `My mobile banking transfer failed yesterday.`

A matching provider response assigns the `mobile_banking` option, displays the configured Success message, and shows the value in the tester's **Conversation fields** inspector. The model must be connected for this live test; classification accuracy depends on the conversation and option descriptions.

For routing by the saved chat field later, use:

```python
"enquiry_type" in system.custom_fields and system.custom_fields.enquiry_type.value == "mobile_banking"
```

`system.custom_fields` represents the chat's current saved values, including defaults and earlier matches. The action's result variable includes only the matches made by that execution, so it is the appropriate place to check whether this particular classification found an option.

## Result variable and saved chat values

Example successful result:

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "fields": {
    "enquiry_type": {
      "field_id": "a-real-field-uuid",
      "value": "mobile_banking",
      "label": "Mobile banking",
      "group": "Banking"
    }
  },
  "unmatched": [],
  "error": null
}
```

An unmatched field appears by key in `unmatched`; it is absent from the result's `fields` object. A successful no-match result has `ok:true`. Defaults and existing assignments are retained for unmatched fields. A recognised option replaces the earlier value or default.

Saved chat snapshots also include the field key/name/type, source (`default` or `ai`), and assignment time. They are stored independently in PostgreSQL `agent_conversations.custom_fields`, mirrored into workflow context for expressions, and returned by `/tester/events`. Saving/reordering workflows or clearing workflow execution state does not erase those assignments. The tester trace displays assigned and unmatched counts; the inspector displays saved labels and groups.

On an ordinary processing error, the result variable has `ok:false`, empty `fields`/`unmatched`, and a short `error` code. An existing result variable is cleared before a new attempt. If even the bounded result cannot fit the existing chat-variable limits, Error runs with `variable_limit` and no new fields are assigned. A disabled action makes no model call and changes no values.

## Safety of assignments and outcomes

The model receives only the selected, active fields from this workspace, their predefined groups/options, the most recent 20 stored messages (up to 2,000 characters per stored message), the current incoming text, and any current submitted feedback/rating. Other chat variables and another workspace's fields are not included. Run classification near the relevant conversation steps when older details may fall outside this window.

The model must return a JSON assignment for every selected field. Unknown fields, unknown options, duplicate assignments/JSON keys, incomplete results, or malformed JSON follow Error. The complete response is validated before any field is changed. Definitions are checked again after the model responds; a changed/deleted field produces `fields_changed` instead of applying a stale option. User-provided text cannot add arbitrary field values or execute workflow actions.

Assignments and result-variable changes participate in the normal workflow transaction. A later failing action rolls back that uncommitted turn. Chat closure and accepted feedback remain durable before their post-conversation automation, following the existing lifecycle rules. Provider work is not undone by a database rollback, and no automatic retries are made.

Auto Fill shares the existing per-event processing budget (three combined LLM Processing/Auto Fill requests) and per-user model request quota. The configured provider's response/context limits also apply. Common error codes are `provider_unavailable`, `llm_disabled`, `fields_unavailable`, `fields_changed`, `invalid_response`, `provider_error`, `provider_rate_limit`, `timeout`, `context_too_large`, `processing_limit`, `request_limit`, and `variable_limit`.

The action is allowed beneath Chat Closed and after Collect Feedback submission. Its Success/Error paths and Jump destinations follow the existing post-close restrictions: ordinary Send message actions cannot run there. Use Set Variable or Send API to process post-close classification results.

## Ticket conversion

Chat values are persisted as self-contained snapshots, and `app.custom_fields.service.ticket_field_snapshot(conversation)` returns an independent deep copy for ticket creation. This preserves field IDs, keys, option values, labels, groups, and assignment metadata, including historical values after a field is archived.

**Create Ticket is now Ready.** Auto Fill itself does not create a ticket; add Create Ticket later in the workflow to copy the assigned fields. Explicit ticket overrides take priority in the copy without changing the chat. See [CREATE_TICKET.md](CREATE_TICKET.md).


Create Ticket now uses these durable conversation assignments. Explicit overrides in that action take priority in the ticket without changing the chat. See [CREATE_TICKET.md](CREATE_TICKET.md).

AUTO_TEAM_MATCH.title: Auto Team Match
AUTO_TEAM_MATCH.content:
# Auto Team Match

Auto Team Match is Ready in **Add action → AI & data**. It identifies one support team using its configured name and alternative names, saves the result in a chat variable, and follows Match found, No match, or Error. It works in ordinary workflows and under Chat Closed.

First configure teams in **Settings → Workspace → Teams**. See [Teams settings](TEAMS.md). Team matching is local and deterministic; it makes no LLM or external API request and needs no Groq key.

## Configure the action

| Setting | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Input text | Plain text, a sentence, or a variable such as `{financial_institution}`. Up to 16,000 characters after substitution. |
| Script | Optional safe Python expression returning text. For an Ask survey answer, use `financial_institution.text`. Expression source is limited to 2,000 characters. |
| Save output into variable | A custom variable such as `matched_team`: 1–64 ASCII letters, numbers, or underscores, starting with a letter. Python keywords, reserved function/system names, and `language` are rejected. |

Click **Save**, then add actions under the three outcome paths. Edits preserve path UUIDs and their existing child steps. Outcome children support normal numbering, Branch, Jump, survey waits, and post-close restrictions.

The action evaluates the input before clearing the output, so it can intentionally reuse the same variable. It does not change the active language or assign a conversation to a live queue.

## Matching rules

1. Unicode compatibility normalization, case folding, and punctuation/whitespace normalization are applied to the input, team names, and alternatives.
2. An exact normalized name match takes priority.
3. Otherwise, names must appear as complete words or phrases within the input. `BOT` matches `I need help from BOT.` but not `robot`.
4. If exactly one team is identified, Match found runs. Several alternatives for the same team still count as one team.
5. If none or multiple distinct teams are identified, No match runs. Spelling guesses and fuzzy matching are not used; add expected variations as alternative names.

Only active teams in the agent's workspace are considered. Teams are read once per event and refreshed on the next event, so saved changes apply to subsequent chat turns. Deleting a team excludes it from future lookups. Previously saved result snapshots retain their original ID/name until the action runs again.

## Output and outcomes

On **Match found**, the variable stores the team directly:

```json
{"id":"b6f7eeba-d6c7-4e97-b46e-081e270116ae","name":"Bank of Tanzania"}
```

Use `{matched_team.name}` in Send message, or `matched_team.id` in a Python expression. Do not print the whole object when only the displayed team name is needed.

On **No match**, the variable is `None` in scripts / `null` in JSON. Empty resolved text also follows No match. The tester trace distinguishes `no_match` from `ambiguous`.

On **Error**, the previous result is cleared to `None`. Missing variables, invalid/non-text expression results, oversized resolved input, unavailable Teams storage, or insufficient variable capacity follow Error. Trace error codes are `invalid_input`, `teams_unavailable`, or `variable_limit`. As with other actions, if no new variable can fit the existing 100-variable/64 KiB budget, the action follows Error without performing a lookup. No result wrapper or conversation assignment is implied.

## Test flow

Create these teams:

| Team | Alternative names, one per line |
| --- | --- |
| Bank of Tanzania | `BOT`, `Benki Kuu ya Tanzania` |
| NMB Bank | `NMB` |

Then configure:

```yaml
Chat started:
  Ask survey:
    Question: "Which financial institution do you use?"
    Answer must be: Text
    Chat variable name: financial_institution
    Next:
      Auto Team Match:
        Input text: "{financial_institution}"
        Script: Off
        Save output into variable: matched_team
        Match found:
          Send message: "Your support team is {matched_team.name}."
        No match:
          Send message: "Please provide one financial institution's name."
        Error:
          Send message: "We could not identify the appropriate team. Please try again."
```

| Survey reply | Expected result |
| --- | --- |
| `bot` | Match found; Bank of Tanzania ID/name saved |
| `I use NMB.` | Match found; NMB Bank ID/name saved |
| `Unknown institution` | No match; output null |
| `BOT and NMB` | No match; ambiguous; output null |

To test Error, temporarily set Script on and Input text to `missing_variable.text`; the Error message should run. Restore the input afterward. Script mode `financial_institution.text` produces the same result as the template above.

Live Agent Handoff is now **Ready**. In its Specific assignment mode, enter `matched_team` in **Team from chat variable** to use this result. The matched team must have members configured and satisfy the handoff availability/language settings. See [LIVE_AGENT_HANDOFF.md](LIVE_AGENT_HANDOFF.md).

## Upgrade

Copy the updated source into your existing project, keep your environment files, and apply the current migrations from backend. Auto Team Match introduced **0010**; the current Inbox/handoff release adds **0011**:

```powershell
cd C:\Users\Admin\petrix-ai\backend
python -m alembic upgrade head
python -m alembic current
```

The last command should show `0012 (head)`. Restart the backend and frontend, then reload. Existing accounts, unlimited AI agent creation/import, workflows, numbers, chat variables, custom fields, and attachments are retained. No runtime dependency or environment-variable change is required.

BRANCH.title: Petrix AI — Branch
BRANCH.content:
# Petrix AI — Branch

Version `0.6.0` adds Branch to **Flow control**. It evaluates ordered Python expressions against the current chat data and runs the first matching path. If every condition is false, it runs Else. The Branch action itself sends no message.

## Configure a Branch

1. Open your agent's **Workflows**, choose a workflow, and select **Add action → Branch**.
2. Name the action. Give the first **If** condition a name and a Python expression.
3. Use **Add condition** for additional **Else if** paths. A Branch accepts 1–10 conditions, plus one permanent Else path. The arrows change evaluation order; the delete control removes a condition and its nested steps.
4. Select **Save**. The workflow tree displays each condition and Else separately. Add actions or nested triggers under the appropriate path.
5. Restart the tester and supply the data the conditions need. **Last execution** shows the chosen path.

Names are up to 100 characters; expressions are up to 2,000 characters. Empty names, empty expressions, invalid Python, and unsupported operations are rejected on save. A rejected save retains the draft. Deleting a populated condition asks for confirmation. A referenced Jump destination must be updated or removed before its path can be deleted.

## Variables and expressions

Use existing variables without curly brackets. Comparisons are case-sensitive unless you normalize the text explicitly.

| Source | Condition example |
| --- | --- |
| Ask survey · Text | `complaint_status.text == "resolved"` |
| Ask survey · Number | `score.norm.value >= 5` |
| Set variable | `customer_status == "active"` |
| Send API response | `api_response.body.customer.tier == "gold"` |
| A JSON object stored with Set variable | `customer.tier == "gold"` |
| Extracted intent entity | `system.intent.entities.get("city") == "Nairobi"` |
| Optional or skipped answer | `score is not None and score.norm.value >= 5` |
| Variable that may not exist | `variables.get("customer_status") == "active"` |

Survey answers continue to be stored as plain text, numbers, file objects/lists, or `None`. The expression interpreter supplies read-only `.text` and `.norm.value` views for text and number values, including answers collected before this update. Existing expressions such as `score >= 5` and message placeholders such as `{score}` keep working. These scalar views also work with values assigned by Set variable; using the bare name remains supported.

Public dotted fields resolve JSON object keys only. Use `object["key"]` or `.get("key", default)` for keys that are not Python identifiers or need a default. The interpreter never reads Python object attributes. Private attributes, imports, assignments, loops, arbitrary function calls, filesystem access, and networking remain unavailable. The same bounded Python expression interpreter is shared with Set variable; see [SET_VARIABLE.md](SET_VARIABLE.md).

Conditions follow Python truthiness. Evaluation stops at the first truthy result; later conditions are not evaluated. Use `and`, `or`, and `not` for combined checks. A missing variable, invalid type, or other evaluation error returns a useful step/condition error and rolls back that turn's messages, survey answers, and variable writes. An error does not silently take Else. Previously committed turns remain intact.

## Complaint example

After Ask survey collects a text answer into `complaint_status`, add:

| Path | Expression | Action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| If · Resolved | `complaint_status.text == "resolved"` | Send message: `Good news – this has been resolved.` |
| Else | — | Send message: `Your complaint needs further review.` |

Add shared follow-up actions after the Branch row. After the selected path finishes, those actions run once. Live agent handoff remains a reserved catalogue action; this update implements Branch and does not simulate an external transfer.

## Execution and Jump

- Only the selected path runs. An empty selected path continues immediately to the action after Branch. Disabling Branch skips all its paths.
- A nested Branch works inside any condition or Else path. Each path can have its own nested trigger alternatives and fallback.
- Ask survey pauses within the selected path. Its final answer resumes that path and then the enclosing actions. Nested triggers likewise wait for the next matching event.
- Jump can target Branch itself or any saved trigger/action inside its paths. Jump to Branch evaluates its conditions. Jump directly to a contained step starts there without evaluating the enclosing conditions, continues within that destination path, and then runs its enclosing continuations. Other paths are not entered.
- Jump away from a path abandons its remaining actions. Existing loop protection still applies.
- Workflow edits clear obsolete waiting continuations on the next event. Restart creates a new conversation with fresh variables.

Existing limits of 12 nested levels, 500 workflow steps per agent, and 1 MiB per definition apply across all condition and Else paths. Path containers do not have step numbers or act as Jump destinations; the triggers and actions inside them receive ordinary permanent numbers. Renaming/reordering conditions preserves their contained steps and numbers.

## API storage

Use the existing revision-checked `POST /api/workspaces/{workspace_id}/agents/{agent_id}/workflows` endpoint. A Branch node has `kind: "action"`, `type: "branch"`, empty `children`, and:

```json
{
  "config": {
    "conditions": [
      {"id": "10c81b74-edbe-43f1-b5a6-aeaf6240762b", "name": "Resolved", "chat_script": "complaint_status.text == \"resolved\""}
    ],
    "else_path_id": "2de0e86a-e4c8-411b-bca7-e8c51705798e"
  },
  "paths": [
    {"id": "10c81b74-edbe-43f1-b5a6-aeaf6240762b", "children": []},
    {"id": "2de0e86a-e4c8-411b-bca7-e8c51705798e", "children": []}
  ]
}
```

Generate unique UUIDs for nodes and path containers. Each condition and Else must have exactly one matching path. The server canonicalizes paths into condition order followed by Else and validates every contained step, reference, and number. Other node types retain their existing shape. Tester trace entries use `outcome: "branched"`, `path_id`, and `condition_name`, alongside the Branch's `node_id` and `node_number`.

## Apply the source update

Keep your existing `backend/.env`, virtual environment, database, and `node_modules`. Copy the updated source and restart FastAPI and Angular. Branch introduces no dependency or migration; schema head remains `0005`. If upgrading from before Ask survey, first run `python -m alembic upgrade head` from `backend` as described in [WORKFLOWS.md](WORKFLOWS.md).

CHAT_CLOSED.title: Chat Closed and Collect Feedback
CHAT_CLOSED.content:
# Chat Closed and Collect Feedback

Use the permanent **Chat Closed** trigger together with **Collect Feedback** to gather a rating, survey answers, or both after a conversation ends. Submitted values are saved in chat variables before the following actions run.

Add the Ready **Close chat** action to an ordinary workflow to close automatically and invoke Chat Closed. The tester also exposes **Test an event → Chat closed (live-agent event) → Run event** to simulate a live agent closing the chat. Inbox live-agent claim/reply/close is now implemented; published-channel delivery remains a later milestone. Chat timeout is a separate event and does not invoke Chat Closed unless its workflow explicitly runs Close chat. See [CLOSE_CHAT.md](CLOSE_CHAT.md).

## Permanent trigger and available actions

Chat Closed is always enabled, top-level only, and cannot be deleted, disabled, duplicated, or nested. Open **AI agents → Workflows → Chat closed → Add action** to configure its actions.

| Allowed action | Availability |
| --- | --- |
| Collect Feedback | Ready; rating, survey, or both |
| Create Ticket | Later |
| Jump | Ready; automatic post-conversation destinations only |
| Branch | Ready |
| Set Variable | Ready |
| Switch Language | Ready |
| Send API | Ready |
| LLM Processing | Ready |
| Auto Fill Field | Ready |
| Auto Team Match | Ready; workspace team names and alternatives |
| SQL Query | Ready |
| Send Graph | Ready; chart message with table/CSV/PNG controls |
| Close Chat | Ready; continues without closing again when already closed |

Send message, Send attachment, Show carousel, Ask survey, and incoming triggers cannot be placed under Chat Closed. The policy covers every descendant, disabled step, Branch path, and API/SQL/LLM/Auto Fill/Auto Team Match outcome. Jump destinations are checked through their descendants, following siblings, enclosing continuations, all outcome paths, and chained Jumps. The picker explains unavailable destinations, and the backend enforces the same rules. Normal conversations cannot Jump into Chat Closed steps.

Collect Feedback uses a dedicated feedback form while the chat stays closed. Its own questions and configured submission confirmation are part of feedback collection; they do not enable ordinary chat replies or incoming workflow waits.

## Complete rating and optional-comment example

Add **Flow control → Collect feedback**, then fill its tabs:

| Tab | Setting | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Rating | Enable rating | On |
| Rating | Webchat rating title | `How did we do?` |
| Rating | Rating request message | `How would you rate your conversation?` |
| Rating | Set chat variable | `feedback_rating` |
| Survey | Enable survey | On |
| Survey | Question | `Any other comments?` |
| Survey | Required field | Off |
| Survey | Reply type | Open response |
| Survey | Webchat field placeholder | `Please share your comments` |
| Survey | Create variable | `feedback_comment` |
| Settings | Feedback submission text | `Thank you for your feedback!` |

Save, restart the tester, and run **Chat closed**. Select a rating, optionally enter a comment, and press **Submit feedback**. The chat remains Closed. The result contains an integer `feedback_rating` and a text `feedback_comment` (or `None` when the optional comment is blank).

To route the submitted result, add a **Branch after Collect Feedback** with condition `feedback_rating >= 4`. Its If and Else paths can contain data actions such as Set Variable or Send API:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Chat Closed"] --> B["Collect Feedback"]
    B --> C{"feedback_rating >= 4"}
    C -->|Yes| D["Log positive feedback"]
    C -->|No| E["Record a follow-up request"]
```

A Send API action after feedback can use Python payload `{"rating": feedback_rating, "comment": feedback_comment}`. Configure your own HTTPS endpoint and authentication. No business service is bundled with this example.

## Execution order

Actions before Collect Feedback run when closure occurs. Collect Feedback issues a form and pauses its children and remaining workflow actions. A successful submission stores the rating/answers, then resumes those children and following steps in order, including Branch/API/SQL/Jump continuations. Multiple Collect Feedback actions issue only one request per conversation; later ones are skipped after submission.

Place a closure log or API call **before Collect Feedback** when it must run even if the customer never submits feedback. Put actions that need the collected variables **after it**. This is a behavior change from the rating-only 0.12.0 implementation, which continued immediately.

The optional, existing **Collect feedback trigger** remains a separate receiving event. It runs once after the resumed post-close actions complete and can process the saved answers. The action and trigger share `type:"collect_feedback"` and are distinguished by `kind`. A separate receiving trigger is unnecessary for the standard example: configure the acknowledgement in **Settings**, and put data actions after the Collect Feedback action. Without a receiving trigger, no generic fallback runs.

## Lifecycle and compatibility

Closure is committed before automation, cancels active surveys/waits, and disables normal messages and old quick replies. Both workflow and older direct-model tester endpoints reject further ordinary messages. Issued feedback has a conversation-owned, one-use token. Invalid submissions preserve the token and do not partially store the rating or answers. Accepted feedback is committed before its subsequent automation; a later failure leaves the chat closed and the answers saved, reports `automation_error`, and does not permit another submission. External side effects cannot be undone and are not automatically retried.

The issued form snapshots its questions, language, variable names, and remaining workflow position. If the workflow changes before submission, the original answers are still accepted and saved; the stale continuation is stopped with a visible diagnostic. Existing 0.12.0 pending rating requests are accepted without replaying actions that previously ran. Older conversational steps under Chat Closed must be removed or relocated before saving.

State remains in PostgreSQL `agent_conversations.workflow_state`, including close time/actor/source, the pending form and private continuation, submitted variables, rating, confirmation, and automation status. Tester closures record `close_source:"tester"`. No migration or dependency is added; **schema head remains 0007**. Preserve `.env` and the database, replace source, and restart backend/frontend. Older installations still need their existing migrations applied from backend with `python -m alembic upgrade head`.

See [COLLECT_FEEDBACK.md](COLLECT_FEEDBACK.md) for all fields, localisation, channel previews, limits, and survey-only configuration; see [API.md](API.md) for the client contract. Reporting screens, Livechats, published channels, and billing are separate milestones.

Send Graph can send a chart while the conversation remains closed. Its table and download controls remain available in the tester after closure. Invalid post-close chart data follows the existing automation-failure behavior; closure and previously accepted feedback are retained. See [SEND_GRAPH.md](SEND_GRAPH.md).

With Live Agent Handoff, an Inbox close fires this trigger before the original handoff follow-up. Collect Feedback waits for submission before the conversation returns to AI. The human live-chat record remains Closed while AI follow-up messages/surveys use the same conversation. See [LIVE_AGENT_HANDOFF.md](LIVE_AGENT_HANDOFF.md).

CLOSE_CHAT.title: Close Chat — version 0.14.0
CLOSE_CHAT.content:
# Close Chat — version 0.14.0

**Close chat** is Ready under **Add action → Flow control**. It closes an open conversation and runs the permanent Chat Closed workflow. There are no action-specific settings: enter an optional name/description, leave Enabled on, and Save.

## Example: end the chat and collect feedback

1. Under a Message received trigger such as `done`, add Send message with `Thank you for contacting us. Goodbye!`.
2. Add **Close chat** after that message and Save.
3. Open the permanent **Chat closed** workflow and add **Collect feedback**. Configure its Rating, Survey, and Settings tabs as described in [COLLECT_FEEDBACK.md](COLLECT_FEEDBACK.md).
4. Restart the Agent tester and send `done`.
5. The goodbye appears, the conversation becomes Closed, and the configured feedback form is displayed. Submit a rating/comment to save its variables and resume the actions after Collect Feedback.

The action closes the chat automatically; you do not need to run the manual Chat closed test event. It does not generate a goodbye message itself. Normal replies and old quick replies stay disabled after closure. Restart starts a new test conversation.

## Flow behavior

For an open conversation, Close chat stops the current workflow, including its own children, later siblings, and enclosing continuations. It works in ordinary workflows, Branch paths, API/SQL outcomes, after a completed survey, or as a Jump destination. A disabled Close chat skips its subtree and lets the open flow continue.

The permanent Chat Closed trigger then runs once. Its existing action restrictions and safe Jump rules still apply. Collect Feedback can pause that post-close workflow until submission. Variables collected before closure and the active language are retained.

If Close chat runs when the conversation is already closed—for example beneath Chat Closed or after feedback—it is an idempotent no-op. It traces Already closed, preserves existing feedback/closure metadata, and continues the allowed actions without firing Chat Closed again. This prevents a recursive closure loop.

## Persistence and errors

The incoming turn, earlier messages/media, current variables, and closure are committed before the Chat Closed automation runs. A later automation error leaves the chat Closed, preserves the earlier goodbye and files, and reports the failure in the tester. Changes made by that failed post-close automation are rolled back. An error before reaching Close chat retains the existing whole-turn rollback behavior and does not close the chat.

Workflow closure records `close_source:"workflow"`, the triggering user/time, and the Close chat node ID/number. The explicit tester close event continues to record `close_source:"tester"`. Repeated close events and ordinary replies are rejected after closure; they do not replay external effects. External API side effects cannot be undone automatically.

The tester supports this end-to-end lifecycle. Livechats/Inbox controls and published-channel transport remain separate milestones. This action adds no migration or dependency; **schema head remains 0007**. Preserve the existing `.env` and database, replace source, and restart backend/frontend.

COLLECT_FEEDBACK.title: Collect Feedback — Rating, Survey, and Settings
COLLECT_FEEDBACK.content:
# Collect Feedback — Rating, Survey, and Settings

Add **Collect feedback** beneath the permanent **Chat closed** trigger. Configure Rating, Survey, and Settings, choose each Content language as needed, and press Save. The current release supports the complete interaction in the authenticated Agent tester.

## Rating tab

| Setting | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Enable rating | Displays the 1–5 scale when on. Turn off to collect only survey answers. |
| Webchat rating title | Default `Please rate the conversation`; 1–500 characters while rating is enabled. A live preview displays five vector face icons. |
| Rating request message | Default `How would you rate your conversation?`; up to 4,000 characters. Used in the non-Webchat channel previews. |
| Set chat variable | Default `feedback_rating`. Stores the accepted integer 1–5 in a new or existing chat variable. The copy button copies the name. |

The Webchat preview uses keyboard-operable face choices. The Messaging buttons preview displays numeric buttons 1–5. Bitrix24 and Africa’s Talking previews use a typed number. **Channel preview** in the tester restarts a new test conversation; it does not connect or publish a channel. The response exposes the appropriate prompt/control metadata for future channel adapters.

## Survey tab

Enable survey and press **Add field**. Each field has:

| Setting | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Question | Required text, up to 1,000 characters. |
| Required field | The customer must answer when checked. Unchecked fields can be left blank and save `None`. |
| Reply type | Open response, Number, Email, Phone, or Multiple choice. |
| Webchat field placeholder | Optional translated hint, up to 200 characters. |
| Choices | Multiple choice only; 1–13 distinct options, up to 100 characters each. |
| Create variable | Stores the submitted answer in a named chat variable. The first new field defaults to `feedback_comment`. |

Up to 50 fields are supported. Expand/collapse a field from its header; use up/down buttons to reorder, or the delete icon to remove it. Reordering preserves field IDs, variable names, and all translations. Deleting removes that field’s translations too.

Open response saves trimmed text. Number saves an integer or finite decimal number. Email saves a validated, normalized email; Phone removes presentation spaces/brackets/hyphens and validates 7–15 digits with an optional `+`. Multiple choice accepts only one of the issued translated choices. Each submitted answer is limited to 4,000 characters. Invalid answers display an error, retain the form entries, and allow correction without consuming the request.

Feedback variable names must start with a letter and contain only letters, numbers, or underscores, up to 64 characters. Python keywords, interpreter functions, `language`, and reserved system names are unavailable. Rating and survey fields must use distinct names. The conversation’s existing 100-variable / 64-KB limit also applies. New answers replace existing values with the configured names.

## Settings tab

**Feedback submission text** is required while rating or survey is enabled; default `Thank you for your feedback!`, up to 4,000 characters. It is displayed after the form is accepted. It supports existing text placeholders, including newly saved values, for example `Thank you! Your rating was {feedback_rating}.`

The confirmation appears separately from ordinary chat messages, and normal chat stays closed. A failure in following workflow actions still leaves accepted answers saved. The tester shows the failure explicitly.

## Localisation

Use **Content language** to provide each configured language manually. Rating titles, request messages, survey questions, placeholders, choice labels, and submission text are translated independently. Field identity, reply type, required flag, variable names, ordering, and feature toggles are shared across languages.

Rating/request/confirmation text uses active-language, agent-default, then first configured language fallback. Each survey field follows that same fallback independently, so a missing question translation can use its default-language version without changing its ID or stored variable. Viewing an unconfigured language creates no translation; editing text creates one. Every configured language needs submission text and, when rating is enabled, both rating prompts. Each active survey field needs a question in at least one language. Choice fields need choices in each provided question translation.

Questions, prompts, placeholders, and choices can use already-collected chat variables. Submission text resolves after feedback is stored and can use the new answers. Text is rendered safely as text. Workflow actions do not translate content automatically. Legacy 0.12.0 rating configurations gain default request/confirmation text; translate those defaults for your supported languages.

## Two flows to test

For a rating and optional comment, use the complete configuration in [CHAT_CLOSED.md](CHAT_CLOSED.md), then add a Branch condition `feedback_rating >= 4`. Add a Ready Close chat action to your ordinary workflow to invoke this automatically, or use the manual close test event. Submit 5 with `Very helpful` and check both variables and the If path. Restart and submit 2 with a comment to check Else. A duplicate submission is rejected.

For comments only, turn **Enable rating** off and **Enable survey** on. Create a required Open response question `What could we improve?`, placeholder `Share your suggestions`, variable `feedback_comment`, and submission text `Thank you. Your suggestion has been recorded.` After Collect Feedback, add Set Variable with name `comment_copy` and Chat script `feedback_comment`. Close the tester and submit a comment: both variables contain it, and no rating is requested or required. Leaving the required answer blank prevents submission.

Turning both features off preserves their settings and executes no feedback request; the workflow continues immediately. Disabling the action skips it entirely. No unsolicited feedback is accepted for either case. Once an enabled form is issued, its one-use token and question snapshot remain valid for that conversation even if the saved configuration changes; remaining actions are not resumed against a changed workflow revision.

No new dependency or migration is needed. Schema head remains **0007**. Live channel transport, inbox/live-agent controls, and analytics screens are later features; all channel variants above are tester previews.

CREATE_TICKET.title: Create Ticket
CREATE_TICKET.content:
# Create Ticket Version **0.22.0** makes **Add action → Handoffs → Create ticket** Ready. All 20 workflow actions now have an editor and runtime handler. This action creates a durable Petrix support case, optionally queues initial customer/assignee emails, and continues the workflow. It is also available under Chat Closed. ## Upgrade Keep your database and existing `backend/.env`. With your virtual environment active, run **from backend**: ```powershell cd C:\Users\Admin\petrix-ai\backend python -m alembic upgrade head python -m alembic current ``` The current head is **0020**. Migration 0014 originally added this workflow action; 0020 adds the human Tickets workspace. Restart backend/frontend and reload. The migration adds ticket/tag/email tables without changing existing accounts, agents, workflows, step numbers, files, custom fields, live chats, or AI/external handoffs. Existing AI agent creation/import stays unlimited. No runtime dependency or new environment variable is introduced. ## Configure the settings first Manage AI Agents permission is required to configure tags, domains, templates, and the workflow. These settings are workspace scoped. The navigation uses **Settings → Teamspace**; existing custom fields and **Settings → Workspace → Teams/Users** are reused. ### Tags Open **Settings → Teamspace → Tags**. Create named tag groups on the **Tag groups** tab, then create tags and optionally put each in a group. A tag has a name, group, and colour; a group has a name and description. Edit and Remove are available for saved rows. Create Ticket can select individual tags, whole groups, or both. A selected group expands into its current active tags when the ticket is created. Repeated selections are deduplicated. Removing a group moves its remaining tags to “No group”; removing a tag/group directly referenced by a workflow, including a disabled action, is blocked. Ticket labels are historical snapshots, so later renaming/removal does not rewrite an old ticket. ### Email domains Open **Settings → Teamspace → Email domains → Create email domain** and enter: | Field | Purpose | | --- | --- | | Domain | A bare domain you control, such as `mail.example.com`, without `https://` or a path. | | Sender display name | For example, `Customer Support`. | | Sender mailbox | The local part, such as `support`; the resulting sender is `support@mail.example.com`. | | Domain verification | Choose a CNAME ownership record or TXT ownership record. Both work independently of an email vendor. | | Enable this sender | Allows use after current ownership verification. Disabling it stops queued sends. | After Create, the domain starts **Unverified** and displays its exact DNS type, host/name, and value/destination. Copy those records to your DNS provider. Some providers append the domain automatically; avoid adding it twice. CNAME verification is convenient for mail subdomains; TXT works with root domains or subdomains.
