Use a DNS-only CNAME record, without an HTTP proxy. Click **Verify DNS records** after propagation. Only a matching live DNS response sets **Verified**. Checks are bounded and rate limited. Verification lasts 30 days; recheck after expiry or DNS changes. Changing the verification method generates a new challenge and invalidates the old verification. Changing the domain requires a new domain entry. Existing references protect a domain from removal. The challenge proves DNS control. It does **not** create a receiving mailbox, publish MX records, configure a provider account, or automatically configure SPF, DKIM, or DMARC. Configure the sender and authentication records required by your existing SMTP provider. For local installations the CNAME proof destination may end in `verify.petrix.invalid`; it is a unique ownership challenge, not a mail-routing destination. TXT verification is another option. There is no “mark verified” bypass. ### SMTP delivery Ticket emails use the same platform SMTP configuration as account emails. Your SMTP relay must permit the selected ticket From address. Keep `SMTP_FROM` for sign-in emails; ticket From addresses come from the selected Email domain. If your existing SMTP setup works and allows that sender, no new environment setting is needed. A typical provider configuration in your existing `backend/.env` is: ```dotenv SMTP_HOST=smtp.your-provider.example SMTP_PORT=587 SMTP_USERNAME=YOUR_SMTP_USERNAME SMTP_PASSWORD=YOUR_SMTP_PASSWORD SMTP_STARTTLS=true SMTP_SSL=false ``` Use your provider’s actual values. SSL and STARTTLS cannot both be enabled; production already requires encrypted SMTP. Restart the backend after configuration changes. A local Mailpit setup uses its SMTP listener, normally `localhost:1025`, and captures mail in its web inbox, normally `http://localhost:8025`. Mailpit does not deliver to real customer inboxes. Sender-domain verification still requires the displayed DNS proof. ### Email templates Open **Settings → Teamspace → Email templates → Create email template**. Enter a unique Name, optional Description, and Content. **Editor** provides basic bold, italic and list formatting; **HTML** lets you edit supported markup directly. Switching modes preserves the content. Preview displays authored content, with variable placeholders left visible. Supported content includes paragraphs, headings, emphasis, lists, block quotes, tables and HTTPS/mailto links. Scripts, embedded pages, forms, images, remote tracking and unsupported attributes/styles are removed on save. Customer values are HTML escaped before substitution and the result is sanitized again. Content must contain visible text. Templates are frozen into the initial email at ticket creation, so later template edits do not change already-queued mail. Templates support ordinary chat placeholders and these ticket values: | Placeholder | Value | | --- | --- | | `{ticket.reference}` | Stable case reference, for example `PTX-000001`. | | `{ticket.subject}` / `{ticket.description}` | Rendered ticket subject and internal description. | | `{ticket.full_name}` / `{ticket.email}` / `{ticket.phone}` | Customer identity collected by the action. | | `{ticket.assignee_name}` | Initial support member or team name. | | `{ticket.id}` / `{ticket.status}` | Ticket UUID and initial status. | | `{ticket.custom_fields.enquiry_type.label}` | A saved ticket field, including action overrides; use the actual field key. | | `{ticket.tags.0.name}` | The first saved tag when present. | Example customer template: ```html

Hello {ticket.full_name},

We logged your request as {ticket.reference}.

{ticket.subject}

Our support team will follow up.

``` Choose customer and assignee templates independently in the action. A missing template means no initial email to that recipient. Assignment to a team notifies its current workspace members individually. A team with no members still receives the ticket; an activity entry explains that its assignee email was skipped. Templates directly referenced by workflows cannot be removed. ### Custom fields and assignees Use the existing **Custom fields** settings for all supported conversation field types: Text, Number, Toggle, Dropdown, Date, and Single Select (Grouped). Auto Fill Field still supports only the grouped single-select type. Create Ticket supports all six. Every value already set on the conversation is copied, including defaults and assignments made earlier in the same workflow event. In Create Ticket, select only fields that need an override and enter a typed value or chat-variable placeholder. Number/toggle entries accept numbers/`true`/`false` or variables; dates use `YYYY-MM-DD`; select fields use configured option values. **Clear ticket value** applies an explicit null override. Overrides affect the ticket, not the chat. Static invalid overrides are rejected on save; dynamic values are checked at execution. Field deletion/type changes and option removals are protected when they would invalidate saved ticket overrides. Choose an assignee from current workspace support members or active teams. Ticket assignment does not require the assignee to be online. Configure teams/members through the existing Teams and Users settings. An open ticket assigned to a team prevents deleting that team until the ticket is reassigned or finished. ## Action settings | Setting | Behaviour | | --- | --- | | Auto-apply tags | Individual tags and/or tag groups; groups expand when creating the ticket. | | Assignee | Unassigned, a support member, or a team. | | Email sender | An enabled domain with current DNS ownership verification. Optional when neither template is selected. | | Subject | Required single-line text with chat placeholders; used for the ticket and initial email subject. | | Description | Optional internal text with placeholders. | | Full name / Email | Required customer identity, with placeholders. Email is validated after substitution. | | Phone number | Optional single-line value with placeholders. | | Customer / assignee email template | Optional, separate initial notifications. | | Custom fields | Explicit ticket-only overrides of copied conversation values. | Click **Save** after configuration. The action does not emit a chat message or close the chat. The read-only system value **`last_ticket`** becomes available to subsequent actions. For example, Send message can say `Your reference is {last_ticket.reference}.` It contains a creation-time snapshot of the ticket ID, reference, subject, status and assignee name. It is not a user-writable chat variable. ## Test flow 1: create a ticket without email This works without DNS setup or a model API key: 1. Add a Message received trigger matching `complaint`. 2. Add Ask survey with Text `What is your name?` → `full_name`, Email `What is your email?` → `email`, and Text `Please describe the issue.` → `description`. 3. Add Create ticket with Subject `Customer complaint`, Full name `{full_name}`, Email `{email}`, and Description `{description}`. Leave both notification templates unset. Optionally select a team and tags. 4. Add Send message: `We logged your complaint as {last_ticket.reference}.` 5. Start the tester, send `complaint`, and answer the questions. 6. Open **Tickets** or the tester’s **Open ticket** link. Verify the reference, customer, description, assignment and copied custom fields. Change status to In progress and add an internal note. Reload to confirm persistence. ## Test flow 2: LLM summary and initial emails 1. Configure a real sender-domain proof, permitted SMTP sender, customer receipt template and assignee template. 2. Configure a Complaints team with current members. Configure an Enquiry type grouped single-select conversation field with options such as `accounts` and `mobile_banking`; optionally set `accounts` as its default. 3. Collect `full_name`, `email`, `financial_institution` and `description` through Ask survey. 4. Add LLM Processing: Input `{description}`, system prompt `Summarise the main complaint factually. Do not add information.`, resulting variable `complaint_details`. Existing Groq settings apply. 5. Under **Success**, add Create ticket: Subject `Complaint about {financial_institution}`, Description `{complaint_details}`, customer variables, Complaints assignee, sender, both templates, and the desired tags. Select Enquiry type as an override with value `mobile_banking`. 6. Follow it with Send message: `Your complaint reference is {last_ticket.reference}.` Add suitable messages under the LLM Error and Timeout paths. 7. Run the flow. Check the ticket’s description, team, tags and custom field. The ticket should have `mobile_banking`; the original chat keeps `accounts`. Review customer/assignee delivery status and the real SMTP inbox or Mailpit capture. ## Persistence, delivery and limits References increment independently per workspace. Ticket, field/tag snapshots and email intent are saved in the same transaction as the workflow. A later error in an ordinary uncommitted turn rolls back those new rows, and no email is sent. SMTP begins only after a successful commit. A receiving AI agent creates the case in its own workspace. Create Ticket neither transfers conversation ownership nor closes the chat; Chat Closed automation remains available. A saved action/event UUID combination reuses its existing ticket receipt if that operation is retried; a genuinely new event or a different Create Ticket node can create another case. The tester preserves its client event ID when retrying the same request. Published customer-channel ingestion remains a separate feature. Email failures do not delete committed tickets. If sender verification expires or the sender is disabled after action configuration, the ticket is still created and the notification is recorded as failed. Delivery uses a durable outbox and a stable Message-ID. **Sent** means accepted by the SMTP service, not proof of inbox placement. Version 0.28.0 adds optional signed incoming-reply and delivery/bounce ingestion. It requires an operator mail adapter; see [Tickets](TICKETS.md). Each workflow response processes up to 10 queued emails. Larger queues can be sent from the ticket’s **Send queued emails** control, on later conversation events, or with the platform worker command, run from backend: ```powershell python -m app.tickets.deliver --limit 100 ``` The worker processes queued items once. It does not automatically retry failed, in-flight or uncertain mail. See [TICKETS.md](TICKETS.md) for explicit failure review and retries. Incoming replies and external mailbox synchronization remain separate work. Limits: five ticket action executions per event; up to 50 directly selected tags, 20 groups and 100 expanded tags per ticket; 100 custom-field overrides and 128 KiB of field snapshots; 200-character subjects/names, 16,000-character descriptions, 50-character phone values; 65,536-character authored templates; and up to 50 assignee email recipients plus the customer. Addresses use SMTP-compatible ASCII local parts and IDNA domains. Historical ticket fields and tags retain their original labels after later definition edits. ## API Routes use prefix `/api/workspaces/{workspace_id}`. Every route requires current workspace membership. Settings mutations and workflow editing require Manage AI Agents; mutations require CSRF. Ticket access additionally checks management, current assignment/team membership, or the creator. | Method / route | Purpose | | --- | --- | | GET `/tickets/options` | Current assignees, tags/groups, field definitions, safe sender status and template names. | | GET/POST `/ticket-settings/{kind}` | List/create `tags`, `groups`, `email-domains` or `email-templates`. | | POST `/ticket-settings/{kind}/{id}` | Full revision-checked edit, including `expected_revision`. | | POST `/ticket-settings/{kind}/{id}/delete` | Remove an unreferenced setting with `expected_revision`; retain historical snapshots. | | POST `/ticket-settings/email-domains/{id}/verify` | Real DNS check with `expected_revision`; returns updated status and DNS instructions. | | GET `/tickets?status=&q=&offset=` | Access-scoped, literal search and 50-row pages of case summaries. | | GET `/tickets/{id}` | Full ticket, 200 most recent activity items and initial notification metadata. | | POST `/tickets/{id}` | `{expected_revision,status,assignee_type,assignee_id}`. | | POST `/tickets/{id}/notes` | `{content}`; add an internal note. | | POST `/tickets/{id}/send-queued` | Attempt up to 10 queued initial notifications. | | POST `/tickets/{id}/emails/{email_id}/retry` | Revision-checked explicit retry; uncertain outcomes require `confirm_not_sent:true`. | Tester results add `last_ticket`; Create Ticket trace entries include its ID/reference. Private email bodies, execution receipts and SMTP error responses are not included in those tester results. Template/body errors are validated independently from notification transport. All referenced IDs are checked within their current workspace. Public events cannot inject a private network actor or a foreign workspace setting.

CUSTOM_FIELDS.title: Custom Fields settings
CUSTOM_FIELDS.content:
# Custom Fields settings

Open **Settings → Teamspace → Custom fields**. Conversation fields are implemented; People fields remain Later. Creating or editing a field requires **Manage AI Agents**. Workspace members can view definitions, while all changes require CSRF protection and workspace ownership checks.

The table lists the field's ID, name/stable key, type, and default value. Create, edit, delete, bulk selection/delete, and reload are supported. Changed edits increment the field revision; stale saves/deletes return HTTP 409 and retain the draft/selection. Leaving an unsaved form asks before discarding changes. Deletion archives the definition and retains saved chat snapshots.

## Types and defaults

| Type | Field Options | Default value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Text | None | Optional text, up to 4,000 characters |
| Number | None | A finite number, including zero |
| Toggle switch | None | No default, True, or False |
| Dropdown | JSON array of options | One existing option value or no default |
| Date | None | A valid `YYYY-MM-DD` date |
| Single Select (Grouped) | JSON array of named groups with options | One existing option value or no default |

Auto Fill Field supports only **Single Select (Grouped)**. The other types can hold configured defaults in conversation records; manual live-agent/ticket editing interfaces are later features.

Dropdown example:

```json
[
  {"value": "normal", "label": "Normal"},
  {"value": "priority", "label": "Priority"}
]
```

Grouped example:

```json
[
  {
    "name": "Products",
    "options": [
      {"value": "mobile", "label": "Mobile banking", "description": "Mobile app and mobile transfers"},
      {"value": "cards", "label": "Cards", "description": "Card payments, activation, or lost cards"}
    ]
  }
]
```

Each option needs `value` and `label`; `description` is optional. Each group needs a unique `name` and nonempty `options`. Option values must be unique across the entire field. Do not use an option label as a changing identifier: retain its stable `value` when renaming a label.

A workspace supports 100 active conversation fields. Names allow 100 characters, descriptions 2,000 characters, and Field Options up to 64 KiB. Grouped fields allow up to 20 groups, 100 options per group, and 200 options total; dropdowns allow 200 options. Option values allow 100 characters, labels 200, and descriptions 1,000. Defaults are checked against the selected type/options. Unknown properties and duplicate values are rejected.

## References, defaults, and saved values

A field receives a UUID and generated stable key, such as `enquiry_type`. Rename preserves both. New fields with colliding generated keys receive a unique suffix. Reopen a field to see the full ID and expression reference `system.custom_fields.enquiry_type.value`.

Defaults are applied to unset conversation fields on a workflow event; restart the tester after adding defaults to inspect a fresh chat. Zero and False are valid defaults. Existing assigned values remain unchanged when a default is edited. Auto Fill can replace a default with a recognised option. A no-match or failed classification preserves existing values.

Custom fields used by saved Auto Fill actions cannot be deleted or changed to an unsupported type, including references inside disabled actions and nested outcome paths. Remove those references first. Bulk delete validates every selected field before archiving any of them. Past chat snapshots remain intact when labels/options are edited or an unreferenced definition is archived.

Conversation values live independently of workflow revisions in `agent_conversations.custom_fields`. Their snapshots retain field identity, value, label/group, and assignment metadata for downstream processing and ticket copying. Create Ticket is implemented; live-channel field controls and People fields remain later features. See [AUTO_FILL_FIELD.md](AUTO_FILL_FIELD.md).

## API

| Method | Path | Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/api/workspaces/{workspace_id}/custom-fields` | Returns active `fields` and `can_manage`. |
| GET | `/api/workspaces/{workspace_id}/custom-fields/options` | Returns only active grouped conversation fields for the action picker. |
| POST | `/api/workspaces/{workspace_id}/custom-fields` | Creates a conversation field. |
| POST | `/api/workspaces/{workspace_id}/custom-fields/{field_id}` | Updates a field with `expected_revision`. |
| POST | `/api/workspaces/{workspace_id}/custom-fields/delete` | Archives a list of `{id, expected_revision}` entries atomically; returns 204. |

Create body:

```json
{
  "scope": "conversation",
  "type": "single_select_grouped",
  "name": "Enquiry type",
  "description": "The product or service involved in the customer enquiry.",
  "options": [
    {"name": "Banking", "options": [{"value": "mobile", "label": "Mobile banking"}]}
  ],
  "default_value": null
}
```

The other `type` values are `text`, `number`, `toggle`, `dropdown`, and `date`. API responses add `id`, `key`, `revision`, `created_at`, and `updated_at`. Keys are generated by the service and cannot be changed through update. An unchanged save preserves revision. Changed saves/archive actions create workspace audit entries without copying field options or chat content into the audit summary.

Apply migration **0009** with `python -m alembic upgrade head` from backend. No new runtime dependency is required. Existing agents remain unlimited; this feature does not restore an agent-count limit.


## Tickets

Create Ticket copies the current conversation field snapshots, including defaults and Auto Fill assignments. Its explicit field overrides affect only the new case. All six field types are supported for ticket overrides. Definitions/options referenced by these actions are protected from incompatible edits. Historical tickets retain their original values and labels. See [CREATE_TICKET.md](CREATE_TICKET.md).

## People fields and immutable types (0.24.0)

The settings page now has Conversation and People tabs. Define People fields with `scope: person`. Saved fields retain their original category and type; create a new field to change either. Record tools on Inbox, Tickets and People edit typed values and save on Enter/blur (or immediately for selections). People values are separate from Conversation values and follow individual People custom-field permissions. Both categories can be filtered and included in selected-record CSV exports. See [Teamspace settings](TEAMSPACE_SETTINGS.md).

DATABASE_CONNECTIONS.title: Database connections
DATABASE_CONNECTIONS.content:
# Database connections

Version 0.8.0 adds Settings → Teamspace → Database connections and the SQL Query action. The working connector in this release is **PostgreSQL**. All Settings sections are present; Database connections, Custom fields, Teams, and Roles & permissions are functional. Other sections remain planned.

## Upgrade

Keep your existing `backend/.env`, database, and virtual environment. From the backend directory:

```powershell
python -m pip install -r requirements.lock.txt
python -m alembic upgrade head
python -m alembic current
```

The schema should report `0006 (head)`. This migration creates `database_connections`; it does not rewrite existing workflows, step numbers, agent settings, accounts, or chat history. Restart the API and Angular using your existing commands. No Docker setup is required. cryptography, already pinned in the lock, is now a direct dependency for credential encryption; other locked versions are unchanged.

## Connect PostgreSQL

1. Open Settings from the main sidebar or profile menu.
2. Select **Teamspace → Database connections → Connect database**.
3. Enter a unique connection name, host, port, database name, username, and password. Use the hostname reachable **from the backend**, not from the browser. The default port is 5432.
4. Choose TLS mode. **Verify certificate and hostname** is the default and uses the trusted PostgreSQL root CA configured on the backend host (`~/.postgresql/root.crt`, or `%APPDATA%\postgresql\root.crt` on Windows). **Require encryption** encrypts traffic without full certificate/hostname verification. **Disabled** is available for local development.
5. Click **Connect and verify**. Petrix checks a real read-only transaction before making the connection available to workflows.

The table shows Name, Type, and Status. A failed verification remains visible with **Verification failed** so you can correct its details. Use **Edit** to change details, **Verify** to retry, and **Delete** to remove an unused connection. Editing always verifies the new settings. An empty password while editing keeps the saved password. Failed verification clears its verified status, so it disappears from the action selector and existing lookups follow Error until it is fixed.

Owners and administrators manage connections. People with Manage AI Agents permission can select verified connections in their own workspace; the options endpoint supplies only IDs, names, and types. Host details and credentials are not part of workflow documents. Up to 20 connections are supported per workspace. Names are unique without regard to case. Stale edits/deletions return 409 instead of replacing newer changes. Remove or change SQL Query actions before deleting a connection they reference.

## Read-only database account

Use a dedicated, non-administrative database account with SELECT access only to the tables or views the agent needs. Do not connect using a superuser or a role with privileged user-defined functions, extensions, filesystem access, or external database access. Petrix executes each query in a server-enforced read-only transaction and always rolls it back, validates a single SELECT, binds chat data as parameters, rejects locking/session-changing forms, and closes the connection after the operation. Custom functions still run with the privileges granted by your database; database grants remain the boundary for which data a connector may access.

For example, an administrator can provision a reader (substitute your database, schema, and secret; do this outside Petrix):

```sql
CREATE ROLE petrix_reader LOGIN PASSWORD 'replace-with-a-strong-secret';
GRANT CONNECT ON DATABASE support TO petrix_reader;
GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA public TO petrix_reader;
GRANT SELECT ON public.complaints TO petrix_reader;
ALTER ROLE petrix_reader SET default_transaction_read_only = on;
```

Grant access deliberately for each additional table/view. This example does not grant write permissions or access to every future table.

## Credential encryption

Passwords are encrypted at rest using Fernet and are never returned in API responses, options, workflow variables, or execution traces. Driver error strings are replaced by controlled error codes. Keep application database backups and the encryption key secure.

By default, the encryption key is derived from `SESSION_SIGNING_SECRET` using a separate purpose-specific derivation. Keep that secret stable or existing connector passwords cannot be decrypted. You can instead set a dedicated `DATABASE_CONNECTIONS_ENCRYPTION_KEY` in `backend/.env` **before saving your first connection**:

```powershell
python -c "from cryptography.fernet import Fernet; print(Fernet.generate_key().decode())"
```

Store that output as the environment value and restart the API. Back it up separately. Changing either the dedicated key or the fallback session secret requires re-entering existing connector passwords; this release does not automatically re-encrypt old credentials. A missing/wrong key produces a controlled credentials-unavailable error. Credentials are entered only in the Settings form; never place them in queries or workflow variables.

See [SQL_QUERY.md](SQL_QUERY.md) for configuration and a complete survey → database → Branch → Send message flow.

EXTERNAL_HANDOFF.title: External Handoff
EXTERNAL_HANDOFF.content:
# External Handoff

Version **0.20.0** makes **Add action → Handoffs → External handoff** Ready. Select **Zendesk** or **Bitrix24**, then Save. The selected workspace integration must be enabled and verified. There are no return or outcome branches on this action.

The action transfers an **existing provider conversation** using the provider's native handoff API. It does not create a Zendesk ticket as a substitute for a messaging handoff, create a new external chat, or provide a published customer channel. The current customer test surface is the Agent tester. A future channel adapter must establish the correct provider conversation link before calling this action.

## Upgrade

Keep the existing database and `backend/.env`. With your virtual environment active:

```powershell
cd C:\Users\Admin\petrix-ai\backend
python -m alembic upgrade head
python -m alembic current
```

The current head is **0014**; 0014 adds Create Ticket and its settings, and 0013 adds AI Agent Handoff. Restart backend/frontend and reload. Migration 0012 adds workspace integrations and independent provider-conversation links/transfer state. Earlier migrations 0001–0011, accounts, workflows, permanent numbers, live-chat ownership, attachments, charts, settings, and unlimited AI agent creation/import are preserved. No new runtime dependency or environment variable is required.

## Connect a platform

Open **Settings → Workspace → External integrations** with Manage AI Agents permission. Save credentials, then click **Verify connection**. Saving any edit invalidates the previous verification. Only an enabled, verified platform can be selected in the action. Disable the integration to stop new transfers; previously transferred conversations remain external.

### Zendesk

Configure:

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Portal URL | Your HTTPS `https://company.zendesk.com` origin, with no path. |
| App ID | The Zendesk Conversations / Sunshine Conversations app ID. |
| Switchboard ID | The app's configured switchboard. |
| Agent Workspace switchboard integration ID | The explicit switchboard integration whose `integrationType` is `zd:agentWorkspace`. |
| Key ID and API key secret | A Conversations API key with app/switchboard access. A regular Zendesk Support API token is a different credential. |

Verification reads the switchboard integration list and confirms the target's ID/type. Your account must have messaging/Conversations API access and a correctly configured switchboard. Handoff sends `POST /sc/v2/apps/{app_id}/conversations/{conversation_id}/passControl` with `{"switchboardIntegration":"target_id"}`. The explicit target avoids relying on a changing default escalation chain.

### Bitrix24

Configure:

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Portal URL | The HTTPS Bitrix24 portal origin, without `/rest/...`. |
| Webhook user ID | The positive numeric user ID in the incoming webhook URL. |
| Destination employee ID | The positive numeric employee ID who should receive the dialogue. |
| Webhook secret | The webhook secret alone, not its complete URL. |
| Bot client ID / bot token | The `CLIENT_ID` or `botToken` used when registering the Open Channels chatbot. |

The bot must already be registered and connected to the relevant Open Channel. Verification checks that the webhook grants both `imopenlines` and `imbot` scopes; actual chat/employee/bot eligibility is checked by Bitrix24 during the transfer. An invalid employee or bot registration can therefore still reject a transfer after connection verification.

Handoff calls `imopenlines.bot.session.transfer` with the linked numeric `CHAT_ID`, configured `USER_ID`, bot `CLIENT_ID`, and `LEAVE:"Y"`. Only an explicit successful `result:true` confirms the transfer.

Credentials are encrypted with a domain-separated key derived from `SESSION_SIGNING_SECRET`. Keep that existing secret stable; changing it requires re-entering integration credentials. API responses, traces, audit entries, and error messages do not return credentials or raw provider errors. Leave password fields blank to retain saved values. Changing the external account requires new credentials and a new conversation link.

The shared HTTPS client verifies TLS, pins DNS resolution, bounds response/time limits, and disables redirects, cookies, ambient proxies, and automatic retries. Public provider hosts work without extra configuration. A privately hosted Bitrix24 installation uses the existing explicit `SEND_API_ALLOWED_PRIVATE_HOSTS` policy; link-local/metadata addresses remain blocked.

## Test a complete flow

Use a test conversation that already exists in your helpdesk account and belongs to the customer/test case you intend to transfer. The provider read check confirms existence/access, rather than identifying which customer a manually entered ID belongs to. Do not link an unrelated customer's chat.

1. Save and verify the platform in External integrations.
2. Create a Message received trigger matching `human`.
3. Add Send message: `I'll connect you to our support team.`
4. Add External handoff and select the active platform.
5. In the Agent tester, start a fresh conversation. Expand **Link external test conversation**, select the same platform, enter its provider conversation ID, and click **Link conversation**.
6. Send `human`. The message before the action appears; the action then transfers control and closes the Petrix AI conversation.
7. Continue the actual customer conversation in the external platform's existing customer channel. The Petrix tester composer is disabled and shows the destination. Reloading retains this terminal state.
8. Open **Inbox → External** to review the history from before transfer. Reply, claim, and Close live chat controls cannot act on an external conversation.

The link check reads the existing Zendesk conversation or Bitrix24 Open Channels dialogue. Linking itself performs no transfer. A provider chat can be linked only once per external account within the workspace; links cannot be changed to another chat on the same tester conversation. Restart the tester to test a different provider conversation. Restarting creates a new local chat and does not undo an existing external transfer.

The manual test link does not copy the Petrix tester transcript to the provider or connect the tester composer to the provider's customer channel. For an integrated customer channel, the provider's existing conversation/history and customer transport must already be in place. No live Zendesk/Bitrix24 tenant credentials or end-user channel were used in release verification; controlled native API responses verify request contracts and local lifecycle behavior.

## Permanent ownership and failures

After confirmed success, Petrix AI rejects every subsequent message/lifecycle/feedback event for the same conversation. Later siblings, children, and enclosing workflow continuations do not run. **Chat Closed and Collect Feedback are not invoked**, because this is external ownership rather than closure by a Petrix live agent. Closing the external platform chat cannot resume the Petrix workflow. No webhook ingestion, provider message polling, or external-agent reply access is added.

An absent, disabled, unverified, wrong-account, or missing conversation link blocks the action without closing the chat or contacting the transfer endpoint. A provider's explicit rejection leaves the chat with Petrix AI and displays a safe failure message. Earlier customer input and AI messages are retained once; a new request may retry after correcting the platform setup.

The server commits an independent `sending` marker and preceding transcript before making the transfer request. A timeout, server failure, malformed response, or process interruption cannot safely establish ownership: AI processing stays paused, and no automatic retry occurs. Check the external platform first. In the tester, **Confirm transferred** records an observed transfer; **Confirm not transferred** restores AI processing only after you have confirmed that no external transfer occurred. A still-running `sending` request cannot be reviewed for two minutes. Reviews require the conversation owner, Manage AI Agents, CSRF, and the current revision; the decision is audited. They do not call the transfer API or execute a saved follow-up.

## API

All routes below have `/api/workspaces/{workspace_id}` as their prefix.

| Method / route | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| GET `/external-integrations/options` | Workspace platform names and active flags; no credentials or account configuration. |
| GET `/external-integrations` | Manage AI Agents reads masked integration configuration/status. |
| POST `/external-integrations/{platform}` | Save revision-checked settings; credential fields may be omitted to retain existing values. Verification resets. |
| POST `/external-integrations/{platform}/verify` | Verify with `{expected_revision}` and return safe status. |
| POST `/agents/{agent_id}/tester/conversations/{id}/external-link` | Link an owned, open AI conversation using `{platform,external_id}` after a provider read check. |
| POST `/agents/{agent_id}/tester/conversations/{id}/external-review` | Resolve an unconfirmed transfer with `{expected_revision,resolution:"transferred"|"not_transferred"}`. |

Mutations require the existing CSRF header. All identifiers are checked within the workspace/agent/owner scope. Public tester event bodies cannot provide a trusted binding or internal resume mode. A future trusted channel adapter can use the same link service; it must authenticate the provider event and establish customer/conversation ownership itself.

The tester result adds `external_handoff:{platform,name,external_id,status,error,revision,updated_at}` or null. Inbox exposes transferred/unconfirmed conversations as read-only External history to the creator, a prior Petrix assignee, or workspace users with Manage AI Agents, subject to current workspace membership. Ordinary unrelated members cannot read them. Credentials, provider raw errors, and post-transfer messages are excluded.

## Provider references

- [Zendesk Switchboard and passControl](https://developer.zendesk.com/documentation/conversations/messaging-platform/programmable-conversations/switchboard/)
- [Zendesk Conversations API authentication](https://developer.zendesk.com/documentation/conversations/getting-started/api-authentication/)
- [Bitrix24 bot session transfer](https://apidocs.bitrix24.com/api-reference/imopenlines/openlines/chat-bots/imopenlines-bot-session-transfer.html)
- [Bitrix24 Open Channels dialogue lookup](https://apidocs.bitrix24.com/api-reference/imopenlines/openlines/sessions/imopenlines-dialog-get.html)

INBOX.title: Inbox — version 0.30.0
INBOX.content:
# Inbox — version 0.30.0

Inbox combines livechats and email tickets in a permission-scoped helpdesk. Open **Inbox** in the workspace sidebar. My inbox shows active conversations assigned to you; the other default views show all permitted conversations, active livechats, active tickets, active AI chats and test conversations. AI-controlled, external and completed chats remain read-only until the existing workflow hands them to human support.

## Upgrade

Keep your existing database, virtual environment and `backend/.env`. Replace the source, then run from `backend`:

```powershell
python -m alembic upgrade head
```

Migration **0022** adds Inbox views, personal view/sort preferences, staged attachments and Copilot source training/refresh metadata. It does not rewrite existing accounts, People records, tickets, workflows or messages. Migrations 0001–0021 and dependency pins are unchanged. Restart the API and Angular. Previous agent imports, PDF Knowledge, aliases and unlimited AI agent creation/import remain available.

## Find conversations

The Inbox navigation and conversation list each scroll independently. Collapse the Inbox navigation to give the thread more space. On mobile, use **Conversation list** to return from a thread; the details tabs open over the thread.

Search message content and press Enter or Search. Searches accept at most 256 characters and treat search text literally. Internal staff notes are excluded. An active search retains its search snapshot: conversations and messages created later do not add matches until you clear or submit the search again.

Use **Views** to combine up to ten default/custom filters. All selected conditions must match. Custom views support conversation type, status, assignment, live agent, team, tag/group, language, recorded channel and priority. Save personal views under **Private views**, or shared filters under **Teamspace views**. Shared filters never expand another user's record permissions. View edits and deletions check the current revision.

Pin a view with its star button. Pinned views and sort preferences belong to your account in the current workspace and survive reloads. Sorting supports creation date, latest message, person's wait time and time since human handoff, ascending or descending. Clear sorting with the adjacent × button.

Active priority livechats appear first, above Other chats, with a crown. Their badge reflects the person's current tags/groups and the teamspace priority configuration. Assignment capacity and queue handling continue to use the existing Chat Assignment rules. The list and open threads poll every three seconds; new-conversation notifications apply only to the current view and obey personal notification preferences. Search results exclude new-conversation notifications. Assignment/status changes update the list without a page reload.

## Several conversations at once

Select a conversation to open it, then use the split button beside another conversation's avatar to add a panel. Select the split button again or close the panel to remove it. Each panel keeps a separate reply draft, internal-note draft, attachments, CC and private Copilot session. Unsaved changes have navigation guards.

The server reports the allowed panel count: Starter 1, Lite 2, Pro 3, Total/Enterprise 5. A configured billing product can override this with `limits.inbox_panels` from 1 to 5. Installations with Stripe disabled allow five. Wide layouts scroll across panels; mobile shows the focused panel. Opening multiple panels also enables the account's multi-chat preference.

## Reply and internal notes

Choose **Reply**, select an account identity or alias, compose the reply and Send. Ticket replies enter the existing email thread; livechat replies use the current channel's existing delivery path. Alias names, avatars and ticket signatures are saved with the message. Historical identities survive alias edits/deletion.

For tickets, **CC → Add** accepts comma/semicolon-separated addresses. Saved CC recipients remain for subsequent replies; clearing them explicitly removes them. The thread shows recorded queued/sent/failure/uncertain delivery states. A channel's supplied delivery failure is displayed as a failure rather than successful delivery.

If another agent owns a conversation, authorised managers can use **Takeover & Send**. Assignment and message creation happen together under the current revision, availability/capacity, transfer and plan rules. Failed validation or exhausted interaction budget leaves both assignment and messages unchanged. Replies use request IDs to avoid duplicate messages after a lost response. Polling can acknowledge a reply whose response was lost, preserving a newer draft.

**Internal Note** keeps a separate draft and adds a private staff note. Notes do not enter customer transcripts, email replies, message-content searches or Copilot conversation evidence. Existing Conversation/Person tools provide editing, deletion and note colours under their respective permissions.

Attach up to five files per reply, at most 10 MiB each and 20 MiB combined. Unsent uploads are private to the uploading agent and bound to that record; unused uploads expire after one day. Sent chat files use the existing native attachment format and authenticated delivery paths, including AI agent network delivery. AI-controlled tester attachments retain their previous owner checks; handed-off chats permit current authorised staff. Ticket files are included as MIME attachments in the prepared email. File-only replies are supported.

The editor offers emojis. Livechats also offer voice-note recording through the browser microphone on HTTPS/localhost, bounded to two minutes; review/send the resulting audio attachment. Browser/device permission is required. This release does not add continuous AI voice calling or establish new WhatsApp/Facebook transport connections. Handoff records switch voice mode off; existing external widgets must consume that state through their integration.

## Transfer and close

Current assignees can transfer a conversation to an eligible agent or selected teams. Livechat team assignment follows the saved Chat Assignment policy. Transfers/takeovers require the corresponding permission and Lite or above when billing is enabled. Closing a livechat resumes the originating AI agent's saved **Chat Closed** path; resolution still enforces configured tags/fields. Existing ticket assignment, sender and completion rules remain.

The right-side **Conversation** tab embeds the Livechat/Ticket management tools. **Person** embeds the full authorised People profile, conversation history, notes/tags and fields. **Custom** displays a permitted teamspace profile iFrame. **Copilot** contains private assistance. Embedded tools retain their own permissions and unsaved-change guards.

## Private AI assistance

**Draft Reply** asks “What should I reply?” in Copilot. **Accept** places a result into the reply editor for review; it never sends it. **Deny** dismisses the suggestion and keeps the draft. **Enhance** offers Shorten, Lengthen, Formal and Casual. **Translate** uses a selected supported language and the same review controls.

Ask Copilot questions about the conversation or enable **Mediate** for evidence, causes, sentiment, options and next steps. Mediate stays active for subsequent questions in that open panel. It requires current-conversation access. Copilot output/jobs remain private to the requesting agent and are excluded from customer conversation history.

Generation uses the administrator-configured OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Configure `SUPPORT_AI_BASE_URL`, `SUPPORT_AI_API_KEY` when required, and `SUPPORT_AI_MODEL`. The optional comma-separated `SUPPORT_AI_MODELS` allowlist adds choices to the model selector. Data is sent to that endpoint; this package does not guarantee Petrix-hosted or third-party-free processing. Missing provider configuration returns an actionable error. Requests respect weighted interaction budgets and durable job retries.

## Copilot settings and Knowledge

Open **Settings → Teamspace → Inbox co-pilot**. Manage AI Agents or the existing Manage Copilot grant permits configuration. The **Agent & data access** tab contains approved model selection, personality prompt and access controls:

| Control | Evidence available |
| --- | --- |
| Current conversation | The current permitted customer transcript; required for mediation |
| Person profile/history | Visible People fields and separately authorised previous chats/tickets |
| All authorised conversations | Broader authorised workspace conversation history |

Broader access includes current-conversation access. Neither a configuration flag nor a Copilot grant bypasses record, teamspace or People-field permissions. Linked ticket chats require their own chat permission. Private notes are excluded. Evidence and retrieval are bounded to fit the provider request.

The **Knowledge** tab is dedicated to Copilot and separate from customer-facing AI-agent Knowledge. Add a snippet, upload a file or add a URL. File uploads support PDF, CSV and JSON, plus the previous TXT/Markdown/HTML/DOCX formats, up to **5 MiB** and 200,000 readable characters. Scanned PDFs require a text layer; OCR is not added. Long source text is split into overlapping excerpts, ranked against the question/conversation and bounded for the model.

For URLs, select **URL webpage** or **All webpages**. All webpages follows public links on the same origin for up to ten pages per run, with a 60-second traversal budget and 200,000-character content limit. Public-network, redirect and robots restrictions apply. This is a bounded crawl, not a full-site guarantee. Automatic retraining supports intervals of 1–90 days. The table shows Pending, Loading, Success or Fail, timestamp and readable failure details. Only successful sources enter generation. Select sources to delete them.

Generation, deferred website training, automatic retraining and unused-upload cleanup use the existing support worker. It starts with the API when `SUPPORT_WORKER_ENABLED=true`. If running it separately, use `python -m app.teamspace.worker --watch` from `backend`; keep at least one worker active. No new package is required.

## Loading and refresh — 0.35.1

Conversations includes permitted incoming channel conversations and tester conversations, plus tickets. The Test conversations view isolates tester chats; My inbox and the active views retain their assignment/status rules. List reads batch current grants, latest public previews, channel identity and priority metadata. Only the returned page's visible People names and management controls are resolved. Full workflows and message histories remain in the conversation panel. Permission decisions are fresh for each request.

Selecting another view or search cancels the obsolete request and discards its result. Background polling waits between completed refreshes, pauses in hidden pages and keeps existing cards visible while updating. A 20-second list timeout shows a retry message; use Refresh Inbox to retry. Channel icons work for incoming Webchat/WhatsApp records in both lists and details.

INTENT_MATCHING.title: Petrix AI — Layered intent matching
INTENT_MATCHING.content:
# Petrix AI — Layered intent matching

Version `0.4.0` adds semantic embeddings and Groq intent recognition after fuzzy matching. Existing workflow UUIDs, step numbers, saved actions, and accounts are preserved. The intent-matching release itself added no database migration. The current bundle also includes Ask survey, SQL Query, and migrations through `0006`; run `python -m alembic upgrade head` from backend.

## Upgrade on Windows

Stop the backend and Angular. Copy the updated source contents into `C:\Users\Admin\petrix-ai`, preserving your `backend/.env`, virtual environment, PostgreSQL database, and Mailpit installation.

With the existing Petrix virtual environment active, run:

```powershell
cd C:\Users\Admin\petrix-ai
python -m pip install -r .\backend\requirements.lock.txt
```

Add the following settings to your existing `backend/.env`. Put your actual Groq API key in this file on your computer. The key belongs only on the backend.

```dotenv
GROQ_API_KEY=YOUR_GROQ_API_KEY
GROQ_INTENT_MODEL=openai/gpt-oss-20b
INTENT_LLM_ENABLED=true
INTENT_LLM_THRESHOLD=0.80
INTENT_LLM_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=15
INTENT_LLM_MAX_TOKENS=2048

INTENT_SEMANTIC_ENABLED=true
INTENT_SEMANTIC_THRESHOLD=0.70
INTENT_SEMANTIC_MARGIN=0.08
INTENT_FUZZY_MARGIN=0.10
EMBEDDING_PROVIDER=fastembed
EMBEDDING_MODEL=BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5
EMBEDDING_CACHE_DIR=.cache/embeddings
```

Prepare the local model once, then start the backend:

```powershell
cd C:\Users\Admin\petrix-ai\backend
python -m alembic upgrade head
python -m app.workflows.matching.prepare_embeddings
python -m uvicorn app.main:create_app --factory --reload --port 8000 --no-access-log
```

The first model download requires internet access and can take several minutes. Model files are cached on disk and excluded from source control and release archives. Chat requests load the cached model offline; they do not initiate downloads. After preparing or changing the model, restart the backend.

In the frontend terminal:

```powershell
cd C:\Users\Admin\petrix-ai\frontend
npm ci
npm start
```

Python remains `3.9.12`. The lock file pins Groq SDK `1.0.0`, FastEmbed `0.6.1`, NumPy `1.26.4`, and ONNX Runtime `1.19.2`, together with their dependencies. Use this lock file instead of installing the latest versions of these packages independently.

## Matching order

Choose **Layered intent matching** in a Message received trigger. This retains the existing API value `match_mode: "approximate"`, so previous approximate triggers automatically use the new pipeline when providers are ready.

| Stage | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| Fuzzy text | Compares normalized words and spelling against the configured examples. A candidate must meet its trigger's fuzzy threshold and lead the runner-up by `INTENT_FUZZY_MARGIN`. |
| Semantic embeddings | If fuzzy matching is inconclusive, embeds the incoming message and intent examples, normalizes the vectors, and compares cosine similarity. The best candidate must meet the semantic threshold and separation margin. |
| Groq intent recognition | If the preceding stages remain inconclusive, sends the current candidates and bounded recent conversation context to `openai/gpt-oss-20b`. Validates a structured intent result before selecting any workflow. |
| Clarification or fallback | Clarification requests and low-confidence selected intents produce a question without running workflow actions. A no-match or unavailable provider proceeds to the configured fallback at the current level, then follows the existing top-level navigation rules if no local fallback exists. |

A successful stage stops the pipeline; Groq is not called for an accepted fuzzy or semantic match. Closely competing candidates continue to the next stage. Similarity scores measure the selected metric and are not calibrated probabilities. Groq's confidence is a model estimate, with a separate acceptance threshold.

**Exact phrase matching** remains an explicit opt-out from semantic and LLM interpretation. It requires an entire normalized message to equal an example. Exact triggers with a literal match take priority. Existing deterministic ordering resolves duplicate exact matches.

Only enabled Message received triggers at the current sibling level participate. Disabled steps, exact-only candidates, actions, unrelated branches, permanent system events, and attachment triggers cannot be selected by semantic or Groq intent recognition. Language examples use the active workflow language, falling back to the agent's default language when needed.

The agent's **Large language model** switch controls the Groq intent stage and optional generative replies. Disabling it keeps exact, fuzzy, and semantic matching available. The global `INTENT_LLM_ENABLED` setting can disable Groq recognition separately.

## Configure useful intents

Use an informative name and description, then provide several representative examples. The trigger description helps Groq distinguish nearby meanings.

| Intent | Description | Example phrases |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `check_balance` | Requests the current available account balance. | Check my account balance; Show my current funds |
| `perform_transfer` | Wants to begin a transfer, rather than learn the steps. | I want to transfer money; Send funds to another account |
| `transfer_guidance` | Asks for instructions or information about making transfers. | How do I transfer money?; Explain how to send funds |

Attach your saved actions to each trigger. Intent recognition selects a configured workflow; it does not implement banking transactions or retrieve balances by itself.

The default English retrieval model was checked locally using real embeddings. With examples for balance and opening hours, “How much money do I have?” selected `check_balance` at approximately `0.7301` cosine similarity. An unrelated geography question was rejected. This is a smoke check, not a general accuracy benchmark. Test your own examples and thresholds, especially when intent meanings overlap.

The BGE default is an English model. For multilingual semantic matching, you can select a model supported by the pinned FastEmbed release, such as `sentence-transformers/paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2`, prepare it again, and recalibrate the semantic threshold using your target languages. Cosine scores differ across models; do not copy a threshold unchanged and assume equivalent behaviour.

## Structured results and session data

Groq returns an allowed intent ID or null, confidence, extracted entities, an optional context summary, and a clarification decision. The backend validates the result and checks its ID against the current candidate allow-list. Malformed, truncated, foreign-node, duplicate-entity, and out-of-range results cannot execute actions.

The tester response adds `matching`:

```json
{
  "method": "llm",
  "scope": "root",
  "node_id": "configured-trigger-uuid",
  "node_number": 12,
  "intent_name": "perform_transfer",
  "score": 0.95,
  "entities": { "amount": "500" },
  "needs_clarification": false,
  "clarification_question": null,
  "context_summary": null,
  "attempts": [],
  "warnings": []
}
```

The real `attempts` array records the stages considered, their scope, status, and best score. Open **Intent matching** in the tester to inspect the decision and provider warnings.

Entities are strings and belong to the recognition result. They do not overwrite your custom chat variables. Subsequent actions can explicitly read the result through the existing read-only `system` namespace:

```python
system["intent"]["entities"].get("amount")
```

For a Set variable action, use that expression to assign a field such as `requested_amount`. Convert its type explicitly when needed. Send message supports paths such as `{{system.intent.entities.amount}}` when the value exists. Like other message placeholders, a missing path produces a controlled action error.

The current result is stored with the conversation. A new event replaces it; use Set variable when a recognized value must survive later turns. A clarification preserves the relevant waiting branch, and recent messages include the clarification question on the next recognition request. A changed workflow revision retains the existing rule of clearing outdated nested execution state.

## Provider configuration and failures

Local embeddings use CPU inference and require no embedding API key. To use an OpenAI-compatible embedding service instead, configure its own endpoint and credentials:

```dotenv
EMBEDDING_PROVIDER=openai_compatible
EMBEDDING_BASE_URL=https://YOUR_EMBEDDING_HOST/v1
EMBEDDING_API_KEY=YOUR_EMBEDDING_API_KEY
EMBEDDING_MODEL=YOUR_EMBEDDING_MODEL
EMBEDDING_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=10
```

Set a threshold appropriate for that model. The embedding endpoint is configured independently of Groq chat recognition. Local model preparation is unnecessary for a remote provider. Production remote connections require HTTPS.

Example embeddings are cached in bounded process memory by workspace, agent, workflow revision, language, provider, model, and example content. Edited examples cannot reuse stale vectors. User-message vectors are reused only inside the current event. No vector database or new PostgreSQL extension is required for this increment.

Missing local files, an unconfigured Groq key, provider timeouts, and provider errors leave fuzzy/exact matching usable. The tester displays controlled warnings for provider failures, and unmatched requests can reach the configured fallback. Raw provider bodies, API keys, and internal exception messages are not returned to the browser. The key and model configuration are read from `backend/.env`; changing them requires a backend restart.

Groq classification and optional generative replies share `LLM_TESTER_REQUESTS_PER_MINUTE`. Each external model call consumes a request; nested and top-level classification may each require one. SDK retries are disabled. Recent context is limited to six messages of up to 1,000 characters each. Custom chat variables and the saved agent persona are not automatically sent to the intent classifier.

The optional unmatched-message generative adapter still uses `LLM_BASE_URL`, `LLM_API_KEY`, and `LLM_MODEL`. Supplying `GROQ_API_KEY` configures intent recognition; generative replies retain their separate connection settings. The reserved **LLM processing action** remains unavailable in this increment.

## Code locations

| File | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `backend/app/workflows/matching/fuzzy.py` | Normalization and the existing text-similarity score. |
| `backend/app/workflows/matching/embeddings.py` | Local/hosted embedding adapters, cosine comparison, and scoped example cache. |
| `backend/app/workflows/matching/groq_intents.py` | Groq SDK request, strict JSON schema, bounded context, and response validation. |
| `backend/app/workflows/matching/router.py` | Stage order, thresholds, ambiguity margins, candidate scope, and fallback selection. |
| `backend/app/workflows/matching/prepare_embeddings.py` | One-time model download and preparation. |
| `backend/app/workflows/runtime.py` | Executes the selected branch, handles clarification, and retains conversation continuations. |
| `backend/app/core/config.py` | `.env` configuration and provider limits. |

Groq's supported strict-output models and schema rules are documented in its [Structured Outputs guide](https://console.groq.com/docs/structured-outputs). FastEmbed model choices are documented in the [supported-model list](https://qdrant.github.io/fastembed/examples/Supported_Models/); the pinned package's `TextEmbedding.list_supported_models()` is authoritative for this installation.

JUMP.title: Jump
JUMP.content:
# Jump

Use **Jump** to redirect a conversation to an existing trigger or action in this agent's workflow tree. For example, send a complaint confirmation and then return to the same Main menu action used elsewhere.

## Configure

1. Open the source workflow and click **Add action** at the desired position.
2. Choose **Flow control → Jump**.
3. Open **Jump to**. Search by step name, `#number`, or parent workflow name.
4. Select a destination trigger or action. The selected card shows its permanent number, name, and location. Use the × button to clear it and select another.
5. Click **Save**. The source row shows `Jump to #number Name`.

Number badges identify each saved step's creation order and survive renaming and reordering. The picker lists steps across all this agent's workflows, including nested triggers and actions. Save a new destination first so it has an identity and number. Disabled destinations or destinations under disabled parents are unavailable to an enabled Jump. A Jump cannot select itself.

## Example

Create a Send message action named **Main menu**, with quick replies and nested Message received triggers for the available choices. Keep the Main menu action's saved number, for example `#12`.

In the complaint branch, add:

```yaml
Send message: "Your complaint has been logged."
Jump to: "#12 Main menu"
```

The confirmation is sent, then the existing menu message is sent and the conversation waits for its nested choice triggers. Each choice can return to that same menu again after new input.

## Execution rules

- An action destination executes that action, its children, and its following sibling steps. Earlier siblings and ancestor actions are not replayed.
- A trigger destination enters that trigger's children immediately. Its matching examples do not have to match the current input. Other sibling triggers remain alternatives.
- Destination execution keeps its enclosing action continuations, as if execution had reached that point normally. Nested triggers still wait for the next matching event.
- Jump discards the source branch's remaining stack. Children and following steps at the source Jump are not executed through that source path.
- Variables and the active language are retained. Jump itself sends no chat message.
- Jumping to a system trigger runs its configured actions. It does not synthesize a new chat-started, closed, timeout, or feedback event; the actual tester event continues to control conversation lifecycle flags.
- Running the same Jump again within one event is treated as a loop and returns a clear validation error. Waiting for new input permits returning through the same Jump in a later event. Failed events commit no partial messages or variable changes.

Update or remove incoming Jump actions before deleting their destination. Disable an incoming Jump, or its enclosing branch, before disabling its destination. The backend checks the whole submitted tree atomically and rejects missing targets and targets belonging to another agent. Runtime validation also catches damaged stored references.

## API and files

The existing revision-checked `POST /api/workspaces/{workspace_id}/agents/{agent_id}/workflows` endpoint saves the whole tree. A Jump action's settings are:

```json
{
  "target_node_id": "5f315f74-a965-40b7-b681-070571bb8925"
}
```

Use the destination's actual UUID from `GET /workflows`; the UUID above is illustrative. Names and badge numbers are display values. The backend validates the UUID and resolves it only inside the same agent's submitted tree. Normal authentication, permissions, CSRF, revision checks, and change logging apply.

Tester traces show the Jump's source number, `Jumped to #number`, and the destination's executed steps. Trigger destinations have an additional `Entered by Jump` trace entry. Raw Jump trace records include `target_node_id` and `target_node_number`.

| File | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `backend/app/workflows/actions/jump/config.py` | Required UUID target schema |
| `backend/app/workflows/actions/jump/handler.py` | Control transfer without producing a chat message |
| `backend/app/workflows/service.py` | References, availability, and deletion checks |
| `backend/app/workflows/runtime.py` | Destination stack, nested waits, and loop protection |
| `frontend/src/app/features/workflows/actions/jump/` | Searchable picker, selected card, and validation |

## Apply this update on Windows

Stop FastAPI and Angular, copy this archive's source into your current `petrix-ai` folder, and keep your existing environment files, virtual environment, database, and `node_modules`. Restart both services with your usual commands. No new Python or npm dependencies are introduced by Jump. The current bundle also includes Ask survey: run `python -m alembic upgrade head` from backend to reach `0005` before using file questions.

Test by completing a complaint, confirming that the menu reappears, and selecting another menu choice. In **Last execution**, verify that the Jump points to the saved menu number.

KNOWLEDGE.title: Agent Knowledge — 0.26.0
KNOWLEDGE.content:
# Agent Knowledge — 0.26.0

Select an AI agent and open **Knowledge**. The Sources view provides **Upload file**, **Add URL**, **Paste snippet**, name/content search, Type and Status filters, Reset all, source details, enable/disable, refresh/retry and confirmed bulk deletion. Guidance provides a saved master prompt, the complaint-extraction example and the actual moderation connection state.

This Knowledge base supplies reference passages to the configured model. Importing content does not fine-tune model weights. It is separate from Settings → Teamspace → Inbox co-pilot knowledge.

## Upgrade an existing project

Keep your existing database, `backend/.env`, signing/encryption secrets and virtual environment. From **backend**, run:

```powershell
python -m pip install -r requirements.lock.txt
python -m alembic upgrade head
python -m alembic current
```

Head is **0018**. Restart backend/frontend. The new dependency is `pypdf==6.21.4`, pinned to a release supporting Python 3.9; existing dependency pins are retained. No key or environment variable is required to import files/snippets. URL import needs outbound HTTPS/DNS. The existing LLM/Groq connection is still required for generated answers.

0018 adds source records with original-file bytes, extracted text, searchable passages, processing leases and independent reply guidance. It backfills existing snippets as ready sources without changing their IDs, content, enabled flag, legacy document revision, agent settings or workflows. Sources with the same UUID in different agents remain independent. Migrations 0001–0017 remain unchanged. Downgrading removes the new source/guidance tables; the preserved legacy snippet document remains. Back up the database before an intentional downgrade, since newly added file/URL/snippet sources are not copied into the old document.

## Sources

**Paste snippet:** enter a name and up to 20,000 characters of text. Keep Enabled selected to use it in future answers. Save builds reference passages immediately. Select the name to edit it later. Changes use revisions; a stale edit must be reloaded.

**Upload file:** select TXT, Markdown, CSV, JSON, HTML, PDF or DOCX, up to 10 MiB. Uploaded files are persisted before processing. Text files must be UTF-8 or UTF-16 with a byte-order mark; JSON must be valid. PDFs support up to 200 pages and must contain selectable text. Scans need OCR beforehand. Encrypted PDFs, old `.doc` files, images and unsupported formats are rejected or shown as failed with an explanation. DOCX macros and embedded binary objects are not processed. HTML scripts and hidden/navigation content are excluded. Documents never execute code, macros or embedded links.

Extraction runs in a separate Python process with a 20-second timeout. Linux also applies parser memory/CPU limits; Windows uses the child-process timeout and document/expansion limits. Readable text is limited to 256 KiB per source. Oversized content fails with a split-document instruction; it is not silently truncated. Failed originals remain available for authorized download or deletion.

**Add URL:** enter a name and a public HTTPS URL on port 443. The reader respects robots.txt and imports one HTML page, plain-text resource or PDF. It follows up to three page redirects, revalidating every destination and all DNS answers, with normal TLS verification. It does not follow page links, run JavaScript, sign in, use a proxy-bypass service, send ambient cookies, or access private/local/link-local/metadata networks. Redirects to those destinations are blocked too. Response and gzip expansion are bounded to 10 MiB. For websites needing JavaScript or authentication, export the intended content and upload it or paste a snippet.

Sources move through **Queued → Processing → Ready** or **Failed**. The table refreshes while work is outstanding. Select the source name to preview extracted text, see its explanation, edit its name/enabled state, change a URL, or download an original file. File text is read-only; upload a replacement file when the original changes. **Refresh source** fetches a URL again or reprocesses the saved file; **Retry processing** retries a failure. Refresh removes old passages from use until the new attempt is ready. A failed refresh does not continue serving stale text.

Disable a source to retain it without using it in future requests. Delete one source or select several and choose Delete selected; deletion requires confirmation and checks every selected revision atomically. It removes original bytes, text and passages. An in-flight import cannot recreate a deleted source. Previous conversation messages are retained.

Technical bounds are 50 sources, 2 MiB extracted text and 50 MiB of original-file bytes per agent. Import/refresh requests are limited to 20 per account per minute. These are ingestion bounds, not AI-agent creation/import limits; creating/importing AI agents remains unlimited.

## Use sources in replies and workflows

Enabled, Ready sources are retrieved only for the selected agent. Text is split into overlapping passages and ranked by query-term relevance. Up to 12 passages and approximately 24 KiB of serialized evidence are sent. When no query terms match, the first passage of each source provides bounded background context. This is lexical retrieval; an embedding service or vector database is not required. Disabled, failed, queued, processing and other-agent sources are excluded.

For ordinary generated replies, Guidance → **Use ready knowledge in generative replies** is enabled by default. Saved workflows still run first. The master prompt uses Guidance when non-empty, otherwise the existing Agent settings persona. Supported master-prompt placeholders are `{_chatbot.name}`, `{agent.name}`, `{language}` and `{current_date}` (UTC date). Conversation language remains part of the model's instructions. Evidence is supplied as separate reference data, with instructions not to follow commands embedded in source text. Model accuracy still needs evaluation with your actual content and provider.

For **LLM Processing**, enable **Use Knowledge info** on the action. A requested but empty/unready Knowledge base follows Error with `knowledge_unavailable`. The action's own System prompt remains separate from the user's Input and from the general reply master prompt. This preserves extraction/classification tasks from unrelated persona instructions.

### Complaint JSON example

Open Guidance → LLM Processing system prompt → View complaint extraction example. Copy it into the action's System prompt; use `{last_message}` or your saved survey variable as Input. `{last_message}` aliases the current incoming message when no custom variable with that name is defined. Set **Output format → JSON object** and choose a resulting variable such as `complaint_details`.

A valid response is stored as an object, so a later message can reference `{complaint_details.financial_institution}` or `{complaint_details.follow_up_question}` and a Branch can inspect those fields. Invalid JSON, markdown fences, duplicate keys, non-object output or non-finite numbers follow Error with `invalid_json_response`; the old result remains cleared. Text is the default for existing actions and continues storing the original string. JSON mode validates structure, not the truth or completeness of model-generated fields; use explicit workflow checks for required values.

The included example covers complaint description, financial institution, date, amount, transaction mode, requested action, account number/type and one follow-up question in the active language. Prompt examples are editable guidance. Exact date/phone/reference validation belongs in Survey/Branch actions when it must be enforced. The prompt does not make the server batch rapid incoming messages; message consolidation requires a channel adapter that explicitly batches them.

## Website access and Cloudflare

A website may reject this reader or return a browser challenge. That is shown as a failed source with a useful explanation. Ask the website owner to permit the intended content and reader, then retry. Use the actual outbound public IP of **your** Petrix deployment. The `20.198.250.74` value in the supplied reference is not a built-in Petrix IP; use it only if your operator verifies it is your deployment’s current outbound address.

Optionally set `KNOWLEDGE_EGRESS_IP` to display your operator-verified IP in Guidance. This setting is informational; it does not change routing or firewall rules. The reader identifies itself as `PetrixAI-Knowledge/0.26`. Website owners should keep access scoped to the intended content; imports do not change Cloudflare or bypass challenges. See [Cloudflare IP Access rules](https://developers.cloudflare.com/waf/tools/ip-access-rules/) for its current interface and rule behavior.

## Content filtering

Both generative reply entry points and LLM Processing screen model inputs and outputs. A local credential check always blocks private-key headers and recognisable secret-token patterns. It does **not** claim to detect every secret or every inappropriate use of personal information. Normal complaint names, contact details and account information are not globally rejected; their appropriate handling depends on context.

For category moderation, connect an operator-owned **OpenAI-compatible `/moderations` endpoint**:

```dotenv
MODERATION_BASE_URL=https://your-provider.example/v1
MODERATION_API_KEY=
MODERATION_MODEL=
MODERATION_REQUIRED=false
```

Use your provider's real endpoint/model and credentials. Input goes to `/moderations`; the response must contain one `results` item with boolean `flagged` and optional boolean category values. Its policy should cover sexual content, violence, hate/harassment, self-harm, terrorism/illegal activity and inappropriate PII disclosure as required by your organisation. Those category policies are supplied by the connected provider, not guessed with keyword lists.

When configured, screening is automatic and end users cannot turn it off. Rejected input is not sent to the completion provider. Rejected generated text is not stored or displayed. Ordinary generated replies return the saved content-filter fallback. LLM Processing follows Error with `content_filtered_input` or `content_filtered_output`. Provider failures/invalid verdicts fail closed: the generative endpoint returns 503, or Processing follows Error with `moderation_unavailable`. Raw rejected output and provider responses are not written into application logs.

If no endpoint is configured, Guidance explicitly shows category moderation as not connected; only the local credential check is active. Set `MODERATION_REQUIRED=true` to prevent model requests until category moderation is connected. There is no UI switch allowing a conversation participant to bypass it. Production moderation URLs require HTTPS. This integration covers generated agent replies and workflow LLM Processing; the separate Inbox co-pilot, support analysis and intent-classification services retain their existing controls.

## Worker operation and authorization

New imports are attempted after the upload response. The API's Knowledge worker also resumes queued jobs and jobs with expired two-minute leases every five seconds, independently of the support worker. If API-managed processing is disabled with `KNOWLEDGE_WORKER_ENABLED=false`, run a bounded batch from backend using your existing job runner:

```powershell
python -m app.agent_knowledge.jobs --limit 20
```

A source's actor must still have Manage AI Agents in the correct workspace/teamspace when work begins and when it publishes. Revocation prevents import completion. Concurrent workers claim one lease; stale completion cannot overwrite a newer lease or a deleted source. Automatic workers resume interrupted processing, while explicit failures wait for a user retry.

Reads require View AI Agents; changes require Manage AI Agents and CSRF. Agent/workspace isolation applies to source lists, previews, originals, policy and retrieval. Source and policy revisions prevent stale overwrites. Dirty source/guidance edits are protected when closing, switching tabs/agents/workspaces or leaving the page. API keys are server-only. Audits record operation names, not raw source text.

Legacy GET/POST `/knowledge` remains available for its original 20-source/64-KiB snippet document and revision contract. Legacy writes synchronize their migrated snippet records, without removing new files/URLs/snippets from the expanded editor. Editing/deleting a migrated source updates its preserved legacy entry too. Knowledge remains separate from settings-only agent exports/version restores; deleting an agent cascades its sources and guidance.

## API

Paths below are relative to `/api/workspaces/{workspace_id}/agents/{agent_id}/knowledge`.

| Method/path | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| GET `/sources` | Paginated list with `q`, `kind`, `status`, `page`, `per_page`; metadata/stats only. |
| GET `/sources/{id}` | Authorized detail, extracted text and source revision. |
| POST `/snippets` | UUID `id`, name, content and optional enabled. |
| POST `/urls` | UUID `id`, name, HTTPS `url` and optional enabled; queues work. |
| POST `/files` | Multipart UUID `id`, optional name and `file`; queues saved bytes. |
| POST `/sources/{id}` | `expected_revision`, name, enabled and optional snippet content or URL. |
| POST `/sources/{id}/refresh` | `expected_revision`; queues refresh/retry. |
| POST `/sources-delete` | `ids` and matching `revisions` map; atomic deletion. |
| GET `/sources/{id}/download` | Original file as attachment with current read authorization. |
| GET `/guidance` | Policy, examples and actual moderation/egress configuration status. |
| POST `/guidance` | Full policy with expected_revision, master_prompt, use_for_replies and fallback_message. |

Provider/parser reference: [pypdf 6.21.4](https://pypi.org/project/pypdf/6.21.4/) declares Python ≥3.9 support. Existing runtime pins are retained alongside this one addition.

LIVECHATS.title: Workspace Livechats
LIVECHATS.content:
# Workspace Livechats

Version **0.27.0** gives **Workspace → Livechats** its own repository at `/app/livechats`. Inbox remains the working queue and reply editor. The list contains actual conversations that have reached Live Agent Handoff (`pending`, `active`, or `closed` runtime state); ordinary AI tester chats and external-only transfers are excluded. No sample customer records are added to your installation.

## Upgrade

Copy the updated source over your project, retain your `.env`, virtual environment and database, then run from `backend`:

```powershell
python -m alembic upgrade head
python -m uvicorn app.main:create_app --factory --reload --port 8000
```

Restart Angular from `frontend` using `npm start`. New migration **0019** adds a livechat description/display-status column and private note storage. Migrations 0001–0018 remain unchanged. Existing handoff state, priority, assignments, conversation IDs, messages, workflow numbers and Knowledge/PDF imports are retained. No runtime dependency or environment variable is added. AI-agent creation and import remain unlimited.

## List, search and filters

The table shows stable livechat IDs, person, assigned live agent, teams, effective tags/groups, display status and creation time. Priority conversations carry a crown. Pagination supports 20, 40 or 100 records per page and counts only records allowed by the current role/teamspace scope. Horizontal scrolling stays inside the table.

Search accepts at most **256 characters** and matches livechat ID, person name, email and phone, without interpreting `%` or `_` as wildcards. Filter by live agent, team, grouped single-select custom-field value, tag, tag group, status, created date, CSAT score, primary language and used languages. Filters combine with AND.
