Tag-group matching includes a direct tag's current group memberships and explicitly applied groups. Archived labels are excluded.

Dates support Today, This week, This month and inclusive custom start/end dates in the browser's IANA timezone. Primary language is the language at the first handoff; used languages retain the primary and subsequent saved conversation languages. Rating None means no submitted CSAT, not a zero rating.

## Details in Livechats and Inbox

Select a livechat to open its details. The same five tabs appear under the collapsible Livechat details panel in Inbox:

| Tab | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Assignment | Current agent, selected/default alias, teams and person. Authorized operators can transfer to an available eligible agent or to teams. Team routing respects availability, language, capacity and saved assignment policy. |
| Details | Static ID, channel, editable description, status, created time, CSAT and languages. The Livechats panel includes paginated read-only message history. Reply through Open in Inbox when the record is in your queue. |
| Priority | Frozen classification and queue/assignment-limit behavior from handoff. Transfers and later tag/policy changes do not reclassify the same livechat. |
| AI Analysis | Latest authorized summary/sentiment and Refresh analysis, using the existing durable analysis jobs and interaction limits. |
| Notes & Tags | Add/edit/delete up to 100 internal notes, select their colours, and manage existing tags/groups/custom fields according to permissions. |

Notes are staff-only records. They are never placed in customer messages, tester results, conversation state, model conversation transcripts, or exported customer transcripts. Note edits and deletion check their own revision. Description/status/assignment edits and bulk deletion check current livechat revisions. Unsaved drafts are guarded when leaving the panel or switching conversations.

### Status and completion

Open corresponds to an assigned active conversation. Pending can mean an unassigned queue entry or an assigned conversation waiting for follow-up; Overdue is a manual management flag in this release. Marking your assigned active livechat Resolved or Closed calls the existing closure engine, including mandatory-tag checks, Chat Closed, feedback, AI resumption and auto-analysis. It does not bypass workflow execution. Pending chats must first be assigned/claimed; an operator must transfer/take ownership before completing another agent's active chat. Closed and Resolved are completed states; a new human handoff is required to reopen support.

Ticket automatic-overdue settings continue to apply to tickets. This release does not invent an automatic livechat-overdue deadline.

### AI Analysis

Enable Chats analysis and Manual analysis in Settings → Teamspace → AI analysis. The existing support AI configuration (`SUPPORT_AI_BASE_URL`, `SUPPORT_AI_MODEL`, optional API key) is required for real analysis. This is the support-analysis connection, separate from the workflow's Groq intent/LLM Processing connection. If the normal background worker is disabled, process durable work with:

```powershell
python -m app.teamspace.worker
```

Unconfigured providers, disabled analysis, unavailable interactions and plan/permission restrictions produce explicit errors. No fabricated analysis is displayed.

## Export and delete

Select records to add tags, export selected fields and optional conversation transcripts, or delete livechats. Exports use the existing plan checks, durable CSV jobs, IANA timezone, formula-safe cells and Settings → Teamspace → Exports download history. Export and download grants remain separate; current access is checked when exporting, generating and downloading. Emailing a copy is opt-in.

Deletion requires Manage access to every selected record, all current revisions, and explicit confirmation. It removes selected conversations, transcripts, local conversation attachments, notes, label bindings and alias selections. Linked People and tickets remain; tickets lose only their conversation link. Cached analysis/co-pilot output and chat exports containing deleted records are invalidated. Existing remote-channel messages are not deleted from a provider.

Consumed message interactions are retained as text-free usage events, including de-duplication of transferred message copies. Deleting a conversation does not refund its past consumption. Opening the repository does not itself consume an AI interaction.

## Permissions

Existing `view/manage/export/download_livechats_{all,teams,own}` and `transfer_livechats` grants are enforced on the server, together with current workspace membership and allowed teamspaces. View permission does not grant mutation or export. Knowing an ID, owning the original AI tester session or holding unrelated AI-agent permission does not grant access to a human-support record. Inbox eligibility and ownership remain required to send replies; the repository is not a way to bypass them.

LIVE_AGENT_HANDOFF.title: Live Agent Handoff
LIVE_AGENT_HANDOFF.content:
# Live Agent Handoff

Version **0.19.0** makes **Add action → Handoffs → Live agent handoff** Ready and adds a working [Inbox](INBOX.md). A handoff uses the current conversation: the support agent sees its earlier AI messages, customer replies, attachments, and charts. While it is pending or active, new customer messages go to live support and the AI workflow stays paused.

## Upgrade

Keep your existing database, environment files, and virtual environment. Replace the source and run these commands with your virtual environment active:

```powershell
cd C:\Users\Admin\petrix-ai\backend
python -m alembic upgrade head
python -m alembic current
```

The last command should show **0015 (head)** in the current release; 0015 adds Workspace settings, and 0014 adds tickets/email settings and 0013 adds AI-agent handoff and 0012 adds external handoff settings. Restart backend/frontend and reload. Migration 0011 adds live-chat ownership, support profiles, team members, assignment settings, and a selected workspace per login session. Existing accounts, sessions, agent creation/import without limits, workflows, numbers, conversations, custom fields, aliases, media, and charts are retained. Existing teams start with no members and assignment defaults to Manual claim with a limit of five active chats per agent. No dependency or new environment variable is required.

## Prepare live support

1. Have each colleague create a Petrix AI account and finish account/workspace setup.
2. As a workspace owner or administrator, open **Settings → Workspace → Users**. Add the colleague's existing account email. This adds a Member to the workspace; it does not send an email invitation.
3. Open **Settings → Workspace → Teams**, create or edit the support team, and select its members. This is the existing Teams settings section; the general/teamspace wording in some reference material refers to this section in Petrix.
4. Each colleague signs in and opens **Inbox**. If they belong to several workspaces, they select the shared workspace in the Inbox workspace selector. The choice is saved for that login session.
5. The colleague chooses their supported languages, enables **Available to receive chats**, and clicks **Save availability**. A team membership, valid signed-in session, and recent Inbox heartbeat are required for online availability.
6. In **Settings → Teamspace → Chat assignment**, choose a distribution method and active-chat limit.

You can test with one account by adding yourself to a team and becoming available in Inbox. For a realistic test, use separate browser profiles or an incognito window for the customer/tester account and support account. Ordinary Members can use Inbox and their own availability controls without Manage AI Agents permission. Creating workflows, editing teams, and changing assignment settings require Manage AI Agents. Adding workspace members requires an owner or administrator.

## Action settings

| Setting | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Live agent availability check | When enabled, the handoff proceeds only if an eligible agent is online and below the active-chat limit. Otherwise the unavailable path runs. |
| Assign to all live agents | All support agents in the current workspace/teamspace are candidates. They must belong to at least one active support team. |
| Assign to specific live agents or teams | The union of selected agents and members of selected teams. Select up to 50 agents and 20 teams. |
| Team from chat variable | Optional in Specific mode. Enter a variable name such as `matched_team`, without curly brackets. It must contain a team ID or the direct `{id,name}` result of Auto Team Match. Only an active team in the same workspace is accepted. A missing/invalid team variable follows the unavailable path. |
| Assign by language | Further restricts candidates to support agents whose profile includes the AI agent's active language at the moment of handoff. |

The availability switch defaults off, as in the reference screenshot. With the check **off**, eligible offline or busy agents can still receive a **pending** queue entry. They must become available and have capacity before claiming it. If no eligible support agent is configured at all, the handoff does not proceed. The check on/off does not bypass team, language, workspace, or conversation ownership restrictions.

Specific teams must exist before saving the action. Static team/member references are validated against this workspace. All mode clears unused selections. A dynamic team's display name is not trusted for routing: its ID is validated. If a dynamic team variable is configured, it must resolve correctly even when additional static targets are selected.

## Assignment rules

| Mode | Behavior at handoff |
| --- | --- |
| Manual claim | Create a pending conversation visible to eligible support agents. The first successful claimant owns it. |
| Round robin | Choose an online eligible agent with capacity who has waited longest since their last assignment. |
| Least busy | Choose an online eligible agent with the fewest active chats, breaking ties by last assignment. |

Automatic modes apply when the handoff is offered. If availability checking is off and no eligible agent can take a direct assignment, a pending chat is created; an eligible agent can claim it when available. Changing policy does not retroactively assign old queue entries. The active-chat limit is 1–100, default 5, shared across teams within the workspace.

Presence expires after **90 seconds** without a heartbeat. Inbox refreshes presence while an available agent is signed in. Expired/revoked login sessions do not count as online, even if the saved Available switch was on. Capacity is checked again when claiming. A losing claim receives a conflict; the conversation is not assigned twice. Only the assignee can reply or close an active live chat.

## Follow-up paths and return to AI

After Save, two containers appear:

- **When live agent closes chat**: runs after the human closes the conversation and Chat Closed automation has finished. If Collect Feedback pauses for a submission, this path waits for that submission too.
- **When no live agent is available**: runs if the handoff cannot proceed. With availability checking off, an eligible offline agent causes a pending chat rather than this path.

The successful handoff pauses later workflow steps. The action emits no customer-facing text by itself; put a Send message before it if you want a connecting message. After the human closes from Inbox, the server durably records closure, fires the current **Chat Closed** trigger once, and then resumes the original handoff's close path and following actions. The Inbox record stays Closed; the conversation returns to AI mode, allowing messages, surveys, menus, and new customer replies on the same conversation ID. Add Close Chat in the follow-up if the AI conversation should finish instead.

The original action paths and continuation are saved when the handoff begins. Editing the workflow while a human is working does not replace that saved continuation. If its follow-up asks a survey, it continues against the original workflow until the pending steps finish; later incoming triggers then use the current saved workflow. Chat variables and custom-field values are preserved.

If post-close automation or the AI return fails, the accepted human closure and submitted feedback remain saved. Inbox/tester report the automation failure; the failed return is not automatically replayed. Review the workflow before starting a new conversation. Repeated close requests cannot run the return twice. A conversation with an active/pending handoff must be closed through Inbox, rather than the tester's simulated close event.

Teams referenced by a saved handoff cannot be deleted. Teams with pending/active conversations cannot have their member list changed or be archived until those conversations finish. An AI agent with pending/active live chats cannot be deleted. Existing direct assignments remain readable by the assignee after closure, subject to current workspace membership.

## Complete test flow

Create a **Complaints** team containing the support account and make that account available in Inbox. Use Manual claim initially.

```yaml
Message received: "human"
  Send message: "I'll connect you to our Complaints team."
  Live Agent Handoff:
    Availability check: On
    Assign chat: Specific
    Teams: Complaints
    Assign by language: On
    When live agent closes chat:
      Send message: "Your conversation is back with the AI."
    When no live agent is available:
      Send message: "No live agent is available right now."
Chat Closed:
  Collect Feedback:
    Rating enabled: On
    Variable: feedback_rating
```

1. In the Agent tester, send `human`.
2. In the support account's Inbox, open the pending chat and click **Claim chat**.
3. Send a human reply. It appears in the tester with a live-agent label.
4. Reply as the customer. The message appears in Inbox without running another AI workflow.
5. Click **Close live chat** in Inbox. The tester presents feedback first.
6. Submit a rating. The close path sends `Your conversation is back with the AI.` and the AI composer is available again.
7. Make the support account unavailable and start another test. The unavailable path should run when the availability check is on.

To combine Auto Team Match, place it before the handoff and use its Match found path. Set the handoff to Specific and **Team from chat variable** to `matched_team`. Handle Auto Team Match's No match and Error paths explicitly, for example by routing to a known General team.

## Delivery scope

The authenticated Inbox, human messages, claim/close lifecycle, customer tester updates, and post-close return are implemented. Published Webchat/WhatsApp and other channel transports remain separate milestones. The Inbox uses the same persisted conversation and message data as the tester; it is not a mock queue. Livechats navigation opens this working Inbox.

LLM_PROCESSING.title: LLM Processing
LLM_PROCESSING.content:
# LLM Processing

Version 0.15.0 makes **Add action → AI & data → LLM Processing** Ready. Configure it to summarise, classify, extract information, or generate text, then use its response in later actions. It does not send a message by itself.

## Setup

Keep your existing database and `backend/.env`. From **backend**, with the project virtual environment active:

```powershell
python -m alembic upgrade head
```

This applies migration **0008**, adding agent-owned Knowledge text sources without rewriting existing workflows or chat history. No new runtime dependency is required. Add or confirm these settings in `backend/.env`, then restart the backend:

```dotenv
GROQ_API_KEY=your_groq_key
GROQ_INTENT_MODEL=openai/gpt-oss-20b
LLM_PROCESSING_MAX_TOKENS=4096
```

The model selector displays the server's `GROQ_INTENT_MODEL`. Workflows store the `intent` model alias, so changing that environment setting applies to existing actions after restart. API keys remain on the server. The agent's **Enable LLM** setting must be on. `INTENT_LLM_ENABLED` controls intent recognition separately; it does not disable an explicitly configured LLM Processing action.

## Fields

| Field | How to fill it |
| --- | --- |
| Input | Text or substitutions such as `Summarise this complaint: {description.text}`. Text input supports up to 16,000 characters. |
| Script, below Input | Switch to a safe Python expression, such as `description.text` or `{"description": description.text, "rating": rating.norm.value}`. Expressions support up to 2,000 characters; structured results become JSON text. |
| Model | The configured Groq intent model, default `openai/gpt-oss-20b`. |
| Temperature | A number from 0 to 2; default 1. Try 0.2 for a factual summary. |
| System prompt | Instructions for the task, format, and tone, separately from customer input. Supports variables, up to 8,000 characters, or Script mode with a safe Python expression. |
| Use Knowledge info | Includes all enabled text sources saved in the selected agent's Knowledge tab. Add at least one source first. |
| Resulting variable | A custom name such as `complaint_details`: 1–64 characters, starting with a letter, then letters, numbers, or underscores. Python keywords, built-in function names, read-only system names, and `language` are reserved. |
| Advanced: Timeout after | 1–120 seconds, default 30. A provider timeout follows the Timeout path. |

Script mode uses the existing chat-script interpreter. It supports expressions and chat variables, without imports, arbitrary Python execution, filesystem access, or network access. Switching modes preserves the entered text; adjust it to match the selected mode before saving.

Click **Save**, then add actions beneath **Success**, **Error**, and **Timeout**. These paths work with Branch, Jump, nested surveys, and shared steps after the action. Existing step numbers and outcome path IDs remain stable when editing a saved action.

## Test flow: summarise a complaint

1. Open **Workflows → Chat started** and add **Ask survey**. Ask `Please describe your complaint.` with Text answers and chat variable `description`.
2. Add **LLM Processing** immediately after the survey:

   | Setting | Value |
   | --- | --- |
   | Input | `{description.text}` |
   | Model | `openai/gpt-oss-20b` |
   | Temperature | `0.2` |
   | System prompt | `Extract the main complaint from the customer's description. Return a concise, factual summary. Do not add information the customer did not provide.` |
   | Use Knowledge info | Off |
   | Resulting variable | `complaint_details` |

3. Under **Success**, add **Send message**: `I recorded this summary: {complaint_details}`.
4. Under **Error**, add **Send message**: `I could not summarise that right now. Please try again.`
5. Under **Timeout**, add **Send message**: `That took too long. Please try again shortly.`
6. Restart the tester and answer the question, for example: `I deposited money yesterday but it still does not show in my account.`

The generated summary is stored directly as a **string** in `complaint_details`. Reference `{complaint_details}` in Send message, or use `complaint_details` in a Python expression. Do not add `.body` or `.ok`: this action does not use the Send API response wrapper. Only the message action displays the summary. Create Ticket can also use this value in ticket fields.

## Test flow: classify feedback after closure

Under **Chat Closed**, add Collect Feedback with an optional open-response question stored as `feedback_comment`. Add LLM Processing after it:

- Input: `{feedback_comment}`.
- System prompt: `Classify the feedback as positive, neutral, or negative. Return exactly one lowercase word. If no comment was given, return neutral.`
- Temperature: `0`.
- Resulting variable: `feedback_sentiment`.

Under Success, a Branch can check `feedback_sentiment == "negative"` and use Set Variable or Send API to record the outcome. Under Error and Timeout, use Set Variable to record `"unavailable"` in a separate status variable. Ordinary Send message is unavailable after chat closure. Feedback submission resumes the model action while the conversation stays closed.

## Knowledge and language

See [KNOWLEDGE.md](KNOWLEDGE.md) to add files, URLs and snippets. Only relevant passages from this agent's enabled, Ready sources are included. Sources and customer input are separate task-data messages; the system prompt supplies the task instructions. The active conversation language is included in the system context. Switch Language before processing when needed, and state any required output format/language in your task prompt.

Knowledge is supplied to Groq with the prompt when enabled. The Knowledge base supports bounded document extraction, single-page HTTPS imports and lexical passage ranking. It does not recursively crawl a website or fine-tune model weights. Knowledge text and workflows have separate revision histories from agent settings snapshots and settings-only exports.

## Outcomes and limits

Success requires a complete, non-empty text response. Generated text is capped at 8,192 characters and 16,000 UTF-8 bytes; oversized or incomplete responses follow Error instead of silently truncating. The completion token limit is configured by `LLM_PROCESSING_MAX_TOKENS` (256–8,192). Serialized request context is capped at 128,000 bytes. Existing chat-variable limits also apply: 100 variables and 64 KiB total.

A failed attempt clears an existing result to `null` so downstream steps cannot reuse stale generated text. If no variable slot is available, Error runs without a provider request. A disabled action does not call the provider or change variables. Input values are resolved before replacing the result variable, allowing transformations of an existing value with the same variable name.

At most three processing requests run per incoming event, shared across its normal workflow, closure automation, and feedback continuation/callback. Requests also use the existing per-user model quota (`LLM_TESTER_REQUESTS_PER_MINUTE`, default 20). There are no automatic provider retries. Local or provider rate limits follow Error. This is a synchronous workflow action; provider processing is not undone if a later step causes a database rollback, so a manual retry may make another model request.

| Trace error | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `invalid_input` | A variable/expression could not be resolved, or the resolved input was empty/too long. |
| `provider_unavailable` | The server's Groq connection is unavailable or missing its key. |
| `llm_disabled` | LLM is disabled in the agent's settings. |
| `knowledge_unavailable` | Knowledge was requested but no enabled, Ready source is available for this agent. |
| `content_filtered_input` / `content_filtered_output` | Input or generated text was rejected; Error runs without exposing the rejected output. |
| `moderation_unavailable` | Required/connected category screening is unavailable or returned an invalid verdict. |
| `invalid_json_response` | JSON-object output mode did not receive a valid object. |
| `context_too_large` | The serialized request exceeds the context byte limit. |
| `processing_limit` | This event has already used three processing requests. |
| `request_limit` | The per-user model request quota is exhausted. |
| `provider_rate_limit` | Groq returned HTTP 429. |
| `provider_error` | The provider request failed. |
| `invalid_response` | The provider returned an empty, malformed, or incomplete completion. |
| `response_too_large` | The returned text exceeds the response limits. |
| `variable_limit` | The result could not fit the chat-variable limits. |
| `timeout` | The provider exceeded the selected timeout; Timeout runs. |

The tester trace includes outcome, configured model, knowledge source count, and a short error code. It does not expose raw provider errors or API keys. Model accuracy and exact output depend on the selected provider/model; use clear instructions and validate generated text before decisions requiring exact values.

Provider references: [Groq chat completions API](https://console.groq.com/docs/api-reference) and [Groq reasoning output](https://console.groq.com/docs/reasoning). The configured GPT-OSS model requests hidden reasoning and stores only its final answer.

## JSON-object output (0.26.0)

Output format defaults to Text, preserving earlier string behavior. Choose **JSON object** when a task returns structured data. The response must be one valid JSON object with unique keys and finite numbers, without code fences. The resulting variable then stores an object: later steps can use `{complaint_details.financial_institution}` or a Python expression such as `complaint_details.financial_institution`. Invalid JSON follows Error and keeps the cleared result null. Schema/required-field business validation still belongs in workflow actions. See the full complaint example in Knowledge → Guidance.

PEOPLE.title: People — native CRM, version 0.29.0
PEOPLE.content:
# People — native CRM, version 0.29.0

People manages the individuals who interact with Petrix AI and live agents. It provides registration, editable profiles, authorised conversation history, private notes, tags, People custom fields, search/filtering, export and confirmed deletion.

## Upgrade

Keep the existing database, virtual environment and `backend/.env`. Replace the source, then run from `backend`:

```powershell
python -m alembic upgrade head
```

This applies migration **0021**, adding private People notes and retry-safe manual registration metadata. Restart the API and Angular. No new dependency is required over 0.28.0. Migrations 0001–0020 are unchanged. Existing People IDs, contact information, fields, bans, conversations, tickets, workflow exports, Knowledge/PDF bot imports and unlimited AI agent creation/import remain.

## Add and edit a person

Open People and select **Add Person**. Enter a name, email address or phone number and Save. At least one contact identifier is required; an external ID also qualifies when supplied through additional details or the API. Location, country and external ID are optional. If several teamspaces are available for registration, select the intended one.

Email validation, single-line contact validation, valid two-letter country codes, unique external IDs and field-specific permissions apply. Registration uses a request ID so repeating a response-lost request does not create a duplicate. Reusing that ID with changed content is rejected. The same email address is not used to merge unrelated records automatically.

Select a row’s ID or name to open its three-section panel:

| Section | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| Details | The profile’s permitted contact fields, location/country, external ID, creation/update times and observed channels. Changes use the current revision. Existing profile tools retain messaging bans, configured analysis and profile iFrame access under their own permissions. |
| Conversations | Read-only chat and customer email history for this person. Each underlying chat/ticket also requires its own view permission. Messages, saved aliases and supported attachments/media use their existing presentation and access rules. |
| Notes & Tags | Add/edit/delete/colour private staff notes, manage tags/groups and edit People custom fields. |

Profile changes do not rewrite historical message identities or already-prepared email recipients. Registered contact details are used when selecting the person for new tickets. Existing ticket threads retain their own recorded contact details.

Private notes are visible only to authorised workspace members. They are never sent to the person, inserted into their conversation history, or included in customer transcript exports or AI conversation analysis. Notes are revisioned, limited to 8,000 characters each, and support up to 100 notes per person. A stale edit/delete returns 409. Person and note drafts have navigation guards.

## Search and filter

Search accepts at most **256 characters**; longer API requests return 422. Search covers the full ID and the name, email, phone and external ID fields visible to the current role. `%` and `_` are treated literally. Hidden fields cannot be inferred from search results.

| Filter | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| Tags | Effective tags, including tags assigned through selected groups |
| Tag groups | Direct groups and groups represented by effective tags |
| Custom fields | Active People fields and their typed values; configured defaults are respected |
| Channels | Ticket, Webchat, WhatsApp and AI agent handoff; other recorded transports retain their actual labels |
| Country | A saved country, only when the role can view location/country |
| Created on | Today, current week/month, or an inclusive custom range using the browser timezone |

The table shows ID, name, email, phone, location, country, channels, tags, groups and creation time as permitted. It defaults to 40 rows and supports 20/40/60/100 rows with exact filtered totals. Selection applies to the current page.

Channels are derived from the person’s related conversations that the current user can view. Ticket uses linked ticket records; AI agent handoff uses saved transfer metadata. Generic Messaging is not labelled WhatsApp without an explicit WhatsApp channel/provider marker. This update does not establish a new WhatsApp connection or infer countries from IP addresses or phone numbers. Empty information remains empty.

## Export

Select people and choose Export. Choose fields/timezone and optionally email a copy to your account. People exports default to the visible contact fields and **People custom fields**. Custom fields can also be selected individually. Exported defaults match the configured People field defaults. Conversation custom fields are not substituted for People fields.

The existing durable export jobs and Settings → Teamspace → Exports downloads are used. Plan limits, export grants, current profile visibility, field redaction and download grants are enforced again during processing/download. Private staff notes are excluded. Spreadsheet formulas in text values are escaped in CSV output.

## Delete

Select one or more rows and choose **Delete People**, then confirm. The complete selection and its current revisions are validated before any removal. At most 100 records can be deleted in one request.

Deletion removes the CRM profile, its custom-field values, staff notes, labels and ban events. It invalidates related stored People exports and analysis. Linked chats, ticket/email history, account users and consumed interactions are retained; the CRM foreign-key links become empty. An active ban additionally requires ban-management permission before deletion.

Reviewing retained messages, exporting a chat or checking assignment priorities does not recreate the deleted profile. A later real conversation event may register the person again with a fresh CRM ID; deleted notes and labels do not return. Removing a CRM profile does not erase personal information already recorded in chat/ticket content or older message snapshots.

## Permissions

View All People controls profile visibility. Manage All People controls mutations, and the individual name/email/phone/location/unique-ID/tags/custom-field grants remain independent. Registration, editing, notes and deletion use the relevant management grants and teamspace access. Custom team roles also follow their associated people, chats and tickets, within allowed teamspaces.

People access does not grant access to a person’s underlying conversations or AI-agent administration. Conversation history, channel filters and transcripts apply the existing record permissions. Exports and downloads retain their separate grants and plan rules. APIs require current workspace membership; every browser mutation also requires the existing CSRF header.

PERCEPTION.title: Perception — 0.32.0
PERCEPTION.content:
# Perception — 0.32.0

Perception monitors public mentions in a selected teamspace. Open **Perception** in the main navigation. Its six tabs follow the supplied interface and early-release availability.

| Section | Behaviour in this release |
| --- | --- |
| Overview | Unique-entry totals, source-category percentages, top keywords/categories/sentiment, publication-date reporting and three independently configurable charts |
| Keywords | Custom groups, variations, tags, team names/alternative names, enable/include switches, search, paging and confirmed bulk actions |
| Sources | Facebook and X page/profile or keyword sources, recurring schedules, historical/manual collection, run results, duplicate counts, retry and deletion |
| Processing → Translation | Persistent target/excluded language settings; background processing of new entries using the configured AI service |
| Raw Data | Read-only early-release preview of collected content, translations, provenance, keyword/tag snapshots, original links and dates, with filters and paging |
| Alerts | Clearly marked unavailable preview; creating alerts and sending threshold emails are disabled |
| Processing → Categorization | Clearly marked unavailable preview; eligible conversation dropdown/grouped-select definitions can be viewed, but categorization cannot be enabled |

Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, App Store, Play Store and News remain visible, with source creation disabled and API rejection `Scraping is not supported for this platform yet.` Their presence is not a claim of an implemented collection integration. Categories remain empty until an actual category assignment feature exists; unscored sentiment is displayed as **Not scored**.

## Upgrade

Keep the current database and `backend/.env`. From `backend`, run:

```bash
python -m alembic upgrade head
```

Restart the backend and Angular application. Migration **0024** adds six Perception tables. It does not rewrite previous modules or their records. Frozen migrations 0001–0023, backend dependency pins, frontend dependencies and bundled tools remain unchanged. Unlimited agent creation and complete workflow/PDF bot import remain available. Windows Python 3.9.12 stays the installation target; no new package is required over 0.31.0.

## Permissions and scope

**View perception** is required to open or read the module. **Manage perception** additionally permits mutations. These grants are independent: Manage alone does not confer View. Team grants and restricted teamspace membership are respected. The teamspace selector lists only spaces that can be viewed. Every API read and mutation repeats the scope check; disabling controls in the browser is not the authorization boundary. Mutations require the existing session/CSRF mechanism. Edits use revision checks; stale changes return 409.

Source, keyword, entry and processing data belongs to a teamspace. Team keyword options include only active teams in that space. Tags must belong to that space. Custom-field definitions retain their existing workspace scope. Opening Custom Fields still requires its separate permission.

## Collection connection

Facebook and X source management and the durable collection pipeline are implemented. **Real public collection requires an administrator-configured collection service with the relevant platform access.** This source package does not include platform credentials or a hosted scraping subscription, and does not scrape by automating a signed-in personal account. It never fabricates sample posts or reports success when the connection is absent.

Set these server variables:

```dotenv
PERCEPTION_PROVIDER_URL=https://your-collection-service.example/collect
PERCEPTION_PROVIDER_TOKEN=
PERCEPTION_WORKER_ENABLED=true
```

`PERCEPTION_PROVIDER_URL` is the exact POST endpoint; no path is appended. Credentials, query strings and fragments in this URL are rejected. HTTPS is required except for explicitly configured local loopback HTTP endpoints. The token is sent as a Bearer header and never returned to the browser or copied into a run error. Redirects are not followed. Source URLs are sent as data to this fixed, server-owned endpoint; Petrix does not fetch arbitrary user-entered hosts.

The UI readiness flag means the connection has been configured, not that a health check or real scrape has succeeded. The run status/log is the evidence of success. Missing configuration, platform-access failure, malformed data, timeouts and unverified public sources result in **Failed**, with a retry action.

### Collection request contract

The service must accept JSON such as:

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "run_id": "run-uuid",
  "workspace_id": "workspace-uuid",
  "source_id": "source-uuid",
  "platform": "x",
  "method": "keyword",
  "url": "",
  "range_start": "2026-11-01T00:00:00+00:00",
  "range_end": "2026-11-02T00:00:00+00:00",
  "groups": [
    {
      "id": "keyword-uuid",
      "name": "JKIA cancellation",
      "query": "\"JKIA cancellation\" OR \"JKIA\"",
      "terms": ["JKIA cancellation", "JKIA"]
    }
  ],
  "include_comments": false,
  "include_replies": false,
  "page_size": 500,
  "cursor": null,
  "page": 0
}
```

For page/profile collection, `method` is `page`, `url` is the normalized public page/profile URL, and `groups` is empty. Facebook page sources request posts and comments; X sources exclude replies/comments. For Facebook keyword searches, `search_utc_days` is additionally supplied with inclusive UTC search-day strings. The collector can fetch those whole days; Petrix applies the exact saved interval on ingestion.

`range_start` is inclusive and `range_end` is exclusive. The service must verify that a page/profile is public and of the requested type, or that the requested public search is authorized. It must filter by the requested source and date range and return stable platform IDs for deduplication. Petrix validates URLs and dates, verifies keyword IDs, rejects cross-platform links, filters irrelevant keyword hits and drops replies where they were not requested. It cannot independently authenticate a collection service's claim about a remote public page; connect a trusted service.

Return a successful response in this strict shape:

```json
{
  "public_source_verified": true,
  "entries": [
    {
      "external_id": "stable-platform-post-id",
      "content": "A public mention containing JKIA.",
      "url": "https://x.com/public_handle/status/123",
      "posted_at": "2026-11-01T10:20:30Z",
      "kind": "post",
      "keyword_ids": ["keyword-uuid"],
      "language": "en",
      "sentiment": "neutral"
    }
  ],
  "complete": true,
  "next_cursor": null
}
```

`kind` is `post`, `comment` or `reply`; `language` and `sentiment` are optional. Language is a code, and sentiment is `positive`, `negative`, `neutral`, `mixed` or `unknown`. Omit an unavailable score rather than inventing one. Publication timestamps require an offset. Public URLs must use HTTPS and the selected platform. `keyword_ids` must be among the requested groups. For keyword searches, a literal selected term must appear in the content; an empty keyword-ID list is filled only from such relevant matches.

For another page, return `complete: false` and a non-empty `next_cursor`. Completion and cursor must agree. Maximums: 500 records per page, 10 pages per run, 2 MiB per response page, 30,000 characters per entry, 45-second request timeout and 10-second connect timeout. A repeated cursor, invalid record or exhausted page budget fails the run without saving partial entries. Choose shorter manual date ranges for large volumes.

Each request carries an `Idempotency-Key` of `<run_id>:<page>`. The service should honor this key on retries. Network calls execute outside database transactions. Durable run leases and fencing tokens prevent an interrupted/deleted run from saving late results. A failed run can be retried up to ten attempts.

## Keywords

Custom groups have a main keyword, up to 30 variations (200 characters each), optional tags and an enabled state. The limit is **50 enabled groups per workspace**, including included team groups in their current teamspaces. Variations do not consume separate group slots. The two master switches control whether enabled custom or included team groups participate in collection. Disabling a master switch does not silently bypass the enabled-group limit.

Team names and alternative names are read from the current team record. Changes appear without copying stale team names into a new group; archived/deleted teams stop matching. Team tags can be edited from **Edit tags**. The group can be linked to one keyword source per platform in its teamspace. A Facebook source and an X source may both use it.

Disabling/removing a linked group, excluding a team or turning off a master switch prompts for confirmation. Disabling multiple groups and **Select all matching** also require confirmation. Bulk operations apply the displayed search/status filter, not an unscoped workspace selection. Sources left without active groups immediately lose their recurring schedule and receive a **Recurring scraping auto-paused** log. Inactive groups are pruned from source scope on its next scrape. Sources do not restart automatically when a keyword is enabled again.

## Sources and ranges

Facebook accepts a page slug URL or `pages/name/id`; non-page routes such as groups, events, watch and posts are rejected. The collection service must verify that it is an actual public page. X accepts exactly one valid handle under `x.com` or `twitter.com`, including www/mobile variants. Home, search, settings, messages, status URLs and multi-segment paths are rejected.

A source's platform, method and page/profile URL are fixed after creation; create a separate source to change them. Names, linked keywords, recurring state, interval and source timezone are editable. Allowed intervals are 1–30 days, 1–720 hours or 10–720 minutes.

Manual/historical ranges begin no earlier than 1 January 2024 and span at most one calendar year. Date-only end values include the entire selected day; timestamp ends are exclusive. Future calendar dates are rejected. Date-only current-day requests collect only records already published when the run executes. X ranges support seconds; naive local timestamps use the source timezone. Ambiguous/nonexistent daylight-saving wall times are rejected; an explicit UTC offset resolves ambiguity through the API. Facebook keyword manual/historical ranges accept only whole UTC date strings.

Enabling recurring scraping, creating a recurring source or changing its interval schedules a run at **now + interval**, covering `[now, scheduled_time)`. Subsequent runs cover `[previous_scheduled_end, previous_scheduled_end + interval)`. Delayed workers keep those frozen contiguous windows. Retrying a failed recurring run retains its coverage and does not create another successor. Automatic scheduling is in UTC and ignores the source timezone. Disabling/changing a schedule cancels queued recurring runs; an already running scrape retains its frozen request.

Logs retain trigger, status, date range, attempts, initiating user and configuration events. Facebook page results split Posts/Comments; X page results show Posts; keyword sources split results by group. Each row shows new/duplicate counts. Unique entries are deduplicated by teamspace, platform and stable external ID across sources. Provenance, keyword names and tags are retained in entry snapshots. Deleting a source removes its configuration/logs and frees keyword links while retaining collected entries.

## Background processing and translation

The API normally runs a separate Perception worker. For an external worker, set `PERCEPTION_WORKER_ENABLED=false` on the API and run from backend:

```bash
python -m app.perception.worker --watch
```

Omit `--watch` for one tick. The worker handles collection and entry processing, independent of the Inbox/Knowledge workers. Schedules and queued work survive restart; an expired in-progress lease is explicitly failed for retry.

Translation uses the existing `SUPPORT_AI_BASE_URL`, `SUPPORT_AI_MODEL` and optional `SUPPORT_AI_API_KEY` connection. It sends public entry content to that configured service, without a claim of Petrix-hosted inference. Source language and sentiment are accepted from valid collection data; missing sentiment/language can be classified by this AI connection. When no model is configured, unscored content remains unscored. A requested translation is marked failed rather than silently omitted.

The translation configuration is frozen for each newly collected entry. Originals are retained. Already-target-language and excluded-language entries are not translated. Translation/sentiment output is validated as structured data; invalid responses fail processing. **Retry failed processing** uses each entry's frozen configuration and requires a configured model. Saving new settings affects new entries, not old ones.

## Reports

Reports use original publication dates in the stored **Workspace General → Timezone** setting; scraped dates remain available in Raw Data. The reporting range is at most 366 days, and hourly grouping accepts up to seven days. Day/week/month/quarter/year grouping and source/platform/category/sentiment/keyword segmentation are available. Comparison A and B have their own filters and do not alter the main chart's saved controls.

Totals count unique entries. An entry can have several source/keyword/category associations; segmented mention counts can therefore exceed the total unique-entry count. Relative charts normalize series shares within each bucket. The twelve largest series are shown separately and all remaining values are retained in **Other**. Empty time buckets and daylight-saving offsets remain explicit. CSV/table views expose exact plotted values; PNG downloads use the existing chart renderer. Palette choice persists in the browser. Empty data displays zero/No results, with no seeded production records.

## API outline

Paths below are relative to `/api/workspaces/{workspace_id}/perception`.

| Method | Path | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/options` | Permitted teamspaces, platform availability, languages and configured-service flags |
| GET / POST | `/{space}/settings` | View/save master keyword switches and translation configuration |
| GET / POST | `/{space}/keywords` | Search/list/create custom groups |
| POST | `/{space}/keywords/{id}` | Revision-safe custom group update |
| POST | `/{space}/keywords/bulk` | Confirmed scoped selection actions |
| POST | `/{space}/teams/{id}` | Include/exclude a team keyword group and update its tags |
| GET / POST | `/{space}/sources` | List/create sources |
| GET / POST | `/{space}/sources/{id}` | Detail/log history and revision-safe updates |
| POST | `/{space}/sources/{id}/recurring` | Toggle/reschedule recurring collection |
| POST | `/{space}/sources/{id}/scrape` | Queue a manual range |
| POST | `/{space}/sources/{id}/retry/{run}` | Retry a failed run without changing coverage |
| POST | `/{space}/sources/{id}/delete` | Confirmed source deletion |
| GET | `/{space}/overview` | Summary/top tables and three chart configurations |
| GET | `/{space}/entries` | Read-only preview, filters and pagination |
| POST | `/{space}/processing/retry` | Requeue failed entry processing |

No alert-delivery or categorization mutation endpoint is exposed in this early release.

PLATFORM_GUIDE.title: Petrix AI platform guide — 0.35.1
PLATFORM_GUIDE.content:
# Petrix AI platform guide — 0.35.1

This is the current-release guide for Advisor and the in-dashboard documentation viewer. Earlier manuals can contain historical release and upgrade notes; this guide takes precedence for current availability. The current schema head is **0028**. From the `backend` directory, use `python -m alembic upgrade head`, then restart the API and frontend. Keep the existing database and `.env`. Agent creation and import are unlimited. Webchat sends show customer text immediately and retain conversation order independently of identical timestamps; 0027 also backfills saved histories without changing their text or IDs.

## Advisor: platform help and private history

Open **Advisor** using the lightning bolt in the main navigation. Type a question in **Type something...** and send, or choose a suggested question to pre-fill the composer. **Start Chat** opens a fresh discussion. Previous conversations are private to the current user and workspace, respect teamspace access and are grouped by recency. Select one to continue. The history menu can delete a private conversation after confirmation.

Advisor explains platform features and navigation. It does not change settings, execute workflows, send customer replies, inspect other users' histories or read private Inbox/CRM records. It uses bundled documentation and explicit user attachments. Source links and available platform shortcuts accompany replies.

Advisor works in documentation mode without an AI connection. An optional OpenAI-compatible model adds conversational answers and attachment analysis. Operator settings are `ADVISOR_BASE_URL`, `ADVISOR_API_KEY`, `ADVISOR_MODEL`, and `ADVISOR_VISION_ENABLED`. If no dedicated connection is configured, the existing support AI connection, then the existing tester model connection, can be used. Vision input must be explicitly enabled for a model that accepts images.

Attach up to five PDF, DOCX, TXT, Markdown, CSV, JSON, PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP files with the paperclip. Each file is limited to 10 MiB, with 20 MiB per message. Text documents must contain readable text; scanned PDFs do not receive OCR. Original attachments are retained privately; image previews are normalized. The configured model receives bounded relevant text and, when vision is enabled, up to two normalized images. Image interpretation is not claimed in documentation mode. A queued turn survives refresh; failed/interrupted turns can be retried. Removing an unsent attachment deletes its staged copy; sent files are removed with their private conversation.

Footer links open the Developer API reference, Documentation, Privacy Policy and Terms of Use. Legal pages remain marked development previews until final legal documents are supplied.

## How do I test an AI agent?

1. Open **AI agents** and select the agent.
2. Save workflow and settings changes.
3. Use the conversation tester on the right. On narrow screens, open its chat/tester button.
4. Start or restart the tester and send a question.
5. Review messages and the execution trace. **Test an event** simulates supported lifecycle events.

Fixed workflow messages can run without a model. Generative replies require the agent LLM setting and a working configured model. Saving a workflow and testing it are separate actions. The **Publish** tab supports Webchat and WhatsApp. Add a website channel, configure it, use Preview, save and enable it, then install its generated script. Saving a tester workflow alone does not update a published snapshot. For WhatsApp, choose the channel type, complete Meta connection verification and the callback/messages subscription, then save and enable it. WhatsApp publishing requires Lite or above; see the WhatsApp guide.

## What is a teamspace?

A teamspace is an area inside a workspace that scopes membership, records, operational settings and permissions. Default is created initially. Open **Settings → Workspace → Teamspaces** to manage spaces. Membership and team roles determine which spaces a user can access. Some definitions, including custom-field keys, remain workspace-wide.

## How do I add custom fields?

Open **Settings → Teamspace → Custom fields**, choose Conversation fields or People fields, and select **Create new field**. Set a stable key, name, type, options and default where appropriate, then save. Supported types include text, number, toggle, date, dropdown and grouped single select. Type/category are fixed after creation. Field definitions and values saved on a person/chat/ticket are separate. **Manage custom fields** is required to manage definitions.

## Can I ban customers?

Yes. Configure Rules and Reasons in **Settings → Teamspace → Banning**, then use authorized record tools to apply a ban to a person. Rules map previous offences to a duration; temporary bans expire. Removing a ban retains offence history. Active bans block customer/support replies, AI processing and claiming the affected chat. View and Manage bans are separate grants.

## How do I add team members?

Open **Settings → Workspace → Users** to add eligible existing accounts or use the invitation controls. Assign a role and teamspace access. Open **Settings → Workspace → Teams** to configure team members, alternative names and team roles. Managing users and managing teams require separate permissions. Adding a person in People creates a customer record, not a staff account.

## Knowledge PDFs, workflows and intent matching

Upload a readable PDF, add a public URL or paste a snippet under **AI agents → Knowledge**. Wait for training success before testing. Retrieval is bounded to relevant document passages. Input/output moderation uses the configured moderation connection when available/required.

An enabled workflow that matches an intent and executes a fixed Send message controls that reply. Uploaded Knowledge does not automatically replace a matched fixed message. General questions need a generative/fallback route that reaches Knowledge retrieval, a working model and the agent LLM setting. Avoid a broad catch-all intent that always sends a canned response. The trace shows which route executed. Embeddings support semantic matching/retrieval; unavailable connections are reported instead of silently implying successful semantic search.

Workflow LLM Processing can use its supported Knowledge configuration, structured JSON output and Success/Error/Timeout paths. It is distinct from Advisor and Inbox Copilot. A valid agent import uses format `petrix-agent`, schema version `1`; portable workflow/PDF exports can include both workflows and Knowledge documents.

## Workflows and supported actions

Workflows connect triggers to saved actions. Permanent step numbers identify actions, while tree order controls execution. Ready actions include Send message, Set variable, Jump, Ask survey, Branch, Send API, SQL Query, Switch Language, Send attachment, Show carousel, Close Chat, Collect Feedback, LLM Processing, Auto Fill Field, Auto Team Match, Send Graph, Live Agent Handoff, External Handoff, AI Agent Handoff and Create Ticket. Each action has its own guide. Features marked Later or unavailable cannot be activated by describing them to Advisor.

Send API supports configured HTTPS requests and separate response paths. SQL Query uses verified encrypted connectors and parameterized read-only queries. Ask survey collects validated answers and file uploads. Jump uses stable IDs to redirect to an existing saved node. Closing restricts subsequent conversation actions; Collect Feedback runs within its supported closed-chat lifecycle.

## Inbox, Livechats and Tickets

Inbox combines permitted chat/ticket queues, saved private/teamspace views, content search, personal pins/sort and up to five draft-safe panels subject to configured plan limits. Claim, transfer or use Takeover & Send when required. Replies, private notes and record tools have separate behavior. Attachments and recorded voice notes are native message attachments. Copilot suggestions are private until inserted and sent.

Livechats is a separate searchable repository with scoped filters, details, history, notes, transfers, exports and confirmed deletion. Tickets provides manual creation, subject/status/assignment, CC replies, private notes, custom fields and scoped exports/deletion. Email delivery uses configured SMTP/provider adapters; a real delivery receipt is needed to confirm delivery beyond SMTP acceptance.

## People CRM

People stores customer name, email, phone, location, tags, custom fields and interaction history. Use **Add Person** to register a customer. The detail panel includes Details, Conversations, and Notes & Tags. Notes are internal. Search is limited to 256 characters; tags/groups, custom fields, channels, country and date narrow results. Field-level permissions can hide individual profile values. Export and confirmed bulk deletion require their corresponding grants.

## Account, aliases, themes and presence

Open **Settings → My profile → Account** for profile fields, language, notification sounds and preferences. Use **Your account** for Online/Away/Offline presence and System/Light/Dark theme, workspace switching and sign-out. Availability and assignment capacity are independent of permission grants.

Open **Settings → My profile → Aliases** to create a display name, avatar and ticket email signature, choose a default alias and use it in the Inbox reply editor. Previously sent messages retain their original alias/avatar/signature snapshots. Deleting an alias prevents future use while retaining past identity snapshots.

## Analytics: reports, charts and scrolling

Analytics includes Live report, Messaging, Chats, CSAT, Tickets and Live agents. Select a date range and permitted teamspaces, apply filters and scroll the report pane to reach lower charts and tables. CSV and PNG controls export the displayed chart. CSAT summary/chart/table share filters. Agent views include measured activity, a users table and assignment heatmaps. Missing historical evidence is shown as unavailable, not invented.

Workspace General stores the reporting timezone. Each report has its own grant. Aggregate report access does not automatically confer access to underlying chat records or private People fields. The report's record links still require record permissions.

## Perception: public mentions

Perception supports Overview, custom/team Keywords, Facebook/X Sources, recurring/manual/historical collection, logs, deduplication and Translation. A compatible configured public collection service with platform access is required. Translation uses the configured AI service. Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, App Store, Play Store and News are not supported for collection in this release.

Raw Data is a read-only early-release preview. Alerts and Categorization are unavailable previews. A maximum of 50 enabled keyword groups applies per workspace. Disabling linked groups requires confirmation and pauses recurring sources with no active keywords. Frozen recurring date ranges remain contiguous despite delayed execution; failed runs can be retried.

## Settings, permissions and exports

Workspace settings include General, Teamspaces, Plan & billing, Roles & permissions, Users, Teams, IP allowlist, Whitelabelling and configured integrations. Teamspace settings include AI analysis, banning, assignment, fields, email configuration, exports, Copilot, tags, canned replies, overdue/mandatory ticket rules and profile/analytics embeds.

View and Manage permissions are independent. Record permissions can cover all, assigned teams or own records. Membership restrictions and team roles also apply. Owners/protected Admin retain broad access. Advisor can explain a feature without granting permission to use it.

Exports are durable jobs with Pending/Running/Completed/Failed states, selected fields, timezone and scoped download access under **Settings → Teamspace → Exports**. CSV exports include formula protection. Billing uses configured products and recorded weighted interactions; a self-hosted installation without an allowance remains unmetered. Do not assume a configuration change, email or payment has happened merely because Advisor explains how to do it.

## Publish and Webchat websites

Open **AI agents → Publish**, create or select a Webchat channel, and configure Setup, Appearance, Proactive messages, Multichannel widget links, Pre-chat form, Mobile and Installation. The design panel updates while editing. **Preview** opens an expiring draft sandbox without enabling the channel. **Save & publish** on an enabled channel captures saved agent settings/workflows; existing chats keep their version. Ready Knowledge sources remain available through their configured retrieval routes.

Copy the channel's own Installation script before the website's closing body tag. A real external website needs a reachable HTTPS API_BASE_URL. Enable exact-origin whitelisting when appropriate. Each website visitor receives an isolated capability and can continue their own history, complete pre-chat fields, run workflows and reach human support in Inbox. Staff credentials, workflow traces, variables and private notes are not exposed to visitors. WhatsApp is also available from Publish with its own Meta account, credentials and webhook setup. Other channel types are unavailable.

Voice/audio use compatible browser speech/recording services. Enable Speech-to-text and Text-to-speech in the agent Voice tab before enabling Webchat voice conversations. Browser availability and permissions apply. Ordinary audio clips and transcript-based hands-free voice turns remain distinct. Refer to the Webchat guide for installation, privacy boundaries, rate/file limits and browser testing.

## Developer APIs and documentation

The Advisor footer opens an authenticated in-dashboard Developer API reference generated from the running application's OpenAPI schema, with a JSON download. Documentation is bundled with the source and available without an external documentation host. The API uses the existing session, CSRF, workspace and record access controls. Do not put credentials in questions, source URLs or screenshots unless necessary for the task; access tokens stay in server configuration and are not needed to ask platform questions.

## Publish → WhatsApp

Add or open a WhatsApp channel in **AI agents → Publish**. Basics controls its name, configured language, Inbox icon and inactivity timeout. Configuration stores the Meta App ID, App secret, system User access token and Phone number ID privately. Save and verify the connection. In Webhook/Setup, copy the callback URL and separately generated Petrix verify token into Meta, verify the callback and subscribe to messages. Refresh status, enable the channel and save. A publicly reachable HTTPS API address and Lite or above are required for publishing.

Customer messages run the captured workflows and configured Knowledge/model. Human Handoff reaches the native Inbox, where authorised replies and files use the ordered delivery queue. Activity shows queued/sent/delivered/read and failed/blocked/uncertain outcomes. Unknown sends are held for review instead of replayed; known failed/blocked parts can be explicitly retried after the cause is corrected. Customer messages open a 24-hour service window; use approved templates through your WhatsApp business tools outside it. No template campaigns, bulk messaging or WhatsApp voice calls are implemented. Current Meta pricing is per delivered message under its applicable categories and conditions, separately from Petrix. See **WHATSAPP** for setup and recovery.

## Inbox loading and button hover (0.35.1)

Inbox Conversations contains permitted chats arriving from connected channels and permitted tester chats, together with tickets. My inbox shows active work assigned to you. Active livechats, Active tickets, Active AI chats and Test conversations apply their respective status/source filters. Listing uses a fresh permission snapshot for each request and batched message/channel metadata; full conversation data remains in the detail panel. Switching views cancels obsolete requests. Background updates keep rows visible, and a timed-out request can be retried with Refresh Inbox. Publishing Add Channel and Analytics Apply dates keep readable foreground/background colors on hover in dark and light themes. No new migration is needed over 0.35.0.

SEND_API.title: Petrix AI — Send API
SEND_API.content:
# Petrix AI — Send API

Version `0.7.0` implements server-side HTTPS requests with **Success**, **Error**, and **Timeout** paths. Use a response in later Send message, Branch, Set variable, or Send API actions. The request action itself sends no chat message.

## Settings

Open **Workflows**, choose an insertion point, and select **Send API** under **AI & data**.

| Setting | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| HTTP method | GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, or DELETE. GET sends no request body. |
| URL endpoint | An HTTPS URL, up to 2,048 characters in the saved configuration. Use variables in its path or query, for example `https://api.example.com/complaints/{complaint_ref}`. |
| Headers | Up to 20 optional key/value pairs. Names are case-insensitively unique. Values support variables, for example `Authorization` → `Bearer {access_token}`. Sensitive header values are masked in the editor and can be revealed. |
| Payload (JSON) | Shown for POST, PUT, PATCH, and DELETE. Choose JSON or Python expression. Empty means no body. A JSON content type is added unless you configure one. |
| Resulting variable | A custom chat variable, starting with a letter and using letters, numbers, or underscores, up to 64 characters. System names and Python keywords are reserved. |
| Request options → Timeout | Connection and read/write inactivity timeout, from 1 to 60 seconds; default 30. A slow response is also checked against elapsed time while its body is consumed. DNS resolution uses the host operating system's resolver limits. |

Select **Save**, then add actions under the outcome paths in the tree. A rejected save keeps your draft. Editing the request retains its outcome steps and their permanent numbers.

## Variables and payloads

Variables must exist before the action runs. URL values are substituted once and encoded so an answer cannot replace the endpoint's hostname, add query parameters, or change its path structure. Header values are substituted once and checked for line breaks and invalid characters.

For JSON mode, put placeholders inside JSON strings:

```json
{
  "reference": "{complaint_ref}",
  "customer_name": "{customer_name}"
}
```

The JSON is parsed before substitution. Quotes and backslashes in answers remain data, rather than changing the JSON structure. This mode retains the JSON literal's value types: a substituted JSON string stays a string.

Use Python expression mode for typed variables and objects:

```python
{"reference": complaint_ref, "amount": amount.norm.value, "confirmed": True}
```

Reference survey text with its bare name or `.text`, and survey numbers with their bare name or `.norm.value` in Python expressions. The result is encoded as JSON. Scripts use the existing bounded interpreter, without `eval`, imports, assignments, or arbitrary calls. JSON input supports up to 16,000 characters; Python expressions up to 2,000. Rendered data must fit the existing chat-value limits.

An access token can come from an earlier action. For example, if a token endpoint's resulting variable is `token_response`, set the next request's Authorization value to `Bearer {token_response.body.access_token}`. The token response must actually contain that field. Petrix does not obtain or invent authentication credentials automatically.

## Resulting variable

Every outcome replaces the previous result, including failures, so a failed request cannot leave a stale successful body.

For a variable named `complaint_status`, a successful JSON response looks like:

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "status_code": 200,
  "body": {"status": "resolved", "reference": "REF-123"},
  "error": null
}
```

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `ok` | True only for Success. |
| `status_code` | HTTP status when available; otherwise null. |
| `body` | Parsed JSON for `application/json` or `+json` responses, text for other responses, or null for an empty response. It is null when the response cannot be retained. |
| `error` | Null on success, otherwise a controlled error code. Raw exception text, request headers, and credentials are not copied into this field. |

Arrays, objects, JSON scalar values, plain text, and empty bodies are supported. The result, including its envelope, must fit the existing 16 KiB variable limit, nesting limits, and 8,192-character text limit. Reading stops at 64 KiB of response bytes. Gzip decoding is bounded too. Responses that exceed these limits use Error without retaining a partial body. If the result fits one variable but exceeds the conversation's remaining 64 KiB total capacity, Error stores a small `variable_limit` result instead.

## Outcome paths

| Path | When it runs |
| --- | --- |
| Success | An HTTP 2xx response with a usable body. |
| Error | HTTP non-2xx, connection/TLS/DNS failure, blocked endpoint, invalid/oversized response, invalid request inputs, or a request/value limit. |
| Timeout | A connection/read/write timeout or elapsed response-reading budget. |

Only the selected path runs. It can contain its own actions, surveys, nested Branch or Send API actions, trigger alternatives, and local fallback. An empty path continues immediately. After the selected path finishes, execution joins the actions following Send API.

Surveys and nested triggers pause in the selected path; resuming them does not repeat the completed API call. Jump can enter Send API itself, which makes a new request, or a step inside an outcome path, which bypasses the request and starts at that step. Jump away abandons the current continuation. Disabled Send API skips the request and all outcome paths.

Common error codes are `http_error`, `network_error`, `timeout`, `request_error`, `blocked_endpoint`, `invalid_response`, `response_too_large`, `variable_limit`, and `request_limit`. Request preparation errors, such as missing URL variables, take Error without contacting the endpoint. A chat turn can make up to ten API calls; further calls in that turn take Error with `request_limit`.

## Complaint lookup example

1. Add Ask survey with a Text field and chat variable `complaint_ref`.
2. Add Send API with method GET, URL `https://api.example.com/complaints/{complaint_ref}`, and resulting variable `complaint_status`. Add authentication headers if the real endpoint requires them.
3. Under Success, add Branch with condition `complaint_status.body.status == "resolved"`. Configure its messages for resolved/open results.
4. Under Error, add Send message: `We couldn't check your complaint right now. Please try again.`
5. Under Timeout, add Send message: `The service took too long. Please try again shortly.`

For a simpler Success response, add Send message using `Complaint {complaint_status.body.reference}: {complaint_status.body.status}.` Use field names actually returned by your API. The example host is a placeholder, not a supplied complaint service.

## HTTPS and private business systems

Requests originate from the Petrix backend. The destination must be reachable from that server and have a trusted TLS certificate. Certificates are verified against the original hostname, even though the connection is pinned to a validated DNS address. Redirects are returned as Error rather than followed. There are no automatic request retries, ambient proxy use, or shared browser/session cookies. Configure explicit headers for the external service.

Public HTTPS hosts require no additional setting. To use an internal banking or business API, an operator can add exact approved hostnames or IP addresses to the existing `backend/.env` and restart FastAPI:

```dotenv
SEND_API_ALLOWED_PRIVATE_HOSTS=core-api.bank.internal,10.20.30.40
```

This enables private addresses for those exact hosts; subdomains and wildcard patterns are not implied. Metadata/link-local, unspecified, multicast, and reserved destinations remain blocked. Every resolved address is checked before any request is sent, preventing mixed public/private DNS answers from bypassing the policy. URL credentials, dynamic hostnames, fragments, and transport/proxy headers are rejected.

An external POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE can change another system. Petrix's database rollback cannot undo an external change if a later workflow action fails. Use the destination's idempotency mechanism for operations that must tolerate a user retry or repeated workflow execution. No automatic retry is introduced by this action.

## Storage and API

The workflow node has `kind: "action"`, `type: "send_api"`, empty `children`, and three `paths` containers. Config fields are `method`, `url`, `headers: [{key,value}]`, `payload_mode`, `payload`, `variable_name`, `timeout_seconds`, `success_path_id`, `error_path_id`, and `timeout_path_id`.

Generate distinct UUIDs for each outcome and include exactly one matching `paths: [{id,children}]` entry per outcome. The server stores them in Success/Error/Timeout order. Child nodes use ordinary permanent step numbers; path containers are unnumbered and cannot be Jump destinations. Existing limits of 500 steps, 12 nested levels, and 1 MiB per workflow apply across all paths.

Use the existing revision-checked workflow save endpoint. Existing membership, Manage AI Agents, CSRF, conversation ownership, rate limiting, and conflicting-save checks apply. Tester trace records `type: "send_api"`, the selected `path_id`, `outcome: "success" | "error" | "timeout"`, `status_code`, and `error`, alongside the step UUID/number. Response bodies remain in the configured chat variable.

No migration or new dependency is required. Schema head remains `0005`; HTTPX and the TLS libraries are already pinned. Keep your current environment files and database, copy the source update, then restart FastAPI and Angular. See [WORKFLOWS.md](WORKFLOWS.md) if upgrading from an earlier schema.

SEND_ATTACHMENT.title: Send Attachment
SEND_ATTACHMENT.content:
# Send Attachment

Send one predefined file as an assistant message, then continue through the action's children and following steps. This action works inside Branch and API/SQL outcome paths and can be reached by Jump. It does not pause for a reply unless you add a nested trigger or an Ask survey action.

## Configure the action

1. Open an agent's **Workflows**, open a trigger, and choose **Add action → Messaging → Send attachment**.
2. Choose **Content language** from the languages already configured for that agent.
3. Choose a **File format** and **Source**, provide the file, and click **Save**.

| File format | Extensions |
| --- | --- |
| Image | jpg, jpeg, png, gif |
| Audio | mp3, m4a, wav |
| Video | mp4, avi, mov |
| Document | pdf, csv, doc, docx, xls, xlsx, ppt, pptx |

| Source | Configuration |
| --- | --- |
| Upload file | Browse or drop one non-empty file, at most 20 MiB (20,971,520 bytes). The backend checks extension and basic file contents; images also undergo image validation. Files are retained in PostgreSQL. |
| File link | A complete HTTP or HTTPS file URL, at most 2,048 characters. Query strings are allowed. Credentials, fragments, placeholders, whitespace, and non-web URL schemes are rejected. A recognised extension must match the selected format; extensionless endpoints and download-handler URLs are accepted, using a generic filename for the selected format. |
| Chat script | A safe Python expression returning a file URL string. Examples: `'https://example.com/forms/complaint.pdf'`, `file_url`, or `uploaded_form.url` from an attachment survey answer in this conversation. No curly-brace substitution is performed by this action. |

Hosted links are delivered directly to the browser; the backend does not fetch, proxy, inspect, or store their contents. The 20 MiB upload limit cannot be checked for a hosted URL. Use an accessible direct file URL and the correct format. Hosted files must remain available for as long as the link is needed; their contents may change outside Petrix AI. Authentication required by the host still applies.

The tester displays uploaded images and native audio/video controls, plus a download card. Documents receive a download card. Hosted files receive an **Open file** card; media also receive a preview. Actual audio/video playback depends on the browser's container and codec support, particularly AVI and MOV. A browser that cannot preview the media can still open or download it.

## Languages

Configure each language independently with the **Content language** dropdown. English and French can use different filenames, formats, or sources. Merely viewing an unconfigured language does not create an empty translation.

The runtime selects the active conversation language, then the agent's default language, then the first saved attachment. As with Send message, a missing translation uses this fallback. Provide all required language files before relying on a multilingual flow. **Switch Language does not translate file contents.** Stored translations remain in the action when an agent's configured languages change.

## Complaint form example

1. Add a **Message received** trigger named `Complaint form`, with exact English example `complaint form`.
2. Add **Send message**: `Here is the complaint form. Please complete it and keep a copy.`
3. Add **Send attachment**, select **Document → Upload file**, and upload `complaint-form.pdf`.
4. Add **Send message**: `Would you like help completing this form?`, with quick replies `Yes` and `Main menu`.
5. Add appropriate nested message triggers for those replies. Under `Main menu`, use **Jump** to your existing menu action.
6. Save, restart the tester, and send `complaint form`. You should receive a message, a downloadable PDF, and the follow-up question in that order.

To test localisation, configure French on the agent, add `formulaire de réclamation` to the trigger's French examples, provide the French messages and a French attachment, and put **Switch Language → French** before jumping to the shared menu or form trigger. The same attachment action will then send the French file.

## Chat script examples

Use a variable containing a URL:

```python
# Set variable: variable_name = file_url; chat_script = the expression below
'https://example.com/forms/complaint.pdf'
```

Then configure Send attachment as **Document → Chat script** with `file_url`.

To return a file collected by **Ask survey**, create an Attachment field named `uploaded_form`. Follow it with Send attachment, choose the matching file format and enter `uploaded_form.url`. Only actual files belonging to this conversation can be accessed through a relative survey URL. Another conversation's file, a workflow asset URL, and arbitrary server paths are rejected.

An expression returning a number, dictionary, missing variable, invalid URL, or mismatched extension produces a controlled tester error. The whole turn rolls back, including generated messages and newly copied file bytes. At most ten attachment actions may execute in one turn, including through Jump; this complements the existing workflow step limit.

## Storage, access, and upgrade

Apply migration **0007** from the backend directory before starting this version:

```bash
python -m alembic upgrade head
```

The migration adds `workflow_assets` and raises the conversation-file storage constraint to 20 MiB for sent copies. Survey answers keep their existing 10 MiB per-file and 20 MiB per-answer limits. Existing accounts, settings, workflows, step numbers, and survey files are retained. Keep your existing `backend/.env` and database.

Uploads are immutable, scoped to an agent and workspace, and require Manage AI Agents permission and CSRF protection. Workflow saves verify every upload reference and its selected format, including disabled steps and outcome paths.
