Unused draft/replaced uploads are deleted by the editor when discarded, saved, or removed; the server refuses to delete files still referenced by the saved workflow. Each agent can store up to 100 uploaded assets and 1 GiB in total. An interrupted browser session may leave an unused upload; the authenticated deletion endpoint can remove it once it is no longer referenced.

When an uploaded asset is sent, the bytes are copied into an immutable conversation attachment in the same transaction as its assistant message. Replacing or deleting the workflow asset cannot change earlier sent downloads. Conversation downloads are restricted to the conversation's user, workspace, and agent. Readable workflow previews require workspace membership. Media URLs support HTTP byte ranges. Documents are served as downloads, and uploads do not allow SVG, HTML, or executable formats.

The action emits one assistant attachment message per file. Billing/interaction deductions and delivery through published messaging channels are not implemented by this tester release. Agent configuration exports do not yet package workflows or their uploaded files; retain database backups for these assets.

SEND_GRAPH.title: Send Graph
SEND_GRAPH.content:
# Send Graph

**Add action → AI & data → Send graph** is Ready. It sends a chart as one assistant message and continues through its ordinary child actions and following steps. There are no Success/Error outcome paths on this action. It is also available under Chat Closed, including after Collect Feedback submits.

Charts render interactively in the Agent tester and in the live-support Inbox. Published Webchat/channel delivery remains a later milestone. The same saved message format and reusable chart component serve both interfaces. Chart rendering does not call an external chart-image service or send chart data to a third party.

## Settings

| Setting | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Graph type | Bar, Grouped Bar, Stacked Bar, Line, Multi-line, Pie, or Combo. |
| Chart data input | A JSON array, a chat-variable reference such as `{recent_transactions}`, or a Script expression such as `query_result.rows`. |
| Script | Uses the existing safe Python-expression interpreter. Expressions must return rows or JSON text containing rows. No imports, function definitions, assignments, or list comprehensions are supported. |
| Graph title | Optional shared heading, up to 200 characters. Long headings truncate with an ellipsis; hovering reveals the full title. |
| X-axis label | Optional horizontal-axis label and first table/CSV column heading, up to 100 characters. |
| Y-axis label | Optional vertical-axis label and value-column heading, up to 100 characters. Combo has separate bar and line series names instead. |
| Colour scheme | Default, Blue, Green, Grey, Orange, Rose, Violet, Yellow, Neutral, Distinct, Vivid, or Mild. |
| Show grid lines | Available for all types except Pie. |
| Show legend | Available for Grouped Bar, Stacked Bar, Multi-line, Pie, and Combo. Bar and Line have no legend control. |

Title and axis/series labels can include chat variables. Empty labels use sensible table/series defaults. The **Use example data** button fills the appropriate row structure for the selected type. Save preserves the action's ID, number, child steps, and following steps. Graph labels are configured on the action; this release has no separate per-language graph editor.

## Data rows

Single-series Bar, Line, Pie, and both Combo inputs accept `{x, y}` rows:

```json
[
  {"x":"Jan","y":1200},
  {"x":"Feb","y":980},
  {"x":"Mar","y":1450}
]
```

Grouped Bar, Stacked Bar, and Multi-line require `series` on every row:

```json
[
  {"x":"Jan","y":1200,"series":"Deposits"},
  {"x":"Jan","y":800,"series":"Withdrawals"},
  {"x":"Feb","y":1450,"series":"Deposits"},
  {"x":"Feb","y":980,"series":"Withdrawals"}
]
```

`x` is a non-empty label of up to 120 characters, or a finite numeric category normalized to a label. `y` must be a finite JSON number with absolute value at most 10^15; Boolean values and numeric strings are rejected. `series` is a non-empty name of up to 80 characters. Extra fields are rejected. The `series` field must be omitted for single-series types and both Combo inputs. Categories must be unique for a single series; `(x, series)` combinations must be unique for multi-series types. Leading/trailing label whitespace is ignored when checking duplicates.

Pie values cannot be negative. A non-empty all-zero Pie is valid and displays “No positive values,” with zero values/percentages in its legend/table. Bar charts support negative values and draw exactly-zero values as `0` at the baseline. Stacked charts maintain separate positive and negative stacks. Line points follow category order as supplied; multi-series categories follow first appearance. Missing series/category values remain blank in table/CSV and create gaps in lines rather than inventing zero values.

Each input supports up to **100 rows**, with up to **20 series** and **100 total categories** per graph. A resolved chart must fit within **64 KiB**. Input source is limited to 32,000 characters in text/JSON mode or 2,000 characters in Script mode. Existing chat-variable and script limits also apply. A workflow execution sends up to 10 charts. Dense charts and tables scroll inside the message.

Literal JSON is validated on Save, with a row and field error such as `Row 2 is invalid (y: Field required)`. Empty literal arrays are rejected. Variable and embedded-template inputs are validated at execution time. Typed substitutions work in JSON, for example `[{"x":"{month}","y":{amount}}]`, when `amount` is already numeric. Substituted customer text is handled as data and is never reinterpreted as another template or Python expression.

## Combo

Selecting Combo shows two sections, expanded by default:

| Bar data | Line data |
| --- | --- |
| Separate rows/variable and Script toggle | Separate rows/variable and Script toggle |
| Left value scale, with zero baseline | Independent right value scale |
| Y-axis label becomes bar series name, default `Bar` | Y-axis label becomes line series name, default `Line` |

Both inputs use `{x, y}` without `series`. A shared title and X-axis label remain in Styling options. Categories are aligned by label, keeping bar categories first and then any new line categories. An absent category is blank for that series. Series names appear in the legend, tooltips, table, and CSV; they are not drawn as vertical axis titles. The bar series name cannot be `x` (case insensitive); the line series name can. The two series remain separate even if their names are identical.

Default colour scheme uses Distinct for Combo: first colour for the bars and second colour for the line. Other palettes follow their configured colours. The legend can be hidden.

If either input resolves to `None`, an empty/whitespace string, or an empty list, **no graph message is sent and execution continues**. The trace records `skipped` with reason `empty_combo_data`. Both configured input fields must be populated before Save; the skip rule applies to resolved runtime data. Other invalid dynamic chart data produces a normal step-specific workflow error and rolls back an open turn, rather than sending a partial chart. After closure, the existing durable close/feedback rules preserve accepted closure/answers if chart generation fails.

## Chart controls

| Control | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| View as table / View as graph | Toggles between the chart and its scrollable data table. |
| Download data as CSV | Downloads the same categories, series headings, missing values, and numbers shown in the table. |
| Download chart as PNG | Downloads a chart image including the title and enabled legend on a white background. Disabled in table view. |

Hover or keyboard focus on bars, points, or slices reveals exact values; Pie also shows percentages. Values on bars are abbreviated, e.g. `12345` becomes `12.3K`. Line labels appear when space permits and are suppressed when they overlap. The legend lists series names; Pie includes each slice's value and percentage. The tester places legends below the chart.

CSV exports keep numeric values, including negative numbers, numeric and unquoted. Text cells are quoted and spreadsheet-formula prefixes are neutralized; original chart/table labels remain unchanged. Exported PNG uses a white background regardless of the current app theme. Chart data is saved in the message snapshot, so later variable or workflow changes do not change a chart that was already sent.

## Example 1: a complete test without an external service

1. Under Chat started, add **Set variable**:
   - Variable name: `recent_transactions`
   - Chat script:

```python
[{"x":"Week 1","y":12000},{"x":"Week 2","y":8500},{"x":"Week 3","y":15000},{"x":"Week 4","y":11000}]
```

2. Add **Send graph**:
   - Graph type: Bar
   - Chart data input: `{recent_transactions}`; Script off
   - Graph title: `Your transactions this month`
   - X-axis label: `Transaction period`
   - Y-axis label: `Amount`
   - Colour scheme: Blue
   - Show grid lines: enabled
3. Add **Send message**: `You can view the data as a table or download the chart.`
4. Save and restart the tester. The chart and following message should appear. Try table view, CSV, and PNG.

For Script mode, use `recent_transactions` without curly brackets. For Send API responses use `{api_result.body}` or Script `api_result.body`; the body must contain rows or JSON text containing rows.

## Example 2: SQL Query → Branch → Send Graph

Select your verified database connector and use:

```sql
SELECT default_language AS x, COUNT(*)::double precision AS y
FROM public.ai_agents
GROUP BY default_language
ORDER BY default_language
```

Store the result as `agent_counts`. This assumes the connected database contains the existing Petrix `public.ai_agents` table. In **SQL Query → Success**, add Branch with `len(agent_counts.rows) > 0`. In its If path, add Send graph with Script on, input `agent_counts.rows`, graph type Bar, title `AI agents by language`, X-axis label `Language`, and Y-axis label `Agents`. In Else, send `No agent records were found.` Handle SQL Error and Timeout with appropriate messages.

Use numeric columns or cast decimal/numeric database results to `double precision` in the SELECT: the SQL connector serializes Decimal values as strings, while chart `y` must be a number. Alias the returned columns exactly as `x`, `y`, and (for multi-series charts) `series`.

## Upgrade and message contract

Send Graph was introduced in **0.18.0** without a dependency, environment variable, or migration. The current **0.20.0** release includes Inbox and external handoff, and requires schema head **0012**. Replace source while preserving `.env`, run `python -m alembic upgrade head` from backend, restart backend/frontend, and reload the browser. See [Live Agent Handoff](LIVE_AGENT_HANDOFF.md) for the upgrade and support setup.

Workflow `type:"send_graph"` stores flat settings: `graph_type`, `data`, `data_mode`, `bar_data`, `bar_data_mode`, `line_data`, `line_data_mode`, `title`, `x_axis_label`, `y_axis_label`, `bar_label`, `line_label`, `color_scheme`, `show_grid`, and `show_legend`. Modes are `template` or `expression`. Unused data fields are cleared on Save. Ordinary `children` continue after the action; there are no outcome `paths`.

The assistant message has `source:"send_graph"`, empty plain `content`, and a `graph` object containing `version:1`, the resolved type/labels/styles, and normalized `data`, `bar_data`, and `line_data` arrays. Input expressions and variable source text are not included. The existing authenticated message metadata stores this snapshot; no new database table is required.

SET_VARIABLE.title: Petrix AI — Set variable
SET_VARIABLE.content:
# Petrix AI — Set variable

Set variable creates or updates data in one chat session. It does not send a message. A later action can read the value, including Send message using `{complaint_ref}` or `{{complaint_ref}}`.

## Apply the update

Stop FastAPI and Angular, copy the updated project contents into your Petrix folder, and keep `backend/.env`, `.venv`, the database, and Mailpit. Python 3.9.12 remains supported. The current source includes new intent-matching dependencies; follow [INTENT_MATCHING.md](INTENT_MATCHING.md) to install them and configure the additional matching stages before restarting the services.

Set variable uses the conversation JSON storage added in migration `0003`. The current release also includes migration `0004` for permanent workflow step numbers, `0005` for survey file storage, and `0006` for database connections. Run `python -m alembic upgrade head` from `backend` and verify `0006 (head)` before starting the API. See [WORKFLOWS.md](WORKFLOWS.md) for the upgrade commands and numbering behaviour.

## Configure and test

Open **AI agents → Workflows**, choose a workflow, select the desired **Add action** insertion point, then choose **Flow control → Set variable**.

| Setting | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| Variable name | 1–64 ASCII characters. Start with a letter; continue with letters, numbers, or underscores. Names are case-sensitive. |
| Chat script | A Python expression of up to 2,000 characters. Quote literal text; refer to existing variables by their bare names. |

Select **Save**. The action runs at its saved position when its parent trigger matches. Disabling it skips the action and its nested steps while preserving its configuration.

Create these four actions in sequence to try the complaint-reference example:

| Step | Action | Variable name | Chat script / message |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Set variable | `financial_institution` | `"PetrixBank"` |
| 2 | Set variable | `ticket_number` | `"12345"` |
| 3 | Set variable | `complaint_ref` | `financial_institution + "-" + ticket_number` |
| 4 | Send message | — | `Your complaint reference is {complaint_ref}.` |

When placed under Chat started, restart the tester after saving. The reply is `Your complaint reference is PetrixBank-12345.` Open **Session variables** below the tester conversation to inspect the stored values. If the ticket number is numeric, use `financial_institution + "-" + str(ticket_number)` instead.

## Supported expressions

Values retain their types: text, finite numbers, Booleans, `None`, lists, and objects with string keys. Tuples become JSON lists for storage. Use Python spelling `True`, `False`, and `None`; the inspector displays JSON `true`, `false`, and `null`.

| Purpose | Chat script |
| --- | --- |
| Flag | `True` |
| Calculation | `round(amount * 0.16, 2)` |
| Counter with a default | `variables.get("attempts", 0) + 1` |
| Conditional value | `"approved" if score >= 700 else "review"` |
| Clean the incoming message | `message.strip().lower()` |
| Structured data | `{"name": agent_name, "verified": False}` |
| Read structured data | `customer.name`, `customer["name"]`, or `customer.get("name", "Unknown")` |
| Read a list item | `products[0]` |
| Format text | `f"{financial_institution}-{ticket_number}"` |

Supported operators: `+`, `-`, `*`, `/`, `//`, numeric `%`, unary signs, comparisons, membership checks, `and`, `or`, `not`, conditional expressions, indexing, and slicing. Text concatenation requires text operands; use `str()` for a number.

Functions: `str`, `int`, `float`, `bool`, `len`, `round`, `abs`, `min`, `max`, and `sum`. Use positional arguments. `int` and `float` accept one argument; rounding uses `round(value, precision)`. String methods: `lower`, `upper`, `strip`, `lstrip`, `rstrip`, `replace`, `split`, `join`, `startswith`, and `endswith`. Object `.get()` supports an optional default. Plain f-strings work; format specifications do not.

Chat scripts are expressions rather than full Python programs. The interpreter does not expose imports, files, networking, arbitrary functions or attributes, assignments, loops, comprehensions, lambdas, or object mutation. It interprets an allow-listed AST without using `eval`, `exec`, or `compile`.

Version `0.6.0` also supports read-only survey views: `answer.text` for text and `score.norm.value` for a number. Raw values, direct expressions, and existing message placeholders remain supported. Public dotted access resolves JSON keys only; private Python attributes remain blocked. See [BRANCH.md](BRANCH.md).

## System variables

These names are available directly or through the read-only `system` dictionary, such as `system["agent_name"]`:

| Name | Value / access |
| --- | --- |
| `language` | Active session language. Writable; the result must be one of the agent's configured codes. |
| `agent_name`, `agent_id` | Saved agent name and current ID; read-only. |
| `default_language` | Agent's configured default language; read-only. |
| `conversation_id` | Current saved chat ID, including during Chat started; read-only. |
| `message` | Current event's text, or empty text on other events; read-only. |
| `feedback_rating` | Default persisted Collect Feedback rating variable (integer 1–5); configurable/writable since 0.13.0. `system["feedback_rating"]` exposes the submitted CSAT value or `None`. |
| `attachment_name`, `attachment_type` | Current attachment test's filename/category, or empty text; read-only. |

`variables` is a read-only dictionary of custom values. Use `variables.get("name", default)` when a value may not exist yet. System names, helper function names, and Python keywords cannot be custom variable names. The supported system write is `language`, for example a name of `language` and script `"sw"`. Following actions immediately use that language, and the tester follows it on later turns. The agent's saved default remains unchanged.

## Message placeholders

Both `{complaint_ref}` and `{{complaint_ref}}` work. Structured values support paths such as `{customer.name}` or `{products.0.name}`. Existing `{_chatbot.name}`, `{{agent.name}}`, `{{input.message}}`, and `{{feedback.rating}}` placeholders continue to work. Quick reply labels also support variables.

To display a value in bold in the tester, wrap its message placeholder in double asterisks, such as `Your reference is **{complaint_ref}**.` Variables are substituted by the backend before the assistant message is formatted for display.

Substitution is plain text and runs once. A variable containing another placeholder is displayed literally. Booleans, numbers, objects, and lists render as JSON; `None` renders as empty text. Unknown variables/paths produce a tester error instead of sending an unresolved placeholder. Rendered messages are limited to 4,000 characters and quick replies to 100 characters. Quick replies must remain distinct after substitution.

## Lifetime, errors, and limits

Values persist across turns, nested waits, unmatched events, and workflow revisions in the current conversation. A workflow edit clears obsolete execution continuations while retaining variables. Restarting the tester creates a new chat with fresh variables. Existing authentication, CSRF, workspace, Manage AI Agents, and conversation-owner checks protect access.

Invalid names and unsupported scripts are rejected when saving. Missing variables, invalid types, division by zero, unavailable keys/indexes, invalid languages, and size errors are reported when the step runs. Failed turns roll back that turn's assignments and messages; previous saved turns remain intact. Errors identify the step without echoing variable contents. Variables are not implicitly added to LLM prompts.

Each chat supports 100 custom variables using 64 KiB in total. A value uses up to 16 KiB; text up to 8,192 characters; lists/objects up to 100 items per container with eight nested levels. Numbers must be finite; integers have a 256-bit limit. Expressions allow 200 AST nodes, 20 levels of expression nesting, and a bounded operation count. Oversized repetitions, joins, and replacements are rejected before allocating the expanded result.

## Code and API

| Location | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `backend/app/workflows/actions/set_variable/config.py` | Name and expression validation. |
| `backend/app/workflows/actions/set_variable/handler.py` | Evaluate and assign; no message output. |
| `backend/app/workflows/chat_script.py` | Expression interpreter and JSON value validation. |
| `backend/app/workflows/context.py` | Session state, system variables, assignment policy. |
| `backend/app/workflows/templates.py` | Message and quick reply placeholders. |
| `frontend/src/app/features/workflows/actions/set-variable` | Dedicated settings component. |

The workflow node uses `kind: "action"`, `type: "set_variable"`, and config `{ "variable_name": "complaint_ref", "chat_script": "financial_institution + \"-\" + ticket_number" }`. Use the existing revision-checked workflow save API. `/tester/events` now returns a `variables` JSON object alongside messages, trace, language, and lifecycle state. Set variable appears in the trace without creating a message. Other unimplemented action types remain unavailable.

SHOW_CAROUSEL.title: Show Carousel
SHOW_CAROUSEL.content:
# Show Carousel

Show Carousel sends one assistant message containing a horizontally scrollable set of cards. Each language can have **1–10 cards**, with **0–3 buttons per card**. Cards can have an optional uploaded or hosted image, a required title, and an optional subtitle.

## Configure cards

1. Open an agent's **Workflows**, open the relevant trigger, and choose **Add action → Messaging → Show carousel**.
2. Choose **Content language**. Expand **Card #1** to edit it.
3. Enter a title (up to 80 characters) and optional subtitle (up to 200 characters).
4. For **Image**, choose **No image**, **Upload image**, or **Image link**. Uploads accept JPG, JPEG, PNG and GIF up to 20 MiB, using the existing validated workflow-file storage. Drop a file onto the upload area or browse for one. Hosted image links must be complete HTTP(S) URLs.
5. Add up to three buttons and configure their labels and actions.
6. Use **Add card** for more cards. Drag a card by its grip, or use its up/down buttons, to change its order. The delete icon removes that card from the draft.
7. Click **Save**. Restart the tester to replay Chat started, or send the message matching your trigger.

Viewing a language with no carousel does not create an empty translation. Use **Add card** in that language to configure one. Card and button identities survive editing and reordering, while the workflow action retains its permanent step number.

## Buttons

| Button action | Fields | Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Send reply | Button label and Message sent | Adds the configured message as the customer's next chat message and runs normal Message received matching. |
| Link | Button label and Webpage URL | Opens the webpage in another tab. HTTP(S) URLs, query strings, and page anchors are supported. |
| Link with Open in webview | The same Link fields, plus the checkbox | Opens an embedded webpage inside the tester's chat panel, with Close and Open in new tab controls. |

Button labels can use up to 80 characters. Reply messages can use up to 1,000 characters. For example, two cards may both have a button labelled **Select**, while their **Message sent** values are `Transactions` and `Accounts`. Add nested Message received triggers matching those values to route the selection.

Showing a carousel continues through its children and following actions. A reply button does not directly execute an arbitrary node ID; it sends its configured message to the existing workflow matcher, just like a typed reply. Add a nested trigger where the workflow should wait. Link clicks open the webpage without posting a message, resuming a survey, or changing workflow state.

The latest available carousel reply choices remain usable when followed by ordinary explanatory text. They become inactive after the customer replies, a newer interactive prompt appears, a survey starts, or the chat closes. Link buttons remain usable as links. Failed message submissions restore the input and previous choices, consistent with the existing tester.

## Complaint category example

Create a **Message received** trigger with the exact example `make a complaint`. Under it, add **Show carousel**, named `Complaint categories`, with these cards:

| Card | Title | Subtitle | Button label | Message sent |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Transactions | Get help with a transaction. | Select | Transactions |
| 2 | Accounts | Get help with your account. | Select | Accounts |

Upload suitable category images if desired. Under that same carousel action, add two nested triggers:

1. **Message received: Transactions** → **Ask survey**: `What is your complaint reference?`, stored as `complaint_ref` → **Send message**: `We will check complaint {complaint_ref}.` → **Jump** to your existing main menu.
2. **Message received: Accounts** → **Send message**: `Please describe the issue with your account.` → an appropriate survey or support sequence.

Save the steps, restart the tester, send `make a complaint`, and select Transactions. You should see one carousel, then the reference question. Enter a reference and verify the confirmation and menu continuation. Swiping, the horizontal scrollbar, left/right arrow keys on the carousel region, and the previous/next controls navigate the cards.

## Localisation and variables

Configure each agent language independently using **Content language**. Titles, subtitles, button labels, reply values, images, and link choices can differ by language. Add translated trigger examples matching the translated **Message sent** values.

For example, French cards can use `Opérations` / `Comptes`, with **Choisir** buttons sending `Opérations` / `Comptes`. Configure those French examples on the corresponding triggers. **Switch Language → French** selects the French carousel on its next execution, including when reached by Jump.

The runtime uses the active language's carousel, then the agent's default, then the first configured translation. It does not translate text or images automatically. Merely viewing an unconfigured language does not affect existing content.

Title, subtitle, label, and reply-message fields support the existing `{variable}` and `{{variable}}` text substitutions, including survey `.text` and `.norm.value` views. Unknown variables, empty required rendered text, or oversized rendered text produce a controlled tester error and roll back that turn. Image and webpage URLs are fixed URLs in this release; do not put variable placeholders or Python in URL fields.

## Webview behavior

Webview embeds the chosen website in an iframe inside the tester, preserving the conversation behind it. Close returns to the chat without posting a reply. The iframe permits scripts and forms while retaining a sandboxed, separate origin and preventing access to the surrounding application or top-level navigation. The explicit **Open in new tab** link uses `noopener noreferrer`.

Some sites prohibit embedding through their response policies; others need browser storage, authentication, popups, or other features restricted by the sandbox. Those sites should be opened using **Open in new tab**. The application does not bypass a website's embedding policy, proxy its HTML, or claim it can reliably detect every blocked iframe. See the [iframe reference](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/iframe) for browser behavior.

## Storage and compatibility

No new dependency or database migration is added. **Schema head remains 0007**, which must already be applied for image uploads. Keep the existing `.env`, database, and dependency lock files when updating the source. Older installations should run `python -m alembic upgrade head` from backend before starting the API.

Workflow JSON stores card configuration and uploaded image IDs. Uploads use PostgreSQL `workflow_assets`; sent image snapshots use `agent_attachments`, scoped to the conversation owner. A reused uploaded image is copied once per turn and shared by cards in that turn. Replacing a workflow image preserves earlier sent images. The existing 100-file/1-GiB per-agent upload quota is shared with Send Attachment. Image deletion is blocked while any saved attachment or carousel translation references the asset, including disabled steps and outcome paths. Draft/replaced image cleanup follows the existing editor behavior.

Hosted image and webpage URLs are delivered to the browser without backend fetching. HTTP(S) URLs are validated; scripts, file/data URLs, credentials, whitespace, and placeholders are rejected. External content must remain accessible. Carousel text is rendered as text rather than HTML.

Each carousel emits one assistant message regardless of card count. A turn can emit at most ten carousels, in addition to the existing workflow execution limits. Billing deductions and published-channel delivery remain outside the current tester release. Existing agent configuration exports do not package workflows or uploaded images.

SQL_QUERY.title: SQL Query
SQL_QUERY.content:
# SQL Query

Version 0.8.0 adds a PostgreSQL SELECT action with Success, Error, and Timeout paths. First connect and verify your database in [Database connections](DATABASE_CONNECTIONS.md).

## Settings

| Setting | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Database connector | A verified connection from the current workspace. Refresh the selector after verifying a connection in Settings. |
| Query | A single read-only SELECT, up to 8,000 characters in SQL template mode. |
| Query format | SQL template, or a bounded Python expression returning a static SQL string (up to 2,000 expression characters). |
| Timeout after (seconds) | 1–120 seconds, default 30. Connection setup uses at most 10 seconds of the lookup budget; PostgreSQL statement timeouts and remaining-budget checks govern execution/fetching. |
| Resulting variable | A custom chat variable, starting with an ASCII letter, then letters/numbers/underscores, up to 64 characters. Reserved/system names are rejected. |

Use **Save**, then add subsequent steps under the three paths in the workflow tree. Path containers have no step number; actions inside them keep permanent numbers and can be Jump destinations. After the chosen path finishes, following sibling actions continue. A survey or nested trigger inside a path can pause and later resume normally.

## Safe chat parameters

In SQL template mode:

```sql
SELECT ref, status FROM public.complaints WHERE ref = {complaint_ref}
```

`{complaint_ref}`, `{{complaint_ref}}`, and quoted `'{{complaint_ref}}'` are all bound as a single value. Text containing quotes, SQL keywords, or semicolons remains data. Do not concatenate or interpolate raw answers into SQL. Placeholders refer to values, not table names, column names, or SQL fragments.

Survey text also supports `{complaint_ref.text}`; a numeric survey answer supports `{account_id.norm.value}`. Plain variable names and scalar object fields work too. Missing variables or non-scalar parameter values follow Error without contacting the database. Null, text, numeric, and Boolean parameters preserve their types.

In Python expression mode, return the SQL **template** as a string:

```python
"SELECT ref, status FROM public.complaints WHERE ref = {complaint_ref}"
```

Expressions use the existing bounded Python chat-script evaluator. The SQL template expression has no access to chat variables; use the bound placeholders inside its string. Direct interpolation such as `"SELECT ... '" + complaint_ref + "'"` is rejected. This avoids turning a person's reply into SQL syntax.

Supported SQL includes joins, scalar expressions, aggregates, UNIONs, and SELECT subqueries. Writes, multiple statements, WITH statements, SELECT INTO, locking clauses, session changes, sequence modifications, and known side-effect primitives are rejected. A trailing semicolon and SQL comments are accepted. String/identifier escapes with backslashes are excluded to avoid ambiguous parsing. PostgreSQL also enforces read-only access while executing the query. Use a dedicated SELECT-only database account and restrict custom function/extension privileges.

## Result structure

For resulting variable `complaint_status`:

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "rows": [{"ref": "REF-123", "status": "resolved"}],
  "columns": ["ref", "status"],
  "row_count": 1,
  "truncated": false,
  "error": null
}
```

Always check `complaint_status.row_count > 0` before reading the first row. An empty SELECT is successful (`rows: []`, `row_count: 0`), not an Error. A Send message displays one field with `{complaint_status.rows.0.status}`; using `{complaint_status}` prints the full result object.

At most 50 rows and 50 distinct column names are returned. Use aliases for duplicate column names. Results also obey existing chat-variable limits: 16 KiB per value, up to 8 levels of nesting, and 64 KiB/100 variables per chat. `truncated: true` means the row or size limit stopped collection; use SQL filters/order/limit for precise lookups. `row_count` counts returned rows, not all matches. An individual row that cannot fit follows Error. Decimal amounts are strings to preserve exactness; dates/times and UUIDs become strings, bytea becomes base64, and supported JSON/arrays stay structured.

Error and Timeout store the same shape with `ok: false`, empty rows/columns, row_count 0, and a controlled error code. Query/connection details and credentials are not included. Codes include `invalid_query`, `connection_unavailable`, `credentials_unavailable`, `query_failed`, `invalid_columns`, `result_too_large`, `unsupported_result`, `variable_limit`, `query_limit`, and `timeout`. A turn supports at most 10 database lookups. Unverified/deleted/foreign connectors cannot execute. Query errors choose Error; query cancellation or connection timeout chooses Timeout. TLS errors choose Error. Verification establishes access at that time; each runtime lookup checks status and opens a fresh connection.

## Complete complaint flow

Create `public.complaints` and sample data in your own database outside Petrix, then grant your reader SELECT access. Assume REF-123 has status `resolved`.

1. **Message received:** example `Check complaint`.
2. **Ask survey:** “What is your complaint reference?”, Text, variable `complaint_ref`, skipping disabled.
3. **SQL Query:** verified `complaints_db`, SQL template `SELECT ref, status FROM public.complaints WHERE ref = {complaint_ref}`, timeout 30, variable `complaint_status`.
4. Under **Success**, add **Branch**:
   - If `complaint_status.row_count > 0 and complaint_status.rows[0].status == "resolved"`: Send message `Good news – complaint {complaint_status.rows.0.ref} is resolved.`
   - Else if `complaint_status.row_count > 0`: Send message `Complaint {complaint_status.rows.0.ref} is currently {complaint_status.rows.0.status}.`
   - Else: Send message `I could not find that complaint reference.`
5. Under **Error**: Send message `I could not check your complaint right now. Please try again.`
6. Under **Timeout**: Send message `The lookup took too long. Please try again shortly.`
7. After SQL Query, add **Jump** to your existing Main menu step.

Restart the tester, send `Check complaint`, and answer `REF-123`. Expect the resolved message followed by the Main menu. Test an unknown reference for the empty-result path. Test query failure using a missing table in a dedicated development database. Do not modify a live connector just to simulate errors. The tester variable inspector shows rows; its trace shows the selected outcome and returned row count.

## Execution guarantees and deployment checks

Each lookup uses explicit psycopg keyword connection parameters, parameter binding, a short-lived read-only transaction with forced rollback, server-side cursor fetching, controlled TLS mode, PostgreSQL statement timeouts, and bounded results. No SQL is executed by an OS shell or Python eval/exec. Saving the workflow validates connector ownership/verification and path integrity. CSRF, workspace membership, Manage AI Agents, workflow revisions, and tester conversation ownership continue to apply.

Run the backend test suite against an isolated PostgreSQL test database, never a production database. The tests create/drop temporary schemas and test tables. Ordinary PostgreSQL remains the runtime dependency; the local QA harness used for this deliverable is not shipped as a database requirement.

PostgreSQL read-only behavior and psycopg parameter handling are described in the official [SET TRANSACTION](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-set-transaction.html), [transaction management](https://www.psycopg.org/psycopg3/docs/basic/transactions.html), and [query parameter](https://www.psycopg.org/psycopg3/docs/basic/params.html) documentation.

SWITCH_LANGUAGE.title: Switch Language
SWITCH_LANGUAGE.content:
# Switch Language

Version 0.9.0 adds a workflow action that changes the current conversation's active language. It uses languages already configured in that agent's Agent settings. It does not change the agent's default language, affect another conversation, or send a message by itself.

## Configure the action

1. In the agent's **Agent → Languages** settings, enable the languages you need (for example English and French) and save.
2. Open **Workflows**, choose a trigger, and select **Add action → Flow control → Switch Language**.
3. Select **Target language** and press **Save**. The selector contains only that agent's configured languages and initially selects its default language.
4. Add the next actions as children or following siblings. Prepare their messages and trigger examples in the target language.

The action has the same name/description/enabled controls, Save behavior, permanent numbering, role permissions, and unsaved-draft protection as the other workflow actions. It can be nested under Branch/API/SQL paths or reached through Jump.

## English/French menu example

1. Configure English and French on the agent, with English as its default.
2. In the Main menu **Send message**, add an English translation with `Welcome. How can I help you?` and quick answers `French`, `English`, and `Help`. Add a French translation with `Bonjour. Comment puis-je vous aider ?` and quick answers `Français`, `English`, and `Aide`.
3. Under Main menu, add a **Message received** trigger called Choose French. Use example `French` in English and `Français` in French.
4. Under Choose French, add **Switch Language → French**, then a Send message with French translation `Langue changée en français.`, then Jump to Main menu.
5. Add Choose English with example `English` in both languages. Add **Switch Language → English**, an English confirmation `Language changed to English.`, and Jump to Main menu.
6. Add a Help trigger with English example `Help` and French example `Aide`. Give its response both translations, then Jump to Main menu.

Restart the tester in English and send `French`. Expect the French confirmation and French menu, including French quick replies. The tester's Language selector becomes French. Send `Aide` on the next turn; the French trigger example and French response are used. Send `English` to switch back. The execution trace shows the previous and selected languages.

## Runtime behavior

The action writes the existing conversation-level `language` state. Subsequent Send message actions select the matching translation, and subsequent turns match triggers in the saved language. The value is available to Branch and chat scripts as `language` and `system.language`, and to message/API/SQL templates as `{language}`. It is not an extra custom variable.

A survey after the switch uses the selected chat language and retains it when answering/resuming. Survey questions themselves are configured text; write the questions in the intended language. Jump uses the selected language at its destination. Generative fallback requests now explicitly include the active language in their system instruction. Actual model language adherence depends on the configured provider; this update does not add a provider or call one automatically.

Switching to the already active language is allowed. An explicit tester Language change can override the saved chat language on a later event. A new conversation uses the agent's default unless a language is explicitly supplied by the tester. Existing Set variable assignments to `language` remain supported.

Switch Language does **not** automatically translate authored messages, survey questions, or intent examples. Existing Send message behavior falls back to the agent's default/available translation if the selected one is missing. Add the relevant translations and trigger examples for the experience you want.

## Validation and data preservation

Workflow saves reject unsupported or unconfigured targets, including those in nested/disabled paths. Runtime checks configuration again and rejects an unavailable target without committing a partial language change. All changes in a failed turn roll back with that turn's messages and variables.

To remove an agent language, first update or remove Switch Language actions targeting it, including disabled actions. The same guard applies to restoring an older agent-settings version, so restoring settings cannot silently strand a saved language switch.

No new dependency or database migration is required by version 0.9.0. Schema head remains `0006`; existing accounts, settings, workflows, step numbers, and conversations are preserved. Keep your `.env` and restart the API and frontend after copying the updated source. If upgrading from before SQL Query, run `python -m alembic upgrade head` from backend as described in [DATABASE_CONNECTIONS.md](DATABASE_CONNECTIONS.md).

## API configuration

```json
{
  "type": "switch_language",
  "config": {"target_language": "fr"}
}
```

The value is the configured language **code**, such as `fr`, rather than its display name. Standard workflow-node fields still apply. The action uses ordinary `children`, not outcome paths. The tester returns the active language in its existing top-level `language` field and adds `previous_language` / `target_language` to this action's trace entry. No assistant message is created by the switch itself.

TEAMS.title: Teams settings
TEAMS.content:
# Teams settings

Open **Settings → Workspace → Teams** to create the support teams used by [Auto Team Match](AUTO_TEAM_MATCH.md). This section is functional; other unfinished settings sections remain marked Planned.

## Create or edit a team

1. Click **Create team**.
2. Enter a Name, for example `Bank of Tanzania`.
3. Optionally enter a Description explaining the team's purpose.
4. Enter Alternative names, one per line. For example, `BOT` and `Benki Kuu ya Tanzania`.
5. Click **Create**. Use a team's name or Edit button to reopen it and **Save** changes.

The table displays each team's name, alternatives, description, and edit/delete controls. Search includes names, alternatives, and descriptions. Reload retrieves the latest saved settings. Unsaved edits prompt before leaving; saving is protected against double submissions and conflicting revisions.

| Setting | Rules |
| --- | --- |
| Name | Required; 1–100 characters containing at least one letter or number. |
| Description | Optional; up to 2,000 characters. It is informational and not used as a matching alias. |
| Alternative names | Optional; up to 50 distinct names, each 1–100 characters containing letters or numbers. Add abbreviations and variations your customers use. |

Case and punctuation do not distinguish names. A team's name and alternatives must be distinct from each other and from every other active team's names/alternatives in the workspace. For example, `BOT` and `bot` conflict; use one entry. The backend serializes workspace mutations and rechecks collisions, even if two administrators edit concurrently.

Up to 200 active teams are supported. Deleting an unreferenced team archives its definition, excludes it from future matches, and retains earlier chat result snapshots. Teams referenced by a saved Live Agent Handoff cannot be deleted; team membership/deletion changes affecting pending or active live chats are protected. A new team with the same names receives a new ID. Renaming keeps its ID stable. Saved action definitions look up all current active teams rather than holding direct references to one team.

Workspace members can read teams. Changes require **Manage AI Agents** permission and CSRF protection, consistent with the existing custom-field/database settings. A team from another workspace cannot be read, changed, deleted, or matched. Settings changes are recorded in the existing audit log. Stale edits/deletes return 409 and require reloading.

Team definitions, aliases, and member selection are implemented here. Add colleagues in Settings → Workspace → Users, select them as team members, and have them save their availability/languages in Inbox. Live Agent Handoff and queue assignment are implemented; channel publishing remains future work. See [LIVE_AGENT_HANDOFF.md](LIVE_AGENT_HANDOFF.md).

## API

All endpoints are below `/api/workspaces/{workspace_id}/teams`.

| Method and suffix | Request / response |
| --- | --- |
| GET empty suffix | `{ "teams": [...], "can_manage": true }` |
| POST empty suffix | Create with `{ "name": "Bank of Tanzania", "description": "Central bank support", "alternative_names": ["BOT"] }`; returns 201 and the team. |
| POST `/{team_id}` | The same fields plus `expected_revision`; returns the updated team. No-op saves do not increment revision. |
| POST `/{team_id}/delete` | `{ "expected_revision": 1 }`; returns 204. |

Team responses include `id`, `name`, `description`, `alternative_names`, `revision`, `created_at`, and `updated_at`. No credentials or membership records are part of this schema. Apply migration **0011** before using member selection and live handoff; migration 0010 introduced the team definitions. Team create/update optionally accepts `member_ids` (up to 200 distinct workspace user UUIDs); omitted membership preserves existing members on update.

TEAMSPACE_SETTINGS.title: Teamspace settings and support tools — 0.24.0
TEAMSPACE_SETTINGS.content:
# Teamspace settings and support tools — 0.24.0

This release adds working settings for AI analysis, bans, chat assignment, canned replies, Inbox co-pilot, tags enforcement, ticket overdue rules, mandatory ticket fields, profile iFrames, custom analytics and exports. Inbox and Tickets gain record tools; People and Analytics are now usable destinations.

## Install on an existing workspace

Back up PostgreSQL and keep your existing backend `.env`. Replace application source, then run from `backend` with the project's virtual environment active:

```powershell
python -m alembic upgrade head
python -m alembic current
python -m uvicorn app.main:app --reload
```

The current revision is **0016**. `alembic upgrade` requires the revision argument (`head`). This is a source update plus a database migration; extracting the ZIP does not update the database. Restart the frontend and backend after upgrading. Migrations 0001–0015 remain unchanged. Requirements and frontend dependency pins are unchanged; Python 3.9.12 remains the source target. Existing AI agent creation/import stays unlimited.

Migration 0016 adds scoped operation settings, support people, ban rules/reasons/events, canned replies, record tags/groups, many-group tag membership, co-pilot knowledge and durable jobs. It extends ticket status with Overdue and fields with People scope, links native conversations/tickets to people, and retains existing workflow state, custom values, assignments and ticket history. Upgrades are repeatable. Downgrading to 0015 retains old records, maps Overdue to Open and newer assignment modes to Least busy, and removes the new feature data; back up first if intentionally downgrading.

## Teamspaces and permissions

Choose an accessible teamspace at the top of each new settings page. Each has independent View/Manage permissions. Manual analysis uses Trigger AI analysis; results require View AI analysis and access to the record. Workspace roles, Team roles and teamspace restrictions continue to apply. Existing custom roles receive no implicit new grants; configure them under Roles & permissions. Protected Admin and the owner retain full access.

Tags, field definitions and email configuration retain the shared workspace taxonomy introduced in earlier releases, managed from Default. Individual records have their own selected values and labels. Assignment, analysis, bans, canned replies, knowledge, overdue rules, enforcement and embed settings are stored per teamspace. A workspace's customer profile has a primary teamspace; People analysis uses conversations from that teamspace, with the requesting user's record access applied. Automatic People analysis runs in the closing chat's teamspace.

Native authenticated tester conversations identify the customer by account within the workspace. Unverified survey email/name is never used to merge identities. Authenticated incoming AI transfers receive separate conversation-bound identities because the existing transfer protocol does not provide a trusted shared customer identifier. Published anonymous customer channel adapters and mailbox synchronization remain separate work.

## AI analysis

Chats, Tickets and People have separate enable, automatic/manual, customer-message threshold, channel, sentiment, emotion, summary and prompt settings. Automatic analysis queues after closure/resolution. Thresholds count persisted customer-message rows, not text resembling a role label. Channel selections use the related conversation channel. People history is limited to the processing teamspace and the manual requester's authorized conversations.

Open Record tools on a chat, ticket or person and select Analyze. Results show the summary and enabled sentiment/emotion outputs with completion time. The latest completed analysis remains available after reload. Pending/Running/Completed/Failed jobs survive API restarts; expired worker leases can resume. Repeated request IDs do not duplicate jobs or interaction charges. Failed/unconfigured/invalid AI output is visible and is not billed as a completed analysis.

Set these optional server environment values for a self-hosted or other OpenAI-compatible chat-completions endpoint:

```dotenv
SUPPORT_AI_BASE_URL=
SUPPORT_AI_API_KEY=
SUPPORT_AI_MODEL=
SUPPORT_WORKER_ENABLED=true
SUPPORT_WORKER_INTERVAL=5
```

Use the endpoint's API base URL, e.g. the configured service's `/v1` URL; the application adds `/chat/completions`. The model is configured by the operator, not a hard-coded product selector. Conversation content is sent to that endpoint. The UI makes no claim that an external endpoint is Petrix-hosted or that no third party receives data. Keep credentials server-side. The API does not use a fabricated summary when no endpoint is configured.

Analysis and co-pilot use the weighted interaction ledger (`summaries` / `copilot`). Budget reservations include queued work; processing rechecks current access and balance. Optional Stripe product `limits` keys include `analysis_auto`, `analysis_manual`, `ban_rules`, `canned_replies`, `tags`, and `tag_groups`. Analysis monthly limits count completed and queued jobs at submission; failed jobs do not consume that limit. A self-hosted installation with no configured allowance remains unmetered, consistent with Workspace billing. No arbitrary commercial quota is invented.

## Bans and canned replies

Banning has Rules and Reasons tabs, create/edit drawers, selection and bulk delete. A rule maps the number of **previous** offences to minutes/hours/days/weeks/months/permanent; months mean 30 days. The highest matching threshold supplies the default, falling back to one hour without a rule. Reasons have a name and optional description; advanced reason options were not specified. Select a reason when banning from record tools. An override replaces the current ban and records another offence. Removing a ban retains offence history. Temporary bans expire automatically; active bans block customer and support replies, AI processing and claiming the affected conversation. Finite bans are bounded to ten years; use Permanent for longer bans.

Canned replies have a reference name, supported language code and reply text. Name/language are picker metadata. In Inbox, search by name/text, preview and insert. The inserted text is editable, and only Send reply sends it. Manage and View permissions are independent; configured plan quotas apply to creation.

## Chat assignment

Save Method, Limit and Priority independently. New methods apply after saving the method; old Manual/Round robin/Least busy installations preserve their previous behavior until then.

| Method | Selection | Configured billing plan |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Balanced | Fewest active chats, random ties | Starter+ |
| Random | Random eligible agent below capacity | Lite+ |
| Round robin | Rotate eligible agents ordered by when they came online | Pro+ |
| Balanced round robin | Fewest active chats, rotating ties | Pro+ |
| Voluntary | Pending until a live agent claims it; capacity ignored | Total+ |

Eligibility respects workflow-selected users/teams, optional language matching, an active support presence session and View/Manage own livechat grants (broader grants also qualify). Automatic queues drain when agents become available, send heartbeats or close chats, and during worker passes. Unavailable/full agents are skipped. Existing support presence expiry remains 90 seconds.

Select person tags or groups for priority. Priority is frozen at handoff and shown with a crown in the queue. Skip queue assigns priority chats first within capacity. Ignore assignment limit may exceed capacity for priority chats. Voluntary supports Skip queue only; switching from Ignore limit requires confirmation. Removing all configured priority tags/groups disables priority assignment. Editing a customer's tags later does not retroactively change a queued chat's priority.

## Tags, fields and closing requirements

A tag can belong to multiple groups. Record tools distinguish directly selected tags from tags inherited through groups and show group counts. Clearing a group removes its contribution; independently selected tags remain. Bulk Add tags preserves existing direct tags and groups. Filters support tags, applied groups and exact custom-field values.

Fields now have Conversation and People tabs. Category and type are immutable after creation; name, description, options and defaults can be edited while stable keys/IDs remain. Typed record editing supports text, number, boolean, date, dropdown and grouped selections. Inputs save on Enter or blur/Tab; selections save immediately. Conversation and ticket custom values remain independent, including Create Ticket's copy-and-override rules. People field and contact permissions are applied to details, filters, co-pilot profiles and exports.

Tags → Enforcement configures mandatory tagging, minimum effective tag count, and sorting. Closing/resolving a conversation or ticket checks the minimum. Tickets → Mandatory custom fields selects Conversation field definitions required before closing/resolving a ticket. Zero and False are valid values. Archived definitions/tags are not required or counted. A blocked close returns a visible validation error without changing status.

## Exports

Select visible records in Inbox, Tickets or People; choose Export, fields, optional individual custom fields, transcript (chats/tickets), timezone and whether to email a copy to your own account. Exports require Lite+ when billing is configured. CSV is UTF-8 with BOM, proper quoting, and spreadsheet formula protection. Dates use the selected IANA timezone. CSV tags contain **direct assignments only**; group-only tags are excluded.

Jobs and generated CSV bytes are persisted in PostgreSQL. Settings → Teamspace → Exports shows initiator, type, time and Pending/Running/Completed/Failed status, with page controls and Download. History and downloads enforce All/Teams/Own export download grants. Generation and download recheck access to every selected record and every People field. Losing a field permission prevents download of an older CSV containing it. An invalid/inaccessible record rejects the whole request. Select up to 5,000 records; generated CSVs are capped at 20 MiB.

Email copies use the existing SMTP configuration, only to the initiating account. Delivery intent is saved before SMTP and uncertain delivery is not automatically repeated. A CSV remains downloadable even when email delivery is unconfirmed. This does not create a general email campaign or import a mailbox.

## Inbox co-pilot and knowledge

Version 0.30.0 expands these controls; see [Inbox](INBOX.md). Data access can include the current conversation, the current person's authorised profile/history or broader authorised conversations. Broader access includes current access; mediation requires it. Record, teamspace and People-field permissions still apply.

Inbox now provides private Ask, Draft Reply, persistent Mediate, Enhance and Translate. Accept copies a suggestion into the editable reply without sending; Deny preserves the current draft. The Agent tab offers approved model selection and a personality prompt. Processing uses the administrator-configured endpoint, with its actual data-processing explanation.

Dedicated Copilot Knowledge accepts PDF/CSV/JSON and the previous TXT, Markdown, HTML and DOCX formats up to 5 MiB / 200,000 readable characters. Text-layer PDF extraction is supported; OCR is not added. Sources can be snippets, one public HTTPS page or a bounded same-origin crawl, with optional 1–90-day automatic retraining. The worker reports Pending/Loading/Success/Fail. Only successful sources are ranked into bounded excerpts; customer-agent Knowledge is separate.

Version 0.31.0 also adds six native [Analytics reports](ANALYTICS.md), measured agent activity and heatmaps. Custom analytics remains available alongside those reports. The reporting timezone is configured in Workspace General.

## Overdue tickets and embeds

Overdue rules apply after the selected number of days since the ticket's last update or note. Exclude weekends uses Africa/Nairobi business days. Resolved/closed tickets are excluded. The worker marks the ticket Overdue once, records an activity event, and applies the selected live agent and teams. With both selected, the live agent is primary and every selected team has record access within its permission/teamspace scope. Return the ticket to Open/In progress explicitly to restart follow-up timing.

Profile iFrames appear in People details when enabled and permitted. Custom analytics is an Enterprise feature displayed in Analytics → Custom. Both require a complete HTTP(S) URL without credentials. The browser uses a sandboxed frame with no referrer; it does not proxy arbitrary pages or guarantee that an external site permits embedding. External authentication is managed separately. Petrix credentials/customer fields are not appended to the URL.

## Worker operation

The API starts the support worker outside test mode by default. It processes pending jobs, automatic ticket overdue checks and assignment queues. For a separate worker process, disable the API worker and run from backend:

```powershell
python -m app.teamspace.worker --watch
```

Without `--watch`, this runs one maintenance pass and one job. Database row locks and leases coordinate job claims. Only a completed result writes one usage event; request/lease IDs guard retries. Provider failures are saved on jobs, and maintenance errors produce a safe operator log message. The code does not change your local database or start external services merely by downloading the ZIP.

TEST_BOT.title: Workflow + PDF Test Bot
TEST_BOT.content:
# Workflow + PDF Test Bot

Import `examples/workflow-pdf-test-bot.petrix.json` under AI agents → Create AI agent → Import. Use Petrix AI **0.26.1 or later**. The file includes agent settings, saved workflows and one embedded PDF; you do not need to upload the PDF separately. Earlier releases import settings only and cannot load this complete bundle. For the current 0.27.0 app, update the source, apply migration 0019 with `python -m alembic upgrade head` from backend, and restart both services. The portable import feature itself adds no dependency or extra migration. Keep your existing `backend/.env`, virtual environment and database. The portable import feature adds no migration; current app schema head is 0019.

After import, select **Workflow + PDF Test Bot**, open **Knowledge**, and confirm **KCB M-PESA test FAQ** is Ready. Open the tester and start a fresh conversation. LLM must be on, with a valid existing `GROQ_API_KEY` in `backend/.env` and the configured `GROQ_INTENT_MODEL` available. Restart the backend after changing its environment. The PDF action uses the existing Groq LLM Processing connection; it does not need a separate `LLM_BASE_URL` connection or semantic embeddings. Specific workflow commands run without a model connection.

| Send this | Expected behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `Contact support` | Exact workflow reply containing fictional `support@example.invalid`. No model call. |
| `Log demo complaint` | A two-question survey. Enter a made-up name and fictitious issue; confirmation includes `DEMO-1001`. No ticket or email is created. |
| `What is KCB M-PESA?` | PDF-backed LLM Processing replies: “KCB M-PESA is a loans and savings product exclusively offered by KCB Bank Kenya Ltd to Safaricom M-PESA customers.” |
| `What is the document verification code?` | PDF-backed reply includes `KB-KCB-7214`. This marker exists only inside the PDF, not in persona/workflow text. |
| `What is the loan interest rate?` | Prompted response: `The test PDF does not contain that information.` The document contains no rates. |

The first two commands are deliberately exact matches. Other questions run **Fallback → Answer from the uploaded PDF** (`Use Knowledge info` enabled, `{last_message}` input, Text output, temperature 0) → **Send PDF answer**. There is no catch-all “Other questions” intent to intercept questions before Knowledge retrieval. In the trace, the question should show `matching.method: fallback`, `llm_processing` with `knowledge_sources: 1`, then Send message. If the model is unconfigured/unavailable or times out, a separate workflow path explains the failure. Inspect the trace for the specific error.

A multi-question survey retains control until its fields are answered. Finish it or restart the tester before testing the PDF. The model generates PDF answers; exact wording can vary with the configured provider. Automated verification uses a controlled model to confirm that the actual extracted PDF is supplied and that matching/continuations select the intended paths. No live provider answer is claimed as verified.

The PDF is a controlled test fixture. Its definition was supplied in this conversation; it is not an official bank publication. The verification code is test metadata. No real personal details, credentials, banking rates, account access, external endpoint or customer messaging are part of this bot. Import creates a separate agent and retains unlimited agent creation/import.

TICKETS.title: Workspace Tickets — 0.28.0
TICKETS.content:
# Workspace Tickets — 0.28.0

Tickets is the human email support repository. The dashboard provides a horizontally scrollable table, selection, search, filters, pagination and creation. Inbox has Livechats and Tickets views and uses the same ticket editor and four detail tabs. `PTX-000001` is the stable workspace short ID; the UUID is the full ticket ID.

## Upgrade

Keep the existing database, `backend/.env` and virtual environment. Stop the old API, replace the source, and run from `backend`:

```powershell
python -m alembic upgrade head
```

This applies migration **0020**. Restart the API and Angular. No new dependencies are required over 0.27.0. Migration 0020 adds ticket teamspace/team/sender and creation-request fields, revisioned private-note colours, CC and delivery receipt fields, incoming email records and an idempotent mail-event ledger. Existing ticket/chat IDs, workflow actions, custom-field snapshots, aliases, email contents and history remain. Migrations 0001–0019 are unchanged. The default sender uses the existing `SMTP_FROM`; development uses Mailpit. Production SMTP still needs the operator’s working sender configuration.

## Create and reply

Create Ticket is available on Tickets, the Inbox queue’s add button, and the selected livechat’s header. Enter a subject, sender, optional live agent and teams, and select a visible registered person or register a person by email. Select a teamspace when creating an unlinked case. Linked cases keep their chat’s teamspace and copy its conversation fields. Explicit API values override the copied values; the workflow Create Ticket action retains its existing copy-and-override behaviour.

Creation saves the case without sending an email. It opens the ticket editor where the live agent writes and sends the first message. Sender addresses are either the server’s default support mailbox or an enabled DNS-verified Email Domain. A sender change affects future messages. Prepared messages keep their original sender/content/persona.

The editor supports the user’s current alias and ticket signature, optional CC addresses (up to 20), and Send. Takeover & Send is available to agents with transfer permission when the ticket is not assigned to them. Takeover assigns the sender atomically with preparing the email. Repeated requests with the same request ID do not send a second copy; changing the content of a used request ID returns 409. Resolved/Closed cases must be reopened before another outbound reply. An active person ban blocks outbound replies.

Email bodies are displayed as text; pasted markup is escaped. CC is included in the actual SMTP recipient list by the standard mail transport. A partially refused SMTP recipient set is treated as unconfirmed to avoid silently replaying mail already accepted for another recipient. Incoming replies are only available when the optional mail adapter below is connected. Tickets do not run an AI workflow to answer incoming mail.

## Detail tabs

| Tab | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| Assignment | Live agent, multiple teams, person and email. Saving assignment requires transfer permission. Transfers replace the earlier team audience. |
| Details | Full ID, short ID, first email’s creator, editable description, status, created time, future sender and linked conversation. Before any email is sent, creator reads “No email sent.” |
| AI Analysis | Summary/sentiment using the existing Teamspace analysis job and configured provider. Resolve or close the case first. Analysis settings, grants and interaction limits still apply. |
| Notes & Tags | Add/edit/delete/colour staff notes, assign tags/groups, edit conversation custom fields and view activity. Note edits/deletion require the current note revision. |

Statuses are Open, Pending, Overdue, Resolved and Closed. Pending maps to the existing persisted `in_progress` value; older API clients remain compatible. Existing overdue, mandatory-field and tagging enforcement still applies. Closing a ticket does not close the linked livechat or fire its Chat Closed workflow.

Private notes never enter customer emails or customer conversation exports. They are also excluded from AI email-thread analysis. Assignee notifications are separate from the customer thread. Unsaved email, note, assignment, description and field changes have navigation guards; switching Inbox views retains an unsent livechat reply.

## Find and select tickets

Search accepts at most **256 characters** and rejects longer API requests. It searches full ID, short ID, subject, name, email and phone; `%` and `_` are literal characters. The table defaults to 40 rows, with 20/40/60/100 choices. Counts refer to the complete visible filtered selection.

| Filter | Selection |
| --- | --- |
| Live agent | Assigned live agent |
| Team | Any explicitly assigned team |
| Custom fields | An active conversation field and value, including grouped options |
| Created by | The person/live agent who sent the first email, or workflow origin |
| Email sending status | Latest customer outbound message status |
| Tags | Effective assigned tag |
| Tag groups | Direct group or a group represented by an assigned tag |
| Status | Open, Pending, Overdue, Resolved, Closed |
| Created on | Today, current week/month, or an inclusive custom date range in the browser timezone |

| Email sending status | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Pending | No outgoing message yet, or a committed queued item |
| Sending | An SMTP attempt is in progress |
| Sent | SMTP accepted the email; inbox delivery is not yet confirmed |
| Failed to send | An explicit failure or unconfirmed attempt; review the message’s error |
| Delivered | A signed delivery event from the configured provider adapter |
| Failed to deliver | A signed bounce event from the configured provider adapter |

An in-flight marker older than two minutes is displayed as unconfirmed and requires review before retrying. There is no automatic retry of failed/unconfirmed sends. Check SMTP logs before confirming a retry, because Message-ID does not guarantee recipient deduplication. Each saved outgoing item allows at most five attempts. Queue draining remains available through `python -m app.tickets.deliver --limit 100`.

## Export, delete and permissions

Select rows and choose Export to configure fields, timezone, optional transcript and optional account email. Exports use the existing durable jobs and Settings → Teamspace → Exports downloads. Plan limits, export grants and current download grants are enforced again when processing/downloading. Customer transcripts include sent customer messages and received emails, not private notes or assignee notifications.

Delete Tickets asks for confirmation and validates the whole selection and revisions before removing anything. A current SMTP send blocks deletion. Ticket email/note history, per-record aliases and labels are removed; linked chats and registered people remain. Related stored exports/analysis are invalidated. Previously consumed email interactions survive deletion as text-free accounting records. Deleted incoming message IDs remain deduplicated.

View, manage, transfer, export and download grants retain their own/team/all scopes and teamspace restrictions. List/detail, people lookup, notes, replies, transfers, exports and deletion check the relevant scope. Assignment does not grant AI-agent ownership, and AI-agent permissions do not replace custom ticket grants.

Each outgoing email accepted by SMTP and each ingested incoming email consumes **one interaction unit**. CC recipients do not create extra ticket email records. Idempotent retries of the same event do not count again. A delivery receipt does not add a second interaction, and a later bounce does not refund an already sent email. Weighted usage follows the existing workspace usage configuration.

## Optional incoming-mail and delivery adapter

This is a normalized integration contract, not an automatic IMAP connection. The operator’s adapter must verify the mail provider’s own webhook/authentication, normalize the event and sign the following request. The endpoint is disabled until a separate random `TICKET_MAIL_WEBHOOK_SECRET` of at least 32 characters is configured. Do not expose that secret in a browser or reuse a session secret.

`POST /api/ticket-mail/{workspace_id}` accepts JSON with:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `event_id` | Stable provider event identity, maximum 200 characters |
| `type` | `incoming`, `delivered`, or `bounced` |
| `occurred_at` | ISO date/time including timezone |
| `message_id` | Incoming email’s Message-ID, or the stored outgoing Message-ID for a receipt |
| `ticket_id` | Optional explicit ticket UUID |
| `in_reply_to` | Incoming reply’s referenced outgoing Message-ID |
| `from_email`, `to_email` | Required incoming sender and configured support recipient |
| `subject`, `name`, `content` | Incoming subject/name/plain text body; content is required, up to 48,000 characters |
| `teamspace_id` | Optional teamspace for a new unthreaded incoming case |

Example incoming reply:

```json
{
  "event_id": "provider-event-123",
  "type": "incoming",
  "occurred_at": "2026-11-18T15:00:00+03:00",
  "message_id": "<customer-reply-123@example.com>",
  "in_reply_to": "<reply-OUTBOX_UUID@your-support-domain.example>",
  "from_email": "customer@example.com",
  "to_email": "support@your-support-domain.example",
  "subject": "Re: Support request",
  "content": "Thank you. I still need help."
}
```

Send the integer Unix timestamp as `X-Petrix-Mail-Timestamp`. `X-Petrix-Mail-Signature` is the lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 using the configured secret over **timestamp bytes + `.` + the exact raw JSON bytes**. The timestamp must be within five minutes; the body limit is 256 KiB. Header fields reject control characters and unknown fields are rejected.

A reply resolves by `in_reply_to` or explicit ticket ID and must come from the customer or a previous sent CC participant. The recipient must be the current configured default sender or a currently enabled verified Email Domain. New unthreaded mail creates an email-origin case without an AI response or outbound notification. Accepted replies reopen Resolved/Closed cases. Event retries and repeated incoming Message-IDs count once. Reusing an event ID with changed contents returns 409.

Receipts resolve a stored outgoing Message-ID within the workspace. New outgoing IDs are unique across cases. If an old installation contains duplicate Message-IDs, include the matching ticket ID; ambiguous requests return 409. Only a newer receipt changes delivery state. SMTP acceptance never produces Delivered by itself. No receipt/incoming event is fabricated by the UI. Provider-specific adapters, attachment ingestion, IMAP polling and external helpdesk synchronization are not bundled.

WEBCHAT.title: Publish → Webchat — 0.34.1
WEBCHAT.content:
# Publish → Webchat — 0.34.1

Webchat is Petrix AI's website popup. It is available on every plan, without an additional channel charge. Website visitors have isolated sessions and can run workflows, ask questions grounded in trained Knowledge, complete surveys, upload files and continue with live support in Inbox. Model/provider usage still uses the installation's configured connections and existing usage accounting.

## Configure and preview

Open **AI agents → Publish → Add Channel** to create Webchat, or open a channel in the table. Channels start disabled. Viewing and changing channels use the existing View/Manage AI Agents permissions, workspace membership and teamspace restrictions. Changes require CSRF and the current revision. Other Publish channel types remain separate future work.

The editor includes seven sections and a live design panel with Welcome, Chat, Proactive, Pre-chat and Widget screens. The design panel updates while editing. **Preview** opens a separate sandbox using the current draft settings, including an otherwise disabled channel. The preview link expires after 30 minutes; it does not enable or deploy a channel. Preview conversations are marked `tester` and appear with Test conversations rather than ordinary published traffic. The popup preview runs the saved workflows when you interact with it; use the live design panel to review appearance without starting a workflow.

| Section | Controls |
| --- | --- |
| Setup | Internal name, configured agent language, Inbox channel icon, attachments, emojis, hide when live agents are offline, human-message ranking, inactivity timeout, audio, voice and playback |
| Appearance | Optional welcome screen/title/description/start button, chat name/status, left/right placement, popup size, border radius, colours and normalized agent/launcher images |
| Proactive messages | Enabled messages, order, time on page, include/exclude page rules, messages, quick replies, colours and JavaScript trigger ID |
| Multichannel widget | Webchat plus ordered links to configured HTTPS, email and phone support destinations |
| Pre-chat form | Optional introduction/button, standard Name/Email/Phone and explicitly selected active People custom fields, labels, placeholders, required flags and order |
| Mobile | Breakpoint, fullscreen popup, hide entirely, or custom viewport percentages |
| Installation | Channel ID, copyable embed snippet and exact-origin website whitelist |

The multichannel section links to already available support destinations. It does not create WhatsApp, Facebook or email-channel integrations. People fields become public form definitions only when explicitly selected by a channel manager. Other CRM fields, internal notes, workflow variables, matching traces, prompts and provider settings are excluded from visitor responses. A visitor email is contact information, not authentication; records are not automatically merged by email.

**Save & publish** saves enabled channel settings and captures the current saved agent configuration and workflow document. **Save** on a disabled channel stores its settings without enabling it. The list's Enabled switch enables/disables the saved configuration. Saving a draft workflow alone does not alter the published copy. New chats use the newly published copy; existing chats retain their captured agent/workflow revision, including pending surveys and handoff return paths. Ready Knowledge remains retrieved from the agent's currently trained sources, allowing corrected sources to be used without copying private documents into the channel.

## Website installation

Keep the existing database and `.env`. Run from `backend`:

```bash
python -m alembic upgrade head
```

Restart the API and frontend. Migration **0027** adds a durable per-conversation message sequence; 0026 introduced six Webchat tables and three backward-compatible agent voice-input preferences. Migrations 0001–0026 and dependency pins are unchanged in this patch. The API's existing Docker image includes the widget assets automatically. The frontend Nginx configuration allows the public iframe route to supply its own framing policy and supports uploads up to the existing 20 MiB batch limit plus multipart overhead.

For a real external website, configure **API_BASE_URL** in `backend/.env` to the publicly reachable HTTPS API origin, then restart. `localhost:8000` is suitable only when the visitor's own machine runs this API. A website served over HTTPS must load the script/frame over HTTPS as well. Keep **FRONTEND_ORIGIN** set to the actual staff dashboard origin. The embed snippet shown by Installation uses API_BASE_URL; it never uses Proto's embed service.

Copy the exact script from Installation and insert it before `</body>` on each website page. Its structure is:

```html
<script src="https://YOUR-PETRIX-API/api/webchat/embed.js"
        data-channel="YOUR-WEBCHAT-UUID" defer></script>
```

The loader creates one isolated iframe and a launcher. Including the same channel script twice does not create two widgets. Website CSS does not style inside the frame. If the website has a Content Security Policy, permit the API origin in `script-src` and `frame-src`; microphone use also requires the website's Permissions Policy to allow the frame. No staff authentication cookie or private provider key belongs in the snippet.
