Enable whitelisting to approve exact origins such as `https://example.com` and `https://www.example.com`, separately. Schemes, subdomains and non-default ports matter. Paths and wildcard origins are rejected. The frame's `frame-ancestors` policy enforces approved browser embedding, and visitor sessions remain bound to their original website. Disabling a channel or removing its approved origin blocks existing visitor API access too. Domain checks control embedding; visitor capabilities protect conversation privacy. An origin whitelist is not a substitute for authenticating a visitor's real-world identity.

## Visitor conversations and Inbox

Your message appears immediately while the request is sending, followed by the bot replies in workflow order, as in Agent tester. Confirmed messages use a database-assigned per-conversation sequence for sending, polling, refresh and history pagination; timestamps are for display. The upgrade keeps saved message IDs, text and times. For historical messages with identical times, customer input is placed before the tied bot responses; the exact order among multiple old tied responses was not recorded and cannot be reconstructed reliably.

The widget generates a random capability per channel, website origin and browser storage context. Only its hash is stored on the server. The capability is sent in an Authorization header, never in file URLs or staff cookies. Sessions last up to 30 days; browsers that block storage retain the current session in memory and cannot promise cross-refresh history. A parent-origin handshake completes before the frame resumes stored history.

The welcome page shows this visitor's previous conversations. **Start New Chat** starts a separate conversation and applies the configured pre-chat form first. Name, email, phone and validated People custom values are saved on the visitor's CRM record. Public history and message pages are bounded and support loading earlier records. A fresh browser/session cannot read a previous visitor's records. The widget offers a fresh session when an old one expires.

Published traffic uses `webchat`, so existing Inbox, People and Analytics channels recognize it. A Live Agent Handoff workflow queues the same conversation for eligible staff. The visitor sees subsequent human replies and can continue sending text/files. Private staff notes are excluded. Optional thumbs-up/down ranking applies only to human messages in that visitor's conversation. The configured channel icon/name are visible in Inbox to staff with the record's permission. User-facing original files require the same visitor capability and must belong to a public message in that conversation.

Text events and starts use persisted request IDs. Duplicate delivery does not repeat a completed workflow. An uncertain/running request is not blindly replayed; refresh/reconcile before a new send. The request ledger survives commits made by external workflow actions. It cannot make an arbitrary remote API's side effects transactional or prove whether an interrupted external operation happened. Failed turns retain their conversation for review. Per-visitor and per-address limits bound starts/uploads/events; operators can also apply their usual edge rate controls.

Attachments use native conversation storage: up to 10 files, 10 MiB each and 20 MiB total. Survey file questions keep their own single/multiple-file rules and answer tokens. Attachments and audio respect channel toggles, and all public mutations recheck channel/session scope. Existing bans apply to visitor messages and new chats. Published-channel inactivity closure is evaluated by a durable API background worker, even when a visitor closes the popup. Polling also checks the same timeout. Preview timeouts are evaluated while their preview is active. Disable `WEBCHAT_WORKER_ENABLED` when running a separate `python -m app.webchat.worker --watch` process. Request receipts fence concurrent timeout attempts and prevent replay after an interrupted external action.

## Workflow and Knowledge testing

Publishing does not change intent priority. A matched fixed Send message still controls that reply. PDF answers require a route that reaches Knowledge/LLM Processing or the generative fallback, trained sources and a working model. The included `examples/workflow-pdf-test-bot.petrix.json` can be imported as a new agent and published as Webchat. It contains workflow branches and an embedded Knowledge PDF. Its KCB M-PESA question is tested through the public visitor API and real embedded UI with a controlled model fixture.

## Proactive messages and JavaScript API

Time-on-page messages are evaluated against the current page. `*` matches all pages, `/solutions/*` includes a path and `!/solutions/government` excludes it. Exclusions win. Triggering a message opens a small bubble before the visitor starts a chat; it does not silently start a billed conversation or send an email. Required pre-chat fields still apply before a quick reply starts a real conversation.

The installation exposes:

```javascript
window.PetrixWebchat.open();
window.PetrixWebchat.close();
window.PetrixWebchat.toggle();
window.PetrixWebchat.proactive("PROACTIVE-MESSAGE-UUID");
```

The message ID is available on its card. API-only cards skip the timer. Page rules and enabled flags still apply. Communication uses validated frame source, origin and channel ID; no page JavaScript receives the visitor capability. Only the configured channel's own frame can resize its loader.

## Voice, audio and playback

The agent's **Voice** tab now exposes **Speech-to-text**, selected speech languages, **Text-to-speech** and **Include audio transcript**, alongside voice name and speed. Existing saved voice-enabled preferences remain the text-to-speech setting. Speech-to-text defaults off after upgrade and must be intentionally enabled. The selected speech languages must belong to the agent's configured languages.

Webchat **Voice conversations** requires both agent speech settings. **Audio messaging** requires speech-to-text but is independent of voice conversations. Message playback requires text-to-speech. These are browser speech and recording services, not a bundled cloud speech provider: actual availability, voices, language accuracy and possible processing by the browser vendor depend on the browser and its permissions.

Selecting **Voice** immediately requests microphone access. Recognition ends the person's turn after its normal pause detection, sends plain transcript text through the ordinary workflow, plays the AI's textual reply, then resumes listening. The waveform is driven by microphone analysis and Listening/Thinking/Speaking states describe the current step. The language picker uses the published speech languages and is disabled while requesting access. Closing the widget or switching back to Chat releases the microphone and stops speech. A live handoff returns to Chat automatically; Voice is disabled while human support handles it. Unsupported browsers and denied permissions receive an explanation.

Ordinary audio messaging records a playable clip, up to 60 seconds, with a stop/send control. If the browser supplies a transcript and Include audio transcript is enabled, it is retained with that clip. Clips without a browser transcript are still delivered as native attachment events; no server OCR or audio transcription service is invented. Voice-conversation turns always appear as plain transcript messages, independently of the ordinary clip transcript preference. The sandbox embeds the same standard popup; no separate Showcase experience is introduced.

## API map

Management paths are relative to `/api/workspaces/{workspace_id}/agents/{agent_id}/webchat` and require the staff session, existing grants and CSRF for changes.

| Method | Path | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET / POST | empty path | List channels/options / idempotent disabled channel creation |
| POST | `/{channel}` | Revision-checked configuration and published snapshot |
| POST | `/{channel}/preview` | Short-lived draft sandbox URL |
| POST | `/{channel}/delete` | Confirmed removal; customer conversation records remain |
| POST / GET | `/assets` / `/assets/{id}` | Normalize image upload / staff image view |

Public routes are under `/api/webchat`. The loader, frame and explicitly published branding are public; visitor records require the channel-scoped Bearer capability. Public routes do not authorize staff APIs or use their cookies.

| Method | Path | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/embed.js`, `/widget.js`, `/widget.css` | Native widget assets |
| GET | `/{channel}/frame`, `/{channel}/demo`, `/{channel}/config` | Framed popup, sandbox and approved public configuration |
| POST | `/{channel}/sessions` | Initialize/reconcile visitor capability |
| GET / POST | `/{channel}/conversations` | Private visitor history / validated pre-chat start |
| GET | `/{channel}/conversations/{id}` | Public-only messages and earlier-page cursor |
| POST | `/{channel}/conversations/{id}/events` | Idempotent text, closure or feedback |
| POST | `/{channel}/conversations/{id}/poll` | Human reply updates and active timeout evaluation |
| POST | `/{channel}/conversations/{id}/attachments` | Bounded file/survey/audio delivery |
| GET | `/{channel}/conversations/{id}/files/{file}` | Scoped delivered original bytes |
| POST | `/{channel}/conversations/{id}/messages/{message}/rating` | Visitor ranking of a human reply |
| GET | `/{channel}/requests/{request}` | Reconcile this visitor's request status |

## Validation scope

Backend tests exercise actual PostgreSQL migrations and public HTTP routes, isolation, revisions, whitelisting, previews, pre-chat validation, bans, timeout, attachment delivery and PDF/workflow/human-support integration. Browser checks use a separate anonymous website origin. Speech recognition/playback and the microphone are controlled fixtures in automated checks; physical microphone behavior and real browser/vendor speech quality require testing on the intended deployment browser. No external website is deployed by generating this ZIP.

WHATSAPP.title: Publish → WhatsApp — 0.35.0
WHATSAPP.content:
# Publish → WhatsApp — 0.35.0

Publish a saved Petrix AI agent on a WhatsApp Business number. Incoming customer messages run the same saved workflows, intent routing and configured Knowledge/model processing as Agent Tester. A Human Handoff action sends the conversation to the native Inbox, where authorised agents can reply and attach files. People records and interaction accounting remain native to Petrix.

## Requirements and availability

WhatsApp publishing requires **Lite or above**. Channel creation, configuration and read-only connection verification are available for preparation on Starter; enabling, incoming message processing and outgoing delivery enforce the plan requirement. This does not purchase or change a subscription.

You need a Meta Developer app with WhatsApp, a Meta Business portfolio, a WhatsApp Business account and a registered/verified business phone number. Configure a publicly reachable HTTPS `API_BASE_URL` on your Petrix server. A localhost callback cannot receive Meta events. Keep `SESSION_SIGNING_SECRET` stable: it protects the stored channel credentials and generated verify tokens. A restored database requires its original signing secret.

## Create or open a channel

1. Open **AI agents → Publish → Add Channel**.
2. Choose **WhatsApp**, enter an internal name and select **Create WhatsApp**. New channels start disabled.
3. Open the channel from the shared Webchat/WhatsApp table. Expand **Basics**, **Configuration**, **Webhook**, **Setup** or **Activity**.

View and Manage AI agent permissions are checked independently, together with workspace/teamspace access. Changing a channel requires Manage and CSRF protection. Viewing settings never reveals Meta credentials or the Petrix verify token.

## Basics

Set the internal **Name**, a **Default chat language** from the agent's configured languages, and an optional **Icon** displayed to live agents in Inbox. Upload PNG, JPEG or GIF up to 10 MiB; the server normalizes the image. **Auto-close chat on timeout** runs the saved Chat timeout workflow without requiring an open browser. Select **Save**, or **Save & publish** when enabled.

Saving captures the agent settings and workflow document that are currently saved. Existing conversations retain their captured version; new conversations use the latest publication. Saving an Agent Tester workflow alone does not republish a channel.

## Configuration: connect Meta

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| App ID | Numeric Meta app ID from the app's settings. |
| App secret | Meta app secret used to authenticate webhook message signatures. |
| User access token | A system user token assigned to the app and relevant WhatsApp assets. |
| Phone number ID | Numeric WhatsApp Business phone number ID from the app's WhatsApp API setup. This is not the phone number itself. |

In Meta Business settings, select the appropriate portfolio, open **Users → System users**, create/select an authorised system user, and assign the app and relevant WhatsApp assets. Generate a token for that app with `whatsapp_business_messaging` and `whatsapp_business_management`. Add `business_management` where your account/asset administration requires it. Token lifetimes, asset permissions and available account controls are managed by Meta; confirm them in its current guide.

Select **Save connection**, then **Save & verify**. Verification checks token validity, owning app, required WhatsApp scopes, expiry and access to the specified phone number; it does not send a customer message. The channel displays the returned business name/number on success or a safe provider error on failure. Both secrets are encrypted at rest and write-only; leave their fields blank to retain saved values. Credential/phone changes disable the channel and invalidate connection verification. Current default Graph API version is `v27.0`, configurable server-side through `WHATSAPP_GRAPH_VERSION`.

## Webhook and Setup

**Configuration App ID/App secret** belong to Meta. **Setup App ID** identifies the Petrix channel; **Setup App secret / Verify token** is a separately generated Petrix secret used for Meta's callback handshake. Do not use the Meta app secret as the callback verify token.

1. Save your connection so **Webhook** displays its URL.
2. In Meta App → WhatsApp → Configuration, edit the webhook callback.
3. Paste the **Webhook URL** into **Callback URL**.
4. In Petrix **Setup**, select **Reveal verify token** and copy the token into Meta's **Verify Token**.
5. Select Meta's **Verify and Save**. Subscribe to the **messages** field to receive customer messages and delivery updates.
6. Return to Petrix and select **Refresh status**. Once connection and callback checks succeed, enable WhatsApp in Basics and select **Save & publish**.

The public GET callback validates Meta's challenge against the generated token. POST callbacks require `X-Hub-Signature-256`, computed using the Meta app secret and exact raw body. Invalid signatures are rejected before accepting events. Channels on one Meta app share a callback URL; signed events route by their own Phone number ID, which cannot be assigned to two Petrix channels.

**Reissue** creates a new Petrix verify token, invalidates the old token and disables the channel. Update/verify it in Meta and enable again. It does not rotate your Meta app secret or access token. A recorded callback handshake is not evidence that the messages subscription has been enabled; check that setting in Meta.

## Messaging, files and human handoff

Save the business number in your WhatsApp contacts and send a message. Phone-number and business-scoped user ID (BSUID) identities are supported, including customers who share only a BSUID. The server creates isolated native People/conversation records; supplied contact information is not used to merge separate customers. Duplicate Meta message IDs are processed once. New customer messages and bot replies retain the durable ordering introduced in 0.34.1.

Text, native buttons/lists and sequential typed survey answers are supported. Old survey/feedback buttons cannot answer a later question. Incoming images, documents, audio, videos and stickers are downloaded only from validated Meta media locations, with a **10 MiB incoming file cap**, then stored as native private attachments. Audio is retained as a file; this channel does not transcribe WhatsApp audio or provide voice calls. One WhatsApp media message supplies one survey file; use separate survey fields for separate requested documents.

Native outgoing files are uploaded to Meta and delivered as messages. The channel caps images at 5 MiB, audio/video at 16 MiB and other native files at the existing 20 MiB Petrix cap; Meta may reject unsupported formats. Graphs and carousels use readable text/link/media fallbacks rather than web-only interactive displays. Internal notes, workflow traces and private CRM variables are never sent by the channel renderer. CSAT is collected through sequential rating/text/choice questions and the saved one-use feedback token.

Human Handoff uses the existing team routing, availability and claim/takeover permissions. New customer messages and files reach the live conversation; Inbox replies queue native WhatsApp deliveries. Channel name/icon and delivery status are visible to staff. Bans and the WhatsApp service window are checked before accepting a staff reply.

## Delivery activity and recovery

The server persists incoming events before acknowledging the webhook and processes them in order per recipient. It creates an ordered outbox for bot and staff replies. Accepted API sends show **Sent**; only signed Meta statuses mark them **Delivered** or **Read**. Status callbacks cannot downgrade a read message to sent. The API worker runs automatically, or can run separately with `python -m app.whatsapp.worker --watch` from `backend` (set `WHATSAPP_WORKER_ENABLED=false` in the API process when running a separate worker).

Open **Activity** to inspect incoming and outgoing statuses with pagination. Known failed/blocked outgoing messages can be retried after correcting the cause and while the service window is open. Retry preserves already sent parts. An interrupted/unknown send becomes **Uncertain** and is not automatically replayed; a signed Meta status can reconcile it. Review the conversation in Inbox and Meta before cancelling unconfirmed parts or sending a fresh reply. Cancellation cannot recall a message accepted by Meta. Interrupted workflow processing blocks later events for that recipient; review its effects, then **Dismiss** it to continue without replaying external actions. Future customer messages can still be accepted into the durable queue.

Deleting a channel requires confirmation. It stops routing and removes its credentials/transport queue, while retaining native People and conversation history.

## Service window, opt-in and pricing

A customer message opens/resets a **24-hour customer service window**. This release sends normal agent/live-agent replies only within that window. Outside it, wait for another customer message or use an approved template through your WhatsApp business tools. This channel does not implement template creation, template campaigns or bulk outreach. Obtain the person's opt-in before business-initiated messages and follow Meta's business/messaging policies.

Meta manages charges and messaging limits separately from Petrix. Current Cloud API pricing is based on delivered messages and applicable message categories, regions and free-service conditions. The former claim about a universal allowance of 1,000 free conversations is not used here. Consult current Meta pricing for rates and conditions, including conditions for AI business solutions; no Meta pricing is hardcoded into this release.

Official references checked 19 November 2026:

- [WhatsApp Cloud API overview](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/overview)
- [Access tokens and system users](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/access-tokens/)
- [Webhook endpoint verification and signatures](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/webhooks/create-webhook-endpoint/)
- [Sending messages and service windows](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/messages/send-messages)
- [BSUID recipient identities](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/business-scoped-user-ids)
- [Current pricing](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/pricing/)

## Upgrade

Keep the existing database and `.env`. From `backend`, run `python -m alembic upgrade head`, then restart the API and frontend. Additive **0028** introduces five WhatsApp tables; the schema now has **92 tables**. Earlier 0001–0027 migrations and dependency pins remain unchanged. The full ZIP retains all prior modules, unlimited agent creation/import, Analytics scrolling and the Webchat 0.34.1 ordering correction.

No real Meta account or phone is connected by installing this update. Live operation requires your own credentials, publicly reachable callback, Meta verification/subscription and eligible plan. Release tests use signed HTTP and controlled Meta fixtures, not real WhatsApp recipients.

WORKFLOWS.title: Petrix AI — Workflows and LLM Processing
WORKFLOWS.content:
# Petrix AI — Workflows and LLM Processing

Milestone 3 implements the workflow builder, its persistence and runtime, and Send message. The next update adds Set variable with typed session data and message placeholders; see [SET_VARIABLE.md](SET_VARIABLE.md). Other action types have individual reserved backend folders and remain unavailable until their configuration and handlers are implemented.

Version `0.4.0` adds layered intent matching. Follow [INTENT_MATCHING.md](INTENT_MATCHING.md) to install the new dependencies, add the Groq key, and prepare local embeddings before using the additional stages.

Version `0.4.1` implements Jump. Select an existing trigger or action from the searchable numbered tree picker, then Save. The runtime leaves the source branch and resumes at the destination, including its nested waits and enclosing action continuations. Targets use UUIDs so renaming and reordering keep references intact. See [JUMP.md](JUMP.md). No new migration or dependency is required.

Version `0.5.0` adds Ask survey and real file answers. See [ASK_SURVEY.md](ASK_SURVEY.md). It uses migration `0005` to store uploaded bytes with their conversation; existing workflow definitions, numbers, and data are retained.


Version `0.6.0` adds **Branch** with up to 10 ordered Python conditions, separate action paths, Else, survey `.text` / `.norm.value` views, nested waits, and path-aware Jump targets. See [BRANCH.md](BRANCH.md) for configuration and continuation rules. No new dependency or migration is required; that release used schema head `0005`.

Version `0.7.0` adds **Send API**: GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, and DELETE over HTTPS, configurable headers, JSON or Python payloads, response variables, and separate Success/Error/Timeout paths. See [Send API](SEND_API.md). Existing dependencies and migrations are unchanged; that release used schema head `0005`.

## Upgrade on Windows

Stop the API and Angular terminals with Ctrl+C. Copy the updated `petrix-ai` source contents into `C:\Users\Admin\petrix-ai`. Keep your current `backend/.env`, `.venv`, PostgreSQL database, and Mailpit installation.

In PowerShell, activate the environment belonging to Petrix before migrating:

```powershell
cd C:\Users\Admin\petrix-ai
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
python --version
cd .\backend
python -m alembic upgrade head
python -m alembic current
```

Use Python 3.9.12. The migration check must show `0014 (head)` before starting the API. Migration `0003` adds a workflow document for each existing agent and workflow state/metadata to tester chats. Migration `0004` numbers existing triggers and actions and adds a counter per agent. Migration `0005` adds file storage. Migration `0006` adds encrypted database connectors. Migration `0007` adds uploaded workflow assets and 20 MiB outgoing conversation-file storage. Migration `0008` adds agent Knowledge text sources. Migration `0009` adds conversation custom fields and independent saved assignments. Migration `0010` adds workspace support teams and alternative names. Migration `0011` adds support profiles, team members, assignment policy, session workspace selection, and durable live-chat ownership. Migration `0012` adds external integrations and durable provider conversation transfers. Migration `0013` adds authenticated AI-agent connections and durable network sessions. Migration `0014` adds tickets, tags, email domains/templates, activity and initial delivery records. These migrations retain existing action configuration. Deleted greetings stay deleted, and accounts and agent settings remain intact.

```powershell
python -m uvicorn app.main:create_app --factory --reload --port 8000 --no-access-log
```

In a second PowerShell terminal:

```powershell
cd C:\Users\Admin\petrix-ai\frontend
npm ci
npm start
```

For version `0.4.0`, first install the updated dependency lock file and complete the provider setup in [INTENT_MATCHING.md](INTENT_MATCHING.md). Open `http://localhost:4200` and reuse your current session or sign in through Mailpit.

## Configure the greeting first

1. Select your agent and open **Workflows**.
2. Open **Chat started** and select its **Send message** row.
3. Edit the saved message, then select **Save**.
4. Restart the tester using its refresh button.

The starter action stores `Hi! I’m {_chatbot.name}. How can I assist you today?`. The backend replaces the name placeholder using the agent's saved name. No greeting is hardcoded in the Angular tester. Renaming the agent updates the rendered placeholder; disabling or deleting the action stops that message. New agents and agents imported using the existing settings format receive the same starter workflows.

## Triggers and tree rules

### Permanent step numbers

Every saved trigger and action has a number such as **#1** or **#7**, including disabled steps and nested branches. The same number appears in the workflow list, tree, settings panel, and tester execution details. It belongs to that step and stays the same when you rename, move, edit, enable, or disable it. A number identifies a step; displayed tree order determines execution order.

Each agent has its own sequence shared by triggers and actions. New agents start with Chat started **#1**, Chat closed **#2**, Chat timeout **#3**, AI timeout **#4**, Fallback **#5**, and the starter Send message **#6**. The next saved step receives **#7**. Numbers are allocated when Save or Create succeeds; unsaved action drafts have no number. Deleted numbers are never reassigned.

For an existing agent, migration `0004` preserves the numbers previously displayed beside its top-level workflows, then numbers all existing descendants in tree order. It keeps names, UUIDs, configurations, workflow revisions, and saved chat variables. After this one-time upgrade, each number remains stable. Gaps after deletion are expected.

### Trigger behaviour

| Trigger | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| Chat started | Permanent, always enabled, top-level only. Runs when the tester starts or restarts. |
| Chat closed | Permanent, always enabled, top-level only. Runs post-conversation data/feedback actions after a Ready Close chat action or the simulated live-agent close event. Conversational steps and incoming waits are forbidden, including through Jump. |
| Chat timeout | Permanent, always enabled, top-level only. Available as a simulated tester event; automatic channel timers come later. |
| AI timeout | Permanent, always enabled, top-level only. Available as a simulated tester event. |
| Message received | Configurable intent examples per language; exact-only or layered fuzzy/semantic/Groq matching. Starts disabled until examples are configured. |
| Attachment received | Matches selected image, audio, video, or file categories. The current tester sends metadata rather than uploading files. |
| Fallback | One per sibling level. Runs if no enabled alternative at that level matches. The starter top-level fallback is disabled and empty. |
| Collect feedback | Runs once when a closed conversation submits the rating and/or survey requested by a Collect Feedback action under Chat Closed. Variables are saved and the post-close continuation runs before this optional receiving trigger. |

Choose **New workflow** to add a top-level trigger. Enter its name and optional description, then configure it in the settings panel. Add intent examples one per line. **Layered intent matching** tries fuzzy text, then semantic cosine similarity, then structured Groq recognition. Similarity thresholds and ambiguity margins decide whether a stage accepts a candidate or continues. A default-language example set is used when the tester language has none. **Exact phrase matching** uses only normalized literal equality. See [INTENT_MATCHING.md](INTENT_MATCHING.md) for setup, context, entities, and clarification behaviour.

Actions at the same level run in displayed order. Use the Add action insertion points to place a step before the first action, between actions, or at the end. Use the up/down controls to reorder siblings of the same kind. Nested actions run before their parent's following siblings. Disabled nodes skip their entire subtree while preserving all saved settings.

Nested triggers form alternative branches after the actions at that level. Execution pauses there until a later event matches a branch or its local fallback. When that branch finishes, execution resumes the parent's remaining actions. A local fallback takes priority over top-level navigation. If there is no local match or fallback, a matching top-level workflow may interrupt the waiting branch. Workflows allow 12 nested levels, 500 nodes per agent, and a definition size of 1 MiB.

Deleting a node removes its nested steps as well; the UI asks for confirmation. Permanent system triggers cannot be deleted, disabled, duplicated, or moved below another node. Their action children can be changed, disabled, or deleted.

## Send message

- Wrap text or a variable placeholder in `**` to display it in bold in the tester, for example `Welcome to **{company}**`. Newlines and emojis are preserved; assistant text is rendered without interpreting raw HTML.
- Store 1–10 non-empty message variants, each up to 4,000 characters. One variant is chosen at random each time the action runs.
- Store up to 13 distinct, non-empty quick replies of up to 100 characters each. Clicking a current quick reply sends its text through Message received matching.
- Configure each assigned content language manually. The runtime uses that translation, then the agent's default, then the first saved translation if the default has no content yet. Stored translations remain available when agent languages change.
- Message placeholders include `{_chatbot.name}`, `{{agent.name}}`, `{{input.message}}`, and `{{feedback.rating}}`, plus session variables such as `{complaint_ref}` and structured paths such as `{{customer.name}}`. Quick replies also support variables. Substitution runs once as plain text; missing variables produce a controlled tester error.
- Each settings panel has its own Save. Unsaved step settings prompt before navigation; rejected saves preserve the current draft.

## Testing

The tester starts a real saved test conversation and executes Chat started. Exact/fuzzy matching, configured semantic matching, non-LLM actions, and quick replies work when the agent's LLM flag is off. The flag controls Groq intent recognition, optional generative replies, and explicit LLM Processing actions. Execution details show which trigger and actions ran; the Intent matching panel shows stage results and recognized entities. A matched workflow with no enabled message actions produces no artificial assistant reply. Clarification is a separate, explicitly labelled response that does not execute workflow actions.

Use **Test an event** for attachment, closure, feedback, and timeout events. Attachment testing simulates the filename/category only. Add a Collect Feedback action under Chat Closed before closing to issue a rating/survey form. Submit through that form; the token-bearing manual CSAT event remains available for rating-only forms. Channel preview selects Webchat faces, Messaging buttons, or typed Bitrix24/Africa’s Talking ratings, and restarts a new conversation without connecting any channel. Closed conversations reject further ordinary messages. Closure and accepted feedback persist even if subsequent automation fails; the tester reports the error. See [CHAT_CLOSED.md](CHAT_CLOSED.md).

An enabled matching workflow, including a configured fallback, takes priority over generative replies. When no trigger matches, the tester may use the optional model connection if configured and enabled. Otherwise it displays a diagnostic outside the conversation rather than inventing a reply. Generative calls retain the configured per-user rate limit; tester events are limited to 60 per user per minute. Failed provider turns roll back.

Saved changes apply on the next event. A changed workflow revision clears an old nested execution context to avoid continuing deleted or reordered steps. Restart explicitly to replay Chat started after changing the greeting.

## Storage and API

Workflows require Manage AI Agents for editing and testing; read access requires workspace membership. Authentication, CSRF, completed onboarding, and workspace/agent ownership are checked on the backend. A locked workflow row and `expected_revision` reject conflicting saves with 409. Successful changes appear in the agent's Change log.

The prefix is `/api/workspaces/{workspace_id}/agents/{agent_id}`:

| Method | Path | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/workflows` | Definition, revision, trigger definitions, and action catalogue. |
| POST | `/workflows` | JSON `expected_revision` and the complete `nodes` tree. Validates and atomically replaces the document. |
| POST | `/tester/events` | JSON `event`, `conversation_id` after start, optional `language`, and event-specific fields. Returns messages, quick replies, trace, status, and workflow revision. |

Node fields: `id` (UUID), `number` (positive integer), `kind` (`trigger` or `action`), `type`, `name`, `description`, `enabled`, `config`, and `children`. Branch and Send API additionally store `paths: [{id, children}]`, matched to condition/Else IDs or Success/Error/Timeout IDs in the config; their ordinary `children` is empty. See [BRANCH.md](BRANCH.md) and [SEND_API.md](SEND_API.md). IDs and numbers remain stable through editing and reordering. The server owns numbers: saves may omit them for compatibility, and supplied numbers cannot change existing assignments or choose a new step's number. A locked per-agent counter prevents reuse after deletion. System-node IDs are checked by the backend. Future action types cannot be activated by bypassing the catalogue UI.

Tester trace entries include `node_id` and `node_number` for each matched trigger and executed action. A generative reply has both fields set to null because it is not a saved workflow step.

Workflow revisions are separate from agent-settings versions. Agent snapshot restoration and the existing `petrix-agent` import/export schema cover agent settings only. Workflow duplication, deployment snapshots, full-agent workflow import/export, and published channels are later increments. The builder labels saved revisions without claiming a channel deployment.

## Action code layout

| Location | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `backend/app/workflows/actions/registry.py` | Explicit action allow-list, catalogue metadata, config/handler registration. |
| `backend/app/workflows/actions/send_message/config.py` | Send message validation and language schemas. |
| `backend/app/workflows/actions/send_message/handler.py` | Random variant selection, placeholders, and quick replies. |
| `backend/app/workflows/actions/set_variable` | Variable configuration and data-only execution handler. |
| `backend/app/workflows/actions/ask_survey` | Survey field validation, questions, and typed answers. |
| `backend/app/workflows/actions/send_api` | Request validation, bounded HTTPS client, and outcome selection. |
| `backend/app/workflows/actions/branch` | Ordered condition configuration and path selection. |
| `backend/app/workflows/actions/jump` | UUID target configuration and a control-transfer result consumed by the runtime. |
| `backend/app/workflows/actions/<other_action>/__init__.py` | An individual reserved module and unavailable descriptor for each later action. |
| `frontend/src/app/features/workflows/actions/send-message` | Send message configuration UI. New action editors should get their own sibling folder. |
| `frontend/src/app/features/workflows/actions/jump` | Searchable numbered target picker and target validation. |
| `frontend/src/app/features/workflows/actions/branch` | Condition editor, order controls, and expression guidance. |
| `frontend/src/app/features/workflows/workflow-tree.ts` | Shared traversal through ordinary children and action outcome paths. |
| `backend/app/workflows/service.py` | Tree validation and revision-checked persistence. |
| `backend/app/workflows/numbering.py` | Stable per-agent step numbers assigned during a locked save. |
| `backend/app/workflows/matching` | Fuzzy scoring, embedding adapters/cache, Groq recognition, and layered trigger selection. |
| `backend/app/workflows/runtime.py` | Trigger matching, sequential actions, nested waits, and continuations. |

All 20 action types are Ready, including Create Ticket. AI Agent Handoff is Ready for verified receiving Petrix agents; External Handoff is Ready for existing linked Zendesk/Bitrix24 conversations. Send API makes actual configured HTTPS requests, SQL Query executes read-only PostgreSQL lookups, and Switch Language changes the current chat language. Ticket email and published customer-channel adapters remain subsequent integrations.

## SQL Query and Settings (0.8.0)

SQL Query executes a single parameterized SELECT against a verified PostgreSQL connector in the current workspace, in a server-enforced read-only transaction. It stores `{ok,rows,columns,row_count,truncated,error}` and selects Success, Error, or Timeout. Empty rows still mean Success. All workflow traversals and Jump targets include SQL outcome paths. See [SQL_QUERY.md](SQL_QUERY.md) for the complete survey → SQL → Branch → message → menu flow and [DATABASE_CONNECTIONS.md](DATABASE_CONNECTIONS.md) for Settings setup, permissions, encrypted credentials, TLS, and migration `0006`. Other new Settings sections are explicitly marked Planned; existing role controls remain functional.

## Switch Language (0.9.0)

Choose an agent-configured language in **Flow control → Switch Language**. It changes the active conversation language without creating an assistant message or changing the agent default. The language persists through translated messages, triggers on subsequent turns, surveys, Branch, Jump, API/SQL parameters, and generative fallback prompts. Existing state/CSRF/permissions/revision checks apply. Switch Language itself introduced no migration or dependency. The current Send Attachment release requires schema head `0007`. See [SWITCH_LANGUAGE.md](SWITCH_LANGUAGE.md) for setup, missing-translation behavior, removal/restore guards, API config, and an English/French menu test.


## Send Attachment (0.10.0)

Choose **Messaging → Send attachment**, select the content language and file format, and provide an upload (up to 20 MiB), HTTP(S) file link, or safe Python expression returning a URL. The tester displays images, audio/video controls, and downloadable document cards. The action emits a single assistant file message, then continues normally; it works with nested triggers, Branch, Jump, and API/SQL outcome paths. Uploaded files are agent-owned and validated on save; sent copies belong to the conversation and survive later asset replacement. Localisation uses the active language and the existing default/first fallback, without translating file contents. Apply migration **0007** before running the updated backend. See [SEND_ATTACHMENT.md](SEND_ATTACHMENT.md) for supported extensions, script examples, limits, access, and a complete complaint form flow.


## Show Carousel (0.11.0)

Choose **Messaging → Show carousel** and configure 1–10 cards in each content language, with optional uploaded or hosted images, titles/subtitles, and up to three buttons per card. Reply buttons send their configured message through normal nested/root Message received matching. Link buttons open a new tab or a sandboxed webview inside the tester. Cards support drag and up/down reordering, horizontal navigation, and the existing active/default/first language fallback. Uploaded-image references participate in the same ownership, deletion protection, and immutable sent-copy behavior as Send Attachment. No migration or dependency is added; head remains `0007`. Read [SHOW_CAROUSEL.md](SHOW_CAROUSEL.md) for a complete complaint-category flow and webview limitations.

## Chat Closed and Collect Feedback (0.13.0)

Open the permanent **Chat closed** workflow to configure post-conversation actions. Its catalogue contains all 13 allowed action types, now Ready. Send message, Send attachment, Show carousel, Ask survey, and incoming triggers are unavailable, including in Branch/API/SQL/LLM/Auto Fill/Auto Team Match paths or indirect Jump continuations. The backend enforces the same policy. Normal workflows cannot Jump into its steps.

Choose **Flow control → Collect feedback** and configure its **Rating**, **Survey**, and **Settings** tabs. Rating saves an integer in `feedback_rating` or your chosen variable; optional/required Open response, Number, Email, Phone, and Multiple choice fields save additional variables. Titles, request messages, questions, placeholders, choices, and submission confirmations are localisable. The separate feedback form pauses the action’s children and remaining steps until submission, then saves all answers before resuming. Put mandatory closure logs before it; put actions needing feedback after it. This replaces 0.12.0’s immediate continuation behavior.

This `kind:"action"` requests feedback; the optional separate `kind:"trigger"` with the same type runs after submission and continuation. Closure and accepted answers are committed before their automation, so an automation error cannot reopen the chat or lose the answers. Test using **Chat closed (live-agent event)** and the channel preview selector; actual Livechats/published-channel integration comes later. See [CHAT_CLOSED.md](CHAT_CLOSED.md) for the combined flow and [COLLECT_FEEDBACK.md](COLLECT_FEEDBACK.md) for all settings and survey-only testing. No new migration or dependency is required; head remains `0007`.

## Close Chat (0.14.0)

Choose **Add action → Flow control → Close chat**, marked Ready. It has no extra settings. Save it after a goodbye message or other actions that must happen before closing. For an open conversation it stops its children, later siblings, and enclosing continuations, then invokes the permanent Chat Closed workflow once. If Collect Feedback is configured there, the closed tester displays its form and resumes the post-close continuation after submission. When already closed, Close chat is a no-op that continues without firing the trigger again. Disabled actions are skipped normally.

Closure, earlier messages/media, and collected variables are committed before the close automation; a later failure leaves the chat closed and those earlier results intact. Trace entries show Closed or Already closed, and the response records `close_source:"workflow"`. No migration or dependency is added. See [CLOSE_CHAT.md](CLOSE_CHAT.md) for the complete end-to-feedback test.


## LLM Processing (0.15.0)

Choose **Add action → AI & data → LLM Processing**, marked Ready. The editor provides Input and System prompt with optional safe Python Script modes, the configured Groq model, temperature 0–2 (default 1), a Knowledge toggle, and a resulting variable. Advanced settings select a 1–120 second timeout (default 30). The generated final answer is stored directly as text; reference `{complaint_details}` in a subsequent Send message.

Save the action, then add actions under Success, Error, and Timeout. Paths participate in step numbering, editing, insertion, reordering, Branch, Jump target search, nested waits, and post-close restrictions. Model errors clear stale result text. The tester shows the model and short error code in its trace. The action itself emits no chat message, so it can process variables under Chat Closed and after Collect Feedback submission.

The Knowledge tab now saves per-agent enabled text sources; uploads, crawling, and retrieval ranking remain future features. Read [LLM_PROCESSING.md](LLM_PROCESSING.md) and [KNOWLEDGE.md](KNOWLEDGE.md). Apply migration **0008** before starting this release. At release 0.15.0, the Chat Closed catalogue had four future entries marked Later; LLM Processing became Ready.


## Unlimited AI agents (0.15.1)

Workspace agent counts are unlimited, including creation and import after three existing agents. This does not change workflow persistence, execution, or language settings. Reload after restarting the updated backend/frontend. No new migration is added; schema head remains `0008`.


## Auto Fill Field and Custom Fields (0.16.0)

Create conversation fields in Settings → Teamspace → Custom fields. Text, Number, Toggle switch, Dropdown, Date, and Single Select (Grouped) support typed defaults; only the grouped type appears in Auto Fill Field. The action selects up to 20 fields and a result variable, then routes through Success or Error. A valid no-match response follows Success and leaves existing values unchanged. Assignments are validated against workspace-owned predefined options, stored independently on the chat, and exposed as `system.custom_fields.<key>.value`. The result variable contains `ok`, matched `fields`, `unmatched` keys, and `error`.

Both paths participate in numbering, nested actions/surveys, Branch, Jump, and post-close restrictions. Field definitions are revision checked, and referenced fields cannot be deleted or changed to an unsupported type. The tester shows saved fields separately from ordinary chat variables. Ticket conversion remains planned; a shared snapshot copy helper is supplied for that later feature. Apply migration **0009**. Read [AUTO_FILL_FIELD.md](AUTO_FILL_FIELD.md) and [CUSTOM_FIELDS.md](CUSTOM_FIELDS.md).


## Auto Team Match and Teams settings (0.17.0)

Configure team names, descriptions, and alternative names in **Settings → Workspace → Teams**. Choose **Add action → AI & data → Auto team match**, marked Ready. Enter text, a `{financial_institution}` template, or a safe Python expression returning text such as `financial_institution.text`, and specify `matched_team` as the output variable. Save and add actions under **Match found**, **No match**, and **Error**.

The result is a team object with `id` and `name`, or null when no team is identified or an error occurs. Matching ignores case and punctuation, uses complete names/phrases, and routes ambiguous input through No match. Teams are workspace scoped; deleted teams are excluded from future events. All three paths support numbering, nested actions, Jump, and post-close restrictions. The tester displays the result variable and outcome. Live Agent Handoff is available in the current release. Apply migration **0010** from backend, restart, and see [AUTO_TEAM_MATCH.md](AUTO_TEAM_MATCH.md) and [TEAMS.md](TEAMS.md). No dependency change or model request is needed.


## Send Graph (0.18.0)

Choose **Add action → AI & data → Send graph**, marked Ready. Select Bar, Grouped Bar, Stacked Bar, Line, Multi-line, Pie, or Combo. Enter literal JSON, a variable template, or a safe Python expression for the data; configure labels, one of 12 palettes, grid lines, and the appropriate legend. Combo has two expanded data sections with independent scales and series names. A resolved empty Combo input skips the chart and continues. Literal data is checked on Save; dynamic data is checked at execution.

The action emits one immutable chart message and resumes its ordinary children/following steps; it has no outcome paths. Charts support exact hover/focus values, table view, numeric CSV exports, and PNG exports on white. Graphs are available under Chat Closed and after feedback submission. The reusable renderer is integrated into the authenticated Agent tester; live Inbox/published channels remain future work. No new migration or dependency is needed; head stays **0010**. See [SEND_GRAPH.md](SEND_GRAPH.md) for limits, data formats, API/SQL inputs, and complete test flows.


## Live Agent Handoff and Inbox (0.19.0)

Choose **Add action → Handoffs → Live agent handoff**, marked Ready. Configure the availability check, all or specific support agents/teams, optional Auto Team Match result variable, and optional active-language filter. Save and add steps under **When live agent closes chat** and **When no live agent is available**. The successful handoff pauses later AI steps and stores the original continuation; customer messages bypass AI handling until the live interaction ends.

Add existing accounts in **Settings → Workspace → Users**, select team members in **Teams**, and let each support member choose their languages and availability in **Inbox**. **Settings → Teamspace → Chat assignment** chooses Manual claim, Round robin, or Least busy and an active-chat limit. Queues, reply/close, and files are scoped to eligible or assigned members; Members can handle chats without Manage AI Agents permission. Presence requires a valid session and expires without heartbeats.

Closing from Inbox durably fires Chat Closed once. Collect Feedback pauses the handoff return until the customer submits. Then the original close path and following AI steps run on the same conversation, even if workflows were edited during the handoff. A follow-up survey keeps the frozen continuation until it completes. Human closure and accepted answers survive automation failures, and failed returns are not replayed. Apply migration **0011** from backend, restart, and follow [LIVE_AGENT_HANDOFF.md](LIVE_AGENT_HANDOFF.md) and [INBOX.md](INBOX.md). Inbox and tester integration are working; published channel transport remains a separate milestone.


## External Handoff

Choose **Add action → Handoffs → External handoff**, marked Ready. Select an enabled, verified Zendesk or Bitrix24 platform configured under **Settings → Workspace → External integrations**. An existing provider conversation must be linked before the runtime can transfer it. The tester has a dedicated link control that validates provider access.

Confirmed transfer is terminal: no later workflow action, Chat Closed automation, Collect Feedback, or AI return runs. New events for that conversation are rejected; its earlier transcript is read-only under **Inbox → External**. Explicit provider rejections leave AI handling open. Unconfirmed outcomes pause processing and require an observed outcome to be reviewed before any retry. See [EXTERNAL_HANDOFF.md](EXTERNAL_HANDOFF.md) for native API contracts, setup, permissions, and current customer-channel scope. Apply migration **0012** before starting the API.


## AI Agent Handoff

Choose **Add action → Handoffs → AI agent handoff**, marked Ready. Enable incoming credentials on receiving Agent B's **Network** tab. On Agent A, choose **Connect external AI agent**, enter B's ID, secret, and platform origin, then **Verify & Save**. Select the connection and Save the action. Both platforms must support Petrix protocol v1 (0.21.0+); remote instances require HTTPS. The Network workspace map alone does not authorize transfers.

The source interpreter stops at the handoff. B starts once with filtered public source variables in read-only `_transferred_context` and recent sanitized history. B's subsequent messages, surveys, attachments, live support, and feedback continue through A's original tester conversation ID. Reload and explicit retry retain stable transfer/request IDs. B's closure does not resume A; the receiving agent owns its own Chat Closed and feedback lifecycle. Loops are rejected and uncertain transfers remain paused. See [AI_AGENT_HANDOFF.md](AI_AGENT_HANDOFF.md) for the full setup and complaint flow, limits, credentials, file retention, and recovery. Apply migration **0013** from backend before restarting; no dependency change.


## Create Ticket

Choose **Add action → Handoffs → Create ticket**, marked Ready. Configure tags/groups, a support member or team, subject/description, customer identity, optional verified sender and customer/assignee templates, and optional custom-field overrides. Configure **Settings → Teamspace → Tags / Email domains / Email templates** first when needed. Existing conversation fields copy automatically; explicit action values override the copy without changing the chat.

The action persists a support case and continues. Add Send message with `{last_ticket.reference}` afterwards to confirm the reference. It also works under Chat Closed, where conversational actions remain unavailable. Initial emails are attempted only after commit; SMTP failures retain the ticket and expose delivery status/retry in **Tickets**. All 20 workflow actions are implemented. Apply migration **0014** from backend. Read [CREATE_TICKET.md](CREATE_TICKET.md) for two complete test flows, sender ownership/SMTP requirements, limits and API, and [TICKETS.md](TICKETS.md) for assignment, status, notes and email review.

WORKSPACE_SETTINGS.title: Workspace settings (0.23.0)
WORKSPACE_SETTINGS.content:
# Workspace settings (0.23.0)

Open **Settings → Workspace**. General, Roles & permissions, Users, IP allowlist, Whitelabelling, and Plan & billing are implemented. The existing Teams page remains the place to manage teams; Voice API remains Planned. AI-agent creation and import stay unlimited, including on configured Stripe plans.

## Upgrade an existing installation

Back up PostgreSQL, keep your existing `backend/.env`, replace the source, then run from the activated backend environment:

```powershell
python -m alembic upgrade head
python -m alembic current
```

The current head is **0015**. The revision argument `head` is required. Restart backend and frontend, then reload the browser. No runtime dependencies changed. Migration 0015 preserves existing users, teams and members, roles, sessions, workflows, conversations, handoffs, tickets, email settings, files, and unlimited agents. It creates a Default teamspace, associates existing agents with it, and creates the protected Admin role in each workspace. Idle logout and the IP allowlist start disabled; branding starts disabled. Existing legacy role assignments keep their previous behavior until explicitly changed.

## General and branding

General saves the workspace name and an optional avatar. PNG, JPEG, and GIF files up to 10 MiB are accepted; files are decoded and re-encoded as PNG, and GIFs use their first frame. Avatars become 256-pixel squares. A saved name/avatar updates the sidebar and refreshed account context. Remove and Save removes an image. Concurrent changes produce a reload message instead of overwriting a newer save.

Whitelabelling saves a main logo, a square logo, and optional primary/background/sidebar/text colours. Main logos retain their aspect ratio (up to 1024 × 512); square logos become 256 × 256. Logos and colours apply to the actual interface. The expanded sidebar uses the main logo; its collapse control uses the square logo, falling back to the available logo. For a branded sign-up page use `/signup?workspace=WORKSPACE_UUID`. Only explicitly enabled branding (name, logos, colours) is public; credentials, memberships, settings, and conversations are not exposed by the branding endpoint. Removing logos does not delete other workspace data.

When Stripe billing is configured, IP restrictions require Total or Enterprise, and Whitelabelling requires Enterprise. Without Stripe keys this self-hosted installation allows administrators to configure these features; it does not invent a paid subscription or payment history.

## Roles and teamspaces

Each permission has an independent checkbox in an expandable group. Workspace roles include Workspace, Teamspace, AI Agents, Livechats, Tickets, People, Analytics, AI Analysis, Perception, and Data Management. Team roles omit Workspace administration and Data Management, including billing/user/role/team management. A manage grant does not silently grant a corresponding view grant. Enable both when a user needs to open and edit a page.

Create a role, enter a unique case-insensitive name, choose Workspace or Team, and select its grants. A saved role's type is fixed to protect existing assignments; create another role when a different type is needed. Click a row to edit its description/name/grants. Admin has full access and is protected against edits and deletion. The header checkbox skips protected roles; deleting any selected protected role is also rejected by the API. The original workspace owner remains protected independently of custom roles.

Assign Workspace roles in **Users → Edit**. Assign Team roles and the teamspaces where they apply in the existing **Teams** editor. Team grants supplement the user's Workspace grants; they cannot revoke access already granted by a Workspace role. To create a restricted team-only operator, assign an empty custom Workspace role and an appropriate Team role, rather than retaining the legacy Member role (which already permits reading agents). A team's unconfigured teamspace selection means Default only.

Team-role “all” ticket/livechat grants apply to that team's assigned records, not every workspace record. “Own” grants apply to records assigned directly to the user within the team's teamspaces. Workspace grants support all/team/own scopes separately. Deleting a Team role clears its role link and grants while preserving the team, member accounts, membership lists, teamspace assignments, aliases, and saved records.

**Teamspaces** can be created and agents can be assigned to them. Users can have all current/future teamspaces or an explicit selection. Agent reads/writes and custom-role ticket/livechat queries honor those boundaries. Existing conversation custom fields, tags, email settings, and other shared Teamspace settings belong to **Default**; their Team-role grants apply there. Database connections and external integrations remain workspace administration. Future People, Analytics, AI Analysis, Perception, ban rules, exports, and other Planned modules have their catalogued permission flags ready; assigning their flags does not activate an unimplemented module.

The old `/roles` API is retained for legacy Manage AI Agents flags. It requires Manage user roles & permissions and cannot bypass custom-role enforcement.

## Users, invitations, and idle logout

The Users table shows members, email, teams, teamspaces, role, and current live-agent availability. Edit changes role, team membership, and teamspace access. A user's own access and the owner's access are protected. Manage Users alone cannot assign a higher role or a team with grants the actor does not hold; modifying existing administrators additionally requires role-management permission. Removing a member retains their account and access to other workspaces. Active livechats must be transferred/closed before removing their assignee. Existing ticket history remains available.

Invite users by email, selecting the same role/team/teamspace fields. The existing SMTP configuration sends an invitation valid for seven days. The recipient opens its link, signs in with the invited email, and explicitly accepts it. Tokens are stored hashed and consumed once. Pending, accepted, revoked, and expired invitations appear in **Invites**. Resend creates a new token and revokes the old link; Revoke disables a pending invitation. Sending is limited to ten invitations per workspace per minute. A failed SMTP send leaves the invitation revoked and displays a configuration error. No invitation email is sent by installing this update.

Idle logout defaults to Disabled. Choose a timeout from five minutes to 24 hours. Saving a policy resets the idle clock for existing members' sessions to allow a full grace period. Trusted pointer, key, and scroll input sends a throttled CSRF-protected activity request. Inbox heartbeat, polling, and ordinary reads do not extend the clock. The API revokes expired sessions; frontend-only timers cannot bypass it. The setting applies when accessing that workspace; normal absolute session expiry also continues to apply.

## IP allowlist

Use **Enable IP allowlist**, **Exempt admins**, and Start/End ranges. Both IPv4 and IPv6 are supported; one range must use the same address family and start before or at its end. Enter a single address in both fields to allow just that address. Up to 100 ranges can be configured. Enabling without a range is rejected. Saving must keep the current actor's IP allowed or exempt an administrator; it cannot silently lock out the person saving it.

The API checks the policy on authenticated workspace requests, including direct agent/workflow calls and account context. Owner and protected Admin roles can be exempted. The workspace selector and logout remain available to leave a restricted workspace. Public enabled branding and the separately authenticated AI-network protocol are not browser-session access. Network peers use their own credentials and do not acquire workspace administration permissions.

The policy uses the server's resolved socket peer. Supplied local Uvicorn startup commands use `--no-proxy-headers`. For a production reverse proxy, configure Uvicorn `--proxy-headers --forwarded-allow-ips=EXACT_TRUSTED_PROXY_IPS`, restrict direct access to Uvicorn, and have that proxy replace client-supplied forwarded headers. Never trust arbitrary forwarded addresses or use `*` for this allowlist.

## Billing and actual interaction usage

View billing and Manage billing are separate. View billing opens Plan, Breakdown, and Detailed usage; Manage billing authorizes checkout, portal, and saved auto top-up controls. Account status and invoice amounts are fetched from Stripe, not copied from reference screenshots. Without provider configuration, the page shows actual recorded usage and “Billing setup required”; unavailable invoice/payment data stays unavailable. Resource counters include members plus pending invitations, active teams, teamspaces, and agents. An absent configured limit is shown as ∞; the agent limit is always ∞.

Monthly counters follow the subscription's monthly anniversary even for multi-month billing. With no subscription they use the calendar month. Fixed allowances show used/remaining and warnings at 75% and 90%; viewers are directed to an administrator. Bundles can be bought in quantities 1–50 for eligible configured Lite/Pro/Total plans. Purchased interaction balances carry forward when the monthly plan allowance resets. A small monthly usage ledger settles consumed bundle interactions without expiring unused purchases. Bundle prices and credits come from server configuration, and actual checkout quantities/prices are checked against the saved operation before crediting them.

Breakdown and Detailed usage use durable chat messages, sent initial ticket emails, and recorded Auto Fill Field, Auto Team Match, LLM Processing, and SQL Query executions. Action metering starts with this release; older action histories are not fabricated. Copied AI-handoff history, mirrored remote assistant messages, and repeated source-request IDs are excluded from message counts. Failed/queued/uncertain emails are not counted as sent. A successful SMTP receipt becomes an AI email interaction. Unimplemented voice/manual-email/Inbox-analysis categories show zero. Default weight is one per event; server weights may change weighted counts. No customer message content is returned in usage reports.

Reports use **Africa/Nairobi**, inclusive From and exclusive To, and support hour/day/week/month/quarter/year grouping; type/source/teamspace/AI-agent/live-agent/team segmentation and filters; Total, Average/day, Peak day/hour; CSV and PNG downloads. A multi-team queue with no unique routed team is grouped as Unassigned. Select a larger group or shorter range if a chart exceeds 2,000 points. Image export is bounded to 16,000 pixels high; CSV retains the displayed rows. Reset all restores the default range, grouping, segmentation, and filters.

### Stripe configuration

Use test keys/prices first. Add optional values to the existing `backend/.env` (single-line JSON):

```dotenv
STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=sk_test_REPLACE
STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET=whsec_REPLACE
STRIPE_PRODUCTS_JSON={"pro":{"name":"Pro","price":"price_REPLACE_PLAN","mode":"subscription","included":10000,"limits":{"teamspaces":5,"teams":10,"users":25}},"pro_bundle":{"name":"Pro interaction bundle","price":"price_REPLACE_BUNDLE","mode":"payment","credits":1000,"plans":["pro"]}}
USAGE_WEIGHTS_JSON={"ai_messages":1,"people_messages":1,"ai_emails":1,"auto_fill_field":1,"auto_team_match":1,"llm_processing":1,"sql_query":1}
```

Create the corresponding recurring and fixed-price products in the same Stripe account. Server-configured `name` should be Lite, Pro, Total, or Enterprise where those plan entitlements apply. Subscription `included` is its monthly interaction allowance (omit/null for unmetered); `limits` are displayed resource limits. Bundles require positive integer `credits`; `plans` lists eligible plan names in lowercase. Prices, secret keys, and arbitrary charge amounts cannot be submitted by browser users. Restart the API after editing configuration. No Stripe SDK or changed dependency pin is required; the REST client pins API version `2025-06-30.basil`, including item-level subscription period fields.

Enable Stripe Customer Portal and configure allowed plan changes/payment methods/invoices. The new-subscription Upgrade flow uses Checkout; existing subscriptions use the portal for upgrades/downgrades, avoiding a second subscription. The app redirects only to recognized HTTPS Stripe checkout/billing hosts. An existing saved customer is reused per workspace. Checkout retry IDs and provider idempotency keys avoid duplicate purchases from a retried click. A success return URL does not activate a plan or grant credits.

Point Stripe's webhook endpoint at `POST /api/billing/stripe-webhook` and subscribe to `checkout.session.completed`, `checkout.session.async_payment_succeeded`, `customer.subscription.created/updated/deleted`, `invoice.paid`, `invoice.payment_failed`, `payment_intent.succeeded`, and `payment_intent.payment_failed`. Verification checks the raw-body HMAC signature with a five-minute tolerance and a unique event ledger. Payment/session objects are retrieved from Stripe before applying results, so duplicate and out-of-order notifications cannot overwrite a newer provider state. Keep keys server-side; they are never returned by the API.

Auto top-up requires a saved **default** payment method and a configured allowance/bundle. Configure its threshold and enable it explicitly, then run the worker periodically using your scheduler (for example, once per minute):

```powershell
cd backend
python -m app.workspace_settings.worker
```

Each eligible pass buys one bundle when the remaining balance is at or below the threshold. A durable pending operation and Stripe idempotency key are committed before the network charge; overlapping workers use a billing-row lock. Failed or unconfirmed charges pause further automatic purchases. Retry checks the same PaymentIntent/operation instead of silently issuing another purchase. After updating the default payment method in Manage billing, use **Retry top-up**. Authentication-required payments stay visible for attention; the operator can resolve them through Stripe or make a confirmed Checkout purchase. This update does not run a scheduler or make charges merely by opening Settings.

Official integration references: [Checkout](https://docs.stripe.com/api/checkout/sessions/create?api-version=2025-06-30.basil), [Customer Portal](https://docs.stripe.com/api/customer_portal/sessions/create), [PaymentIntents](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_intents/create), [webhook delivery/signatures](https://docs.stripe.com/events/manage-webhook-endpoints), and [subscription period changes](https://docs.stripe.com/changelog/basil/2025-03-31/deprecate-subscription-current-period-start-and-end).
